## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 450

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **CHAPTER 441, SUNDAY THE THIRD. SIX THINGS NAMED OUT LOUD, AND A WOMAN TOLD BEFORE AND NOT AFTER.** A joint of oakum and tar has to be wet twice and dry once between before a boat will come off a bank, and a boat of about nineteen tons is not coming off that tide. Six things were said on the bench stone at about eleven in the morning as what an account of anything in that harbor has to carry, and the sixth is a seam this yard has no copy of. **A woman of no office was told at about four in the afternoon that her name is going on a public sheet, and said she had not asked to be on it and was not going to ask to be taken off it, and that a person who asks to be taken off a piece of paper is a person who has been on it.** The Fish Street room was let out for the sixth time and there was no claim in it.
2. **CHAPTER 442, MONDAY THE FOURTH. THE SEVENTY-FOURTH WIPE, THE EIGHTY-SEVENTH CISTERN, AND A BOAT OFF A BANK.** A caulked joint that has been wet once is not a joint yet, and the *Alewife* came off at about half past two with eleven feet of that joint going under together and holding, and a caulker looked at it and was not paid for looking at it. **A man of about fifty stood in six inches of water holding the end of that yard's own baulk for about an hour and ten minutes because he had said he would, and nobody thanked him and he did not ask.**
3. **CHAPTER 443, TUESDAY THE FIFTH. THE CUSTODY ROOM, ENTERED ONCE.** Ten in the morning, under the second paper, a clerk in it the whole hour, one thing out of three, four people in the room. **A piece of worked lead about the size of a man's palm with a line of nine soundings in it, three of them deep, an office's mark, a hand and a person's own mark, a thumb-sized place left out on purpose, and no figure and no number of any kind.** The original went back under the same number, the third of the three was not looked at and was not named, its claim was not withdrawn, and nothing went out of that room in any hand.
4. **CHAPTER 444, WEDNESDAY THE SIXTH. THE ACCOUNT DRAWN UP, AND THE FOURTH BOX.** Nine boundaries printed on the face of a sheet of about four feet, two of its nine names a person who is not named, and its ninth is a charge on a wall that has not been paid. **Four names asked to be on a rotation that is not an office, and a sheet of four refusals put into a box a man had asked to be left empty, with the page saying who put it there and why.**
5. **CHAPTER 445, THURSDAY THE SEVENTH. THE PUBLIC READING, AND THE SEAL LINE READ ONCE.** About thirty people in a room on that hill and about eleven of them could not read, and the whole of that account was read out with a name and an hour against it. **The seal line was read out loud for the first time in that harbor since the twenty-second of August, which is the day it went up on that door, and the office at the end of it went into a working man's mouth once.** A claim against the copy was entered at a counter off the west basin and was not granted and not refused and is not withdrawn.
6. **CHAPTER 446, FRIDAY THE EIGHTH. THE LINE ON PAPER, AND THREE ACCOUNTS THAT DO NOT AGREE.** The lead did not come down that hill and the line went out on paper, and three men gave three accounts of one stone in about four and a half fathoms that do not agree and all three are kept. **A man of about forty-four put his words against a line of the account and the account was not changed. A diver went down once and came up with an aftertaste and with one afternoon in June he can put a name to and nothing else.**
7. **CHAPTER 447, SATURDAY THE NINTH. THE ONE PARTIAL CONFESSION, FOUR SENTENCES, NO FIFTH.** The far bench was not empty again until after four o'clock, and that bench had not been emptied before four o'clock on any of the days before it. **A man of sixty-one came down a slip into a shed where two people were and said four sentences out loud in his own mouth, and they name no log and no man who put anything in his hand and give no reason that makes them smaller. Nothing was written down, nobody thanked him, nobody forgave him, and the shoe that is not his was on the floor beside that bench at four o'clock.**
8. **CHAPTER 448, SUNDAY THE TENTH. THE CHARTER, THE TITLE SAID ONCE, AND TWO QUESTIONS.** A sheet bought blank at the head of it and left blank for forty minutes in a room over a fish market, four heads written on it and read out, four standing lines, a claim carried on it and not discharged, and four lines saying what it is not. **A man of about fifty said the name of that thing once at about ten past eleven in the morning on the day it was written and wrote it at the head of the sheet himself, and nobody said it after him.** A question about people who cannot speak safely and about people whose own account is held under a lie was asked after the four heads had been read out, by a woman of no office, naming no person, and was not answered and is in a minute as asked. A second question, about who gets into the big Crown wrecks, was asked by a man of about forty-four and no rule was written on that sheet about it and no office was made for it.
9. **CHAPTER 449, MONDAY THE ELEVENTH. THE SEVENTY-FIFTH WIPE, THE EIGHTY-NINTH CHARGE, AND THE FIVE COSTS.** The account was read out a second time with the four words under its fifth line, and a woman of about thirty-one stood up and said she had been asked to hold a sheet of paper flat on a table while a man copied off it, and was not going to say anything else about it there, and nobody asked her a question. **The five costs were set down one under another off a slate and not on a wall, and beside them a ropemaker who does not get her room back, a berth that has not been given back, and a claim window that has not been opened.** A man of about thirty-three read the six lines on the front-street wall aloud to two men who cannot read and then read them the figure off the slate, and said he could not say it was a lie and did not say it was not.
10. **CHAPTER 450, TUESDAY THE TWELFTH. THE READ-BACK, THE THREE VOICES, THE STANDING CONDITION, AND A LINE LEFT BLANK.** The leaf was read back at about ten past five with both definitions on the face of the reading and the fourth column standing at one hundred and twenty-five where it stood. **Three people said one thing each about the water and the harbor and this yard, in three voices, and none of it was written down. The whole of that harbor's standing condition is on the last page once and nowhere else. And in the room over a joiner's shop a man ruled a line under the last head on the open page and left it empty, and wrote the hour against it, and the reason at the foot of that page is that there is nobody in that harbor he can ask.**

THE CONSENT WAS ASKED ON SATURDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF SEPTEMBER OF ELEVEN MASTERS OF THAT HARBOR, ONE AT A TIME, IN THE SAME ELEVEN SENTENCES WRITTEN AT THE HEAD OF A PAGE BEFORE ANYBODY WAS ASKED AND READ OUT OF THE PAGE AND NOT OUT OF A MEMORY, WITH A NAME AND AN HOUR AGAINST EVERY LINE; TEN SAID YES AND ONE SAID NO, AND THE ONE IS A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE OF THE SECOND LAY WHOSE RIGHT FOREARM IS SET OUT OF HIS OWN HAND, WHO GAVE HIS REASON IN HIS OWN MOUTH AND WAS NOT ASKED AGAIN ON ANY OF THE SIX DAYS AFTER IT AND WAS AT HIS OWN BENCH IN THE FRONT ROOM OF A SHOP IN THE SECOND LAY FROM ABOUT EIGHT UNTIL ABOUT SIX ON EACH OF THOSE SIX DAYS. SEVEN BOATS AND ABOUT THIRTY MEN WENT OUT ON FOUR DAYS INSIDE THAT HARBOR'S OWN LINE WITH A SMALL STEAM TENDER OF ABOUT FORTY TONS AHEAD OF THEM. A YOUNG MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE WHO IS SECOND HAND ON THAT TENDER LAID FIFTEEN FATHOMS OF CHAIN WITH A SWIVEL IN IT OFF HIS QUARTER CLEAT TO THE BITT OF THAT BOAT, ROUND A SPURLE AND BACK WITH A WEIGHT ON THE TAIL OF IT, AND SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE WOULD NOT ASK ANYBODY'S LEAVE TO PULL IT AND THAT NOBODY IN THAT BOAT HAD ANY STANDING TO TELL HIM NOT TO, AND THAT THE ONLY REASON HE CAN DO THAT IS THAT HE IS NOT BEING PAID BY ANY OF THEM; THE WEIGHT CAME OVER THE RAIL FOUR TIMES WITH AN HOUR AND A REASON WRITTEN AGAINST EACH OF THEM. LOWFEN AND TIDEWATCH WERE ENTERED AND BOTH AS WORK AND NEITHER AS A TRIP: A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF THE SECOND LAY WHO KEEPS THE WHOLE FOULING LADDER IN HIS OWN BOOK SAID IN A SHED HOW A HEEL IS FITTED WHERE THE REEDS PUT THE GROUND OUT AND PULL IT BACK AND SAID HE HAD NEVER BEEN TO LOWFEN IN HIS LIFE; AND A MASTER OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX OUT OF LOWFEN SAID OUT LOUD THAT HE FINDS THAT CHANNEL BY THREE THINGS AND NONE OF THEM IS ON A PAPER. A BELLWRIGHT OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR NAMED MINA KETT CAME DOWN OFF THE WESTERN REEF LINE WITH HER OWN TOOLS IN A BOX AND TOOK ELEVEN BATTENS OFF A KEEL ON A HARD IN ABOUT TWO HOURS AND TEN MINUTES, AND WAS TOLD SHE WOULD BE PAID A DAY AT THE FIGURE IN CHALK ON A SLATE AT AN END STALL, BEING ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE, AND SAID OUT LOUD ONCE THAT THAT IS A CAULKER'S FIGURE AND NOT HERS, THAT A BELLWRIGHT OFF THAT LINE GETS FIVE SHILLINGS, BEING SIXTY PENCE, AND THAT SHE HAS BEEN GETTING FIVE SHILLINGS FOR NINE YEARS AND HAS NEVER ASKED ANYBODY FOR MORE, AND WAS NOT THANKED AND DID NOT ASK. SHE BROUGHT ABOUT FORTY SMALL PIECES OF LEAD IN THE LID OF HER BOX AND SAID THERE IS A NAIL IN THE DOOR FRAME OF HER WORKSHOP AT TIDEWATCH WITH ABOUT FORTY OF THEM ON IT AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-ONE THERE WHO COPIES A CUT ONTO A PAPER FOR A PENNY TO ANY PERSON WHO WALKS IN, AND THAT NOBODY HAS EVER BEEN REFUSED AT THAT DOOR IN TWENTY-SIX YEARS, AND THAT THESE ARE NOT FOR THIS COAST AND ARE NOT TO GO ON A WALL. THE KEELWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN THE LAST FOUR CHAPTERS, ON THE WATER, IN COMPANY, AT A WAGE OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES, UNDER A CONSENT ASKED FOR ONE MAN AT A TIME, WITH A NAMED TENDER AND A CUTOFF THAT CAN BE PULLED WITHOUT ASKING; IT SETTLES NOTHING, IT PRICES NOTHING, IT IS NOT A THING ANYBODY IS A MEMBER OF, AND IT IS NOT TAKEN BY BEING NAMED. THE WORD IS IN FOUR PLACES AND ALL FOUR ARE IN CHAPTER 439, AND A MASTER OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR SAID IT OUT LOUD AT ABOUT HALF PAST TWO IN THE AFTERNOON ON THE FIRST DAY OF OCTOBER AND A MASTER OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX OUT OF LOWFEN SAID FROM THE DOORWAY THAT THE ASKING IS NOT THE WORK, AND IT IS ON NO SHEET IN THAT HARBOR. ALL THREE OF ITS COSTS ARE ON THE FACE OF THE PAGES AND NONE OF THEM IS SUMMED: A BOAT OF ABOUT TWENTY-TWO TONS OPENED ABOUT NINE FOOT OF HER GARBOARD AND PUT A HOLE IN HER LEE RAIL ABOUT THE SIZE OF TWO HANDS BY STRIKING A BAULK OF OAK THAT THAT YARD'S OWN HANDS HAD LAID DOWN WITH NOTHING ON IT, AND THE BILL CAME TO THAT YARD AND IS NOT CHARGED TO THE OWNER OF ANY OF THE SEVEN BOATS, WHO WAS NOT ASKED TO PAY IT AND DID NOT OFFER; THE MATERIAL AND WAGES OF TEN DAYS CAME OUT OF A BAG THAT STOOD AT FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PENCE AT THE OPEN AND STANDS AT ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-SIX PENCE AT THE CLOSE; AND FOUR PEOPLE ASKED FOR A LINE TO BE STRUCK OUT OF A RECORD INSIDE THESE TEN DAYS AND WERE REFUSED IN THE SAME NINE WORDS EVERY TIME, BEING THAT THAT LINE STAYS, THAT NOTHING COMES OUT OF THAT BOOK ONCE IT IS IN, FOR ANY REASON, TO ANYBODY. SMALL SUPERVISED DIVES WITH A NAMED TENDER, A CUTOFF AND A RECORDED REASON BEGAN AT THE END OF THIS MOVEMENT AND THREE MEN WERE PUT IN THAT BELL ONE AT A TIME, AND THREE ACCOUNTS OF ABOUT TWO FOOT OF PLANK STAND AGAINST EACH OTHER AND NONE OF THEM HAS BEEN SETTLED. NO STAGE WAS TAKEN BEFORE CHAPTER 437 AND THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND WAS NOT USED OR IMPROVED. THE FOURTH COLUMN TOOK NO LINE AND THE REASON WAS ENTERED ONCE, IN THE SECOND COLUMN, ON THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF AUGUST, AND IS ENTERED AGAIN NOWHERE. THE PARTIAL CONFESSION IS NOT PAID IN THESE TEN DAYS AND IS OWED TO THE LAST MOVEMENT. THE FOURTH BOX IN AN OFFICE OFF THE WEST BASIN IS STILL EMPTY AND SOMETHING IS STILL TO GO INTO IT IN THIS VOLUME AGAINST THE WISH OF THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD IS TO ASK HIM ABOUT IT. NOTHING WAS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED ON ANY STANDING DEBT, AND THE HARBOR IS POORER ON THE SECOND DAY OF OCTOBER THAN ON THE TWENTY-THIRD DAY OF SEPTEMBER, WITH NO FLOUR IN THAT MARKET, NO OIL IN THAT HARBOR SINCE THE TWENTY-NINTH OF AUGUST, A LIGHT OUT AND A FIGURE ON A BOARD THAT DID NOT COME DOWN. `outline/volume-09.md` ENDS AT CHAPTER 450 AND WAS READ AND NOT EDITED, AND CHAPTERS 441 TO 450 ARE ITS FIFTH TEN AND ARE NOT WRITTEN. ## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 440

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **CHAPTER 431, THURSDAY THE TWENTY-THIRD. THE EIGHTY-FOURTH CISTERN CHARGE, AND A BOAT ON THE FOUL.** One hundred and sixty-eight pence of oakum, iron, three-inch stuff, canvas and nails went out at about ten in the morning and one hundred and sixty-eight pence of a day's work at a berth came in at about four in the afternoon and the bag stands at five hundred and thirty-two pence where it stood at the open of the day. **A warp round a bollard parted at about two in the morning and a boat of about nineteen tons named the *Alewife* went up the foul off the south end with nobody in her.** Nine men unstepped and landed her mast in about fifty minutes and split a piece out of the mole coping; her wheel went into a boat; both anchors were let go and left in nine foot. Calder Marr packed the open garboard from the inside at about eleven foot and said out loud that it would hold until the flood. **The flood came at about twenty past six, set her beam ends in about four minutes, put her port rail against the mole's footing stones for about an hour and ten minutes, and at about half past seven she came off and took the ground on a bank four hundred yards down the foul in about nine foot.** Nobody was paid for that morning. Nessa Pike told the holder of that writ in the open that she has two figures in that harbor and none at all for a man in the water at four in the morning, and would not make one up, and that the person is the thing that costs and a day for a person has to be written on a paper and asked one man at a time.
2. **CHAPTER 432, FRIDAY THE TWENTY-FOURTH. THE NIGHT'S WINDOW, AND LOWFEN AS WORK.** A hundred and five minutes of ebb, about a quarter to four to about twenty past five. He went down in a bell off her starboard quarter and shored her with two baulks of oak; the boat came down about two inches and stopped dead. He found about nine feet of soft plank nine feet aft of the shore and put his thumb through the veneer of it about the size of a shilling and said that a shore does not stop soft plank. The pump leather went at about half past four and about fifty minutes of fresh water came over the side. **One hundred and sixty-eight pence went out at about nine in the morning.** **Ollum Trevask, of about thirty-four, of the second lay, who keeps the whole fouling ladder in that harbor in his own book and has never shown it to anybody, said out loud that they do not do it that way in Lowfen, where a man takes the mould off a piece of the old keel with the boat still floating in about two foot of water with two men on a pole and a third with the battens, and that the ground under a Lowfen hull is not the ground there next year because the reeds put it out and pull it back, and that a mould there is kept in a head and not in a book, and that he has never been to Lowfen in his life and that is how he knows.** A packet went down that coast at about four in the afternoon offering one day at the figure in chalk and telling whoever came, in the packet, that the figure being offered was not the figure anybody ought to take.
3. **CHAPTER 433, SATURDAY THE TWENTY-FIFTH. ELEVEN MASTERS, ONE AT A TIME, IN THE SAME WORDS.** The words were written at the head of the page before anybody was asked. Ten said yes and one said no. **Rowan Teel, of about fifty-one, of the second lay, whose right forearm is set out of his own hand, said no at about a quarter to six and gave his reason in his own mouth and said he would rather say it then than have somebody come to his door about it on the Tuesday; he was not asked again on any of the six days after it.** **Sedge Rundle, of about forty-six, out of Lowfen, said out loud that he goes by three things and none of them is on a paper.** One of the seven is Nessa Pike's own boat of about thirteen tons and she gave her hours and said the bill comes to her own table and not to anybody else's. A woman of about fifty-eight with an end stall said the figure on that page is her figure, that she wrote it up in chalk on the first of June, and that she is not going to be told what to do with it. One hundred and sixty-eight pence came in and the bag stands at five hundred and thirty-two.
4. **CHAPTER 434, SUNDAY THE TWENTY-SIXTH. A TWELFTH WEEK, AND A BELLWRIGHT OFF THE REEF LINE.** The three nots of the eighth of June past stand in the first day of a twelfth week unasked. **Mina Kett, of about thirty-four, a bellwright of Tidewatch, came down at about half past ten with her own tools in a box and took eleven battens off the keel of a boat of about nineteen tons lying on that hard since June in about two hours and ten minutes, and numbered the ends in pencil with her own marks and not with figures.** She was told she would be paid at the figure in chalk and **said out loud once that that is a caulker's figure and not hers, that a bellwright off that line gets five shillings, being sixty pence, and that she has been getting that for nine years and has never asked anybody for more, and that she was saying it once so that it would be in somebody's head and was not going to say it again and was not going to be thanked for it.** The room over a joiner's shop was let out at two o'clock; about twenty went up and three came down and eleven of the twenty could not read; Hobb Lee read the head-notes out loud with his own name and the hour under each; there was no claim in any of them. **About forty pieces of lead came out of the lid of her box at about four o'clock and the nail in the door frame of her workshop and the woman of about sixty-one and the penny and the twenty-six years are on the page, and she said these are not for this coast and are not to go on a wall.** Two baulks of oak planed went out at one hundred and sixty-eight pence and the bag stands at three hundred and sixty-four.
5. **CHAPTER 435, MONDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH. THE SEVENTY-THIRD WIPE, THE EIGHTY-FIFTH CISTERN, AND THE CUTOFF.** The wall came down bare for the seventy-third time and went up at the angle it has been at since the twelfth and nobody put it back; the cistern was charged and walked on for the eighty-fifth time and the top name on that rota board is still off it. A sheet of good paper came from the counter in a room off that market at about nine in the morning at a penny out of the holder's own coat and not out of that bag, with four days on it and one figure on it. **Mara Venn said one thing about it: that it has got a person in it, that there is no column in that yard's book for a person who has been asked to turn up, and that she would put it in the second column with the hour against it and not in the first.** **Halvard Ness, of about twenty-three, laid fifteen fathoms of chain off his tender's quarter round a spurle and back with a weight on the tail of it, and said he would not ask anybody's leave to pull it and that nobody in that boat had any standing to tell him not to.** The woman of fifty-eight was told that the figure on her slate is the same figure as the charge at the foot of the sheet on the wall of her stall, and said it has been the same figure since the first of June and that two figures on two pieces of wood nine feet apart is no more than that, and asked for her tobacco to be paid for. One hundred and sixty-eight pence came in and the bag stands at five hundred and thirty-two.
6. **CHAPTER 436, TUESDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH. THE FORTY-NINTH WAGE TUESDAY, AND A BOAT THAT STRUCK A BAULK.** The column did not move; forty-nine weeks stand fallen due at the close of the day. Seven boats and about thirty men were on the water from ten past seven until the last of the ebb. **The new piece of keel came off the battens in three pieces and did not fit, and nobody in that company said a word about it for about ten minutes, and then Mina Kett put her thumb into the end of the middle piece and said out loud to about thirty men that it is a guess with a curve in it and that she had told them so; a sixteenth was taken off the whole length and not off one end and it went on in about two hours.** The chain weight came over the rail at twenty-two minutes past two and the reason was written down with the hour against it. **At about ten past two a boat of about twenty-two tons struck a baulk of oak that that yard's own hands had laid down at half past eight in the morning with about nine inches of it out of the water in a sea and no light on it and no flag and nothing on it, and opened about nine foot of her garboard and put a hole in her lee rail about the size of two hands, and nobody was hurt.** The owner said in his own mouth that the baulk is that yard's and the bill is that yard's. Two payments of one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being three hundred and thirty-six pence, went out and one hundred and sixty-eight came in and the bag stands at three hundred and sixty-four.
7. **CHAPTER 437, WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-NINTH. THE BILL, AND THE SECOND MAN IN THAT BELL.** A caulker of about twenty-three who crews in no boat and holds no office and is on no sheet was asked in that shed whether he would take the caulking of that joint on that afternoon and said the figure he works to out loud before he was asked for the day. **A man of about twenty-nine of the third lay went down in that bell at about half past five in the morning, one at a time, and came up and said there is a hole about two foot aft of where the shore is, and that it is not open, and that it is soft, and that his hand went in about the depth of a thumb and came back with a smell off it that was not tar and was not oil, and that he has not been in her in June and is not going to give anybody anything else.** The first man said he had put his thumb through the veneer of that plank on the Friday before last. **Both accounts are in the book and neither agrees with the other.** The plank and iron and roves and copper went out at one hundred and sixty-eight pence and the bag stands at one hundred and ninety-six.
8. **CHAPTER 438, THURSDAY THE THIRTIETH. THE EIGHTY-SIXTH CISTERN, AND A WORD ASKED FOR OUT LOUD.** The third and last charge in these ten days and the top name is still off that board. **The reason a man was put in that bell was written down before he went down, which had not been done before.** A master of about forty-six out of Lowfen went down and said the plank is not soft and is as sound as anything in her and that he put his whole hand flat on it and did not try to force it, and said that he is not going to change it because somebody else had been in there and he had not, and that one of the three men is wrong and he does not know which. **Hobb Lee came down that slip at about eleven in the morning in daylight and asked what the man who keeps a keel right in between tides with a chain and a weight on it is called, and was told there is a word and it is not taken by being said, and said he would not ask again and would not say it at his table and that he would not read it out in that room.** The woman of fifty-eight said three days had gone by and not one penny of any of it had come off anybody's boat and would like that written down somewhere and not on her slate. One hundred and sixty-eight pence came in and the bag stands at three hundred and sixty-four.
9. **CHAPTER 439, FRIDAY THE FIRST DAY OF OCTOBER. FOUR REQUESTS AND THE SAME NINE WORDS, AND THE WORD SAID OUT LOUD.** **A man of about forty-four asked for a line to be struck out of a sheet carrying his name and an hour and eleven minutes of lateness, and was refused. A bellwright of about thirty-four asked for her line to be struck out of the same sheet on the ground that the figure on it is not hers and that a man of about forty-six who cannot read could be told in three weeks that a bellwright is paid a mark and eightpence in Morrow Quay, and was refused, and asked for a second line under it and got one, and that line is in the second column and names her own figure of five shillings, being sixty pence, and the hundred and eight pence a day she is under by. Two men off the first lay asked for a line out of that yard's own leaf and were refused.** It is the same nine words in all four cases and there is no column in that book for which those words are different from any other. **Ormond Kettle said the word out loud at about half past two in the afternoon and was told it is a trade and not a power and settles nothing and prices nothing and makes nobody better off than he was on the Thursday before; Mina Kett said that on her coast it means a man who keeps a keel right and not a man who fits one; Sedge Rundle said from that doorway that the asking is not the work.** One hundred and sixty-eight pence went out and the bag stands at one hundred and ninety-six.
10. **CHAPTER 440, SATURDAY THE SECOND DAY OF OCTOBER. THE READ-BACK, THE FIGURES, AND THE STANDING CONDITION.** The leaf was read back at about ten past five in the evening on the flat of the bench stone at that mole head, in the open, in the ship's own left hand, all four columns including the empty one, **with both definitions on the face of that reading: one hundred and seventy-two at the hour and one hundred and seventy-three at the close; seven hundred and thirty-seven at the hour and seven hundred and thirty-nine at the close; none; one hundred and twenty-five at the hour and one hundred and twenty-five at the close, with no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it, the column not closed and not struck out, and the reason entered once on the twenty-eighth of August and entered again nowhere.** **A caulker of about twenty-three was paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence in coin on the flat of the bench stone at about four in the afternoon, asked for by name at about ten in the morning on Wednesday the twenty-ninth of September past, and on no other day of these ten.** The room over a joiner's shop was let out for the fifth time and about seventeen went up and three came down, and about twenty went up on the twenty-sixth, which is about thirty-seven across the two Sundays. **The woman of no office said one thing four feet off the stone: that what is hers and what is anybody's has to be written down and is not that yard's book, that the four columns and the figure and the method do not go on the table in Fish Street or on any wall in this harbor, that her name does not go on a sheet for any of this, and that forty marks first after food is not reduced by a chain and a weight and a bellwright from off the reef line.** The bag is one hundred and ninety-six pence, being one mark and three shillings, against a wage of six hundred and forty, and is short by four hundred and forty-four pence, being two marks ten shillings and fourpence. **A harbor poorer on the second day of October than on the twenty-third day of September and poorer than on the fourteenth day of May.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **CHAPTER 421, MONDAY THE THIRTEENTH. THE SEVENTY-FIRST WIPE, THE EIGHTY-FIRST CISTERN, AND THE MAN WHO CANNOT READ.** A day at a berth came in at one hundred and sixty-eight pence and the bag is five hundred and seventy-six pence, being three marks eight shillings. **Emmet Slade, of about thirty, of that lay, with a boat of about nine tons and a claim window on a wreck off the point, came up that slip at about two in the afternoon, said he had heard there was a paper against him, said in the first half minute that he cannot read, and was told there is a paper at a counter in an office off the west basin, that nobody in that shed has seen it, that it cannot be read to him there because he would have the reader's head and not the paper, and that nobody in that shed knows whether it is against his boat.** He was told that being told it is not would be a kindness and not a finding, and he said he would go the next day. **And at about four a screw-steam packet put her hook on and a man of about thirty-four landed a sack of printed sheets at a stall and said out loud that the lot had been given to him at the top of a gangway by a man behind a counter with a book open who did not ask his name.**
2. **CHAPTER 422, TUESDAY THE FOURTEENTH. THE FORTY-SEVENTH WAGE TUESDAY, A MESSAGE OUT OF A BOY'S HAND, AND TWENTY-FOUR SHEETS THROUGH A COUNTER.** The column is at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks with twenty empty envelopes folded the same way by a woman of about fifty-eight about eleven weeks ago, and it did not move. **Dill Cardew, of about seventeen, carried a message ashore down the slip at the second lay and a man of about forty-four off the water with two fingers of his left hand stiff took it out of his hand, read it standing up in about the time it takes to read four lines, said it was a thing a man does not carry in a street, put it inside his coat and went up the slip.** What the boy lost was the paper and the hour he was going to be somewhere else in, and he stood on a step for about twenty-five minutes with no reason in his hand. The man he was going to did not send it again. **Twenty-four sheets went through a copyist's counter in a room off that market at a penny a sheet, being twenty-four pence, being two shillings, out of a stall-holder's hand, and the woman of about fifty-nine did not ask what she was copying and was not asked and did not stop.**
3. **CHAPTER 423, WEDNESDAY THE FIFTEENTH. THE NOTICE, PRINTED IN FULL, AND THE FIGURE IT IS PUT UP ON.** The sheet went up at about ten in the morning on the outside of the oil slate, and the oil figure was not taken down first and cannot be taken off. **Its first line says that a piece of worked glass that has had a scene taken from a living person keeps what the scene was, and that what the scene was stands off the piece into the air of a room and settles on the people in that room and is taken home in the clothes; its second says it is not a fever and not a disease and will sit in a market the same as it sits in a room; its third says every person who has been in a room with such a piece is to be entered in the claim book at the counter of the harbor authority of the town where he stands; its fourth says a book is not a court; its fifth says no person and no town is named and that it is put up on the outside of this figure; and its sixth gives the charge for lodging one claim as one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, and says a claim so lodged is read out in the room where the public book is kept, on a Sunday, by a man at the end of the table.** The man of about thirty-four said he could not say it was a lie. **The woman of about fifty-eight turned her slate about so the oil figure was showing again, moved the sack off her counter against her own back boards, and said the figure is not coming off for a piece of paper with a date on the top of it.** About thirty people stood in front of that wall by noon and nobody put a hand on it. **Calder Marr read it twice, found no name in it and no town in it, stood in front of the date at the head of it, and did not go up the hill.**
4. **CHAPTER 424, THURSDAY THE SIXTEENTH. THE EIGHTY-SECOND CISTERN, THE CAULKER'S SEVENTH DAY, AND THE SIX LINES READ ALOUD.** A man of about forty-six read the six lines out loud in the middle aisle at about eleven in front of about thirty people of whom about nine could not read, and wrote his own name and the hour under it on the back of a crate. Four men said out loud they had been in the room on the twelfth, and there were about twenty people in that room and nobody counted who was in it. A man of about thirty-six said he had been in a shed with glass off a wreck in April and had come out and eaten his supper, and a man of about forty-one said he has not been near a piece since the fourth of June and has had a cold in his teeth since about three o'clock on the Sunday, and said out loud that he does not know which of two things is the thing that does it. **And Hobb Lee said out loud that he will not read a claim out at that table as a claim, and gave his reason twice, and said that the day he does he has turned that table into a court with a net-mender at the head of it.**
5. **CHAPTER 425, FRIDAY THE SEVENTEENTH. THE COUNTER SHUT AND THE PAPER ON THE WEST BASIN.** A chandler of about fifty whose wife keeps the count would not sell eight fathoms of tarred rope at four shillings, being forty-eight pence, to **Nate Pry, of about forty-four, of that lay, who carried a piece of worked glass about two hands square out of a boat's hold in June on his own back for a shilling and a half and has not been near a piece since**, and gave his reason in his own mouth: he is not going to stand in his shop and ask a man whether he has been in a room with a piece of glass, and he has a wife and a girl of eleven behind that counter, and he would rather be wrong about himself than about her. He took fourpence on an old account and gave the rope back onto the man's arm. **And at about four in the afternoon a man of about fifty, who works at a table with two papers on it in an office off the west basin, put a four-line paper on that counter with no name on it and no seal at the foot of it, saying a claim has been entered under a sheet that went up in the front street on the fifteenth, that a person who has been in a room with a piece of worked glass with a scene in it is to be entered in the claim book of that harbor under his own name, and that until he has been entered a claim window held by him is held.**
6. **CHAPTER 426, SATURDAY THE EIGHTEENTH. THE BERTH HELD, AND THE WORD *OFF*.** A sheet tied to the peg of a berth at the head of the third lay with a piece of line, dated the seventeenth, held a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers, and her owner said the sixth clause lets me in and does not give me a berth, and put her on the hard at the back of that lay from about seven until about ten and went out on the sixth clause that evening and came in past the outer marks at about five the next morning. **And Emmet Slade, who cannot read, was at a counter in an office off the west basin at about eleven with his name written at the top of a sheet, and was told that the word on it is off, and said that off is a different word to held, and was told that off is the word that is on the paper and that he was not going to be given another one; and asked whether it was against his boat and was told his boat is not on that counter.** A man of about thirty-one with a chart in a bag said one sentence at the foot of a slip and said he is not on a sheet and is not going to be.
7. **CHAPTER 427, SUNDAY THE NINETEENTH. THE ROPEMAKER IS FOUND OUT AND PUT OUT OF HER ROOM.** A man of about twenty-six who stacks empties said on the Friday before last at a quay, to about four people, that the woman who carried a box up two flights of stairs on the Sunday before lives on the third lay; nobody asked him where he got it. **At about eleven in the morning Ruben Priest, of about fifty-eight, who takes the rents in two houses on that slip and has taken this one for eleven years at nine marks a year, being one thousand four hundred and forty pence, paid out of rope, told her the room is not hers after the end of the quarter.** He gave his reason in his own mouth and asked her nothing, and said he was not going to ask because an answer given in a street stays in the head of the man who asked for it. She asked him one question, which was when. She cut the rope off her box at about one o'clock, lifted the panel out and put it back in, knotted the rope the way she knots it, and carried the box down the slip on her own bad knee backwards with the barrow's wheel against the step above her between one o'clock and half past two, and nobody on that lay carried anything for her. **The room over the joiner's shop was let out for the third time the same afternoon, about sixteen went up and three came down, eleven of the sixteen could not read, nine heads were read out loud from about two minutes past two to about twenty-one minutes past three, there was no claim in any of the nine and no claim on that table, and the woman of about fifty-eight came up with her slate and said out loud that a sheet on a wall is not on that table and that she is not going to ask anybody to read it out in there.**
8. **CHAPTER 428, MONDAY THE TWENTIETH. THE SEVENTY-SECOND WIPE, THE EIGHTY-THIRD CISTERN, A DATE THAT ENDED, AND THE DIVER.** **The fourth line of the paper at the top left of that door in Fish Street ended on the said day and that paper has been on that door twenty days and has been answered by nobody**, and about sixteen people went up that stair on the Sunday before and whether one of the eleven was in that room is not a thing anybody in that room looked for. **A man went down in a bell at about eleven foot at a berth on the third lay at ten in the morning with nine foot of a crate of three pieces of worked glass off his left shoulder, put a mend in a garboard with oakum and a marlinspike, and came up at about twenty past eleven.** He sat on the stones and said three things and no more, and said that he has had that taste of iron three times in nine months and that on each of those three times he was within a foot of a piece of worked glass for about as long as it takes to boil an egg, and that he has got no reading out of it and is not going to say that he has. **The ship's hand said out loud that she has got no figure for that and is not going to invent one, and wrote one line in the second column against a reason with no name against it.**
9. **CHAPTER 429, TUESDAY THE TWENTY-FIRST. THE FORTY-EIGHTH WAGE TUESDAY, AND THE BOY TELLS HIM TWICE AND WRONG.** Forty-four pence went out for a loaf and a half, a candle and a pot, and the bag is five hundred and thirty-two pence, being three marks four shillings and fourpence. **A boy of about seventeen was sent by a man behind a counter in that market to tell Emmet Slade that his window is stopped and that he is to hand in a third of anything landed, and told him in about eight words in the middle of that slip; and he said out loud that there is no third of anything, and that he has now got it twice and both times a bit different, and that the next market was the following morning, and he went home and did not take his boat out.** Nobody in that yard asked that boy where he was on the fourteenth. **And at about half past nine in the evening the holder of that writ said out loud, once, in a working man's own account of what he wrote down on the twenty-second day of August past and why, that he wrote eleven dates on a leaf of his own hand in a room over a fish market, in the order he read them, off a board about a yard wide, with no name and no figure against any of the eleven, and that he did it because in July he had a thing only he had and in August two other men had things only they had, and that he is not going to tell anybody what is on it unless it is read out in that room on a Sunday with his name and the hour under it.**
10. **CHAPTER 430, WEDNESDAY THE TWENTY-SECOND. THE READ-BACK, THE FIGURES, AND THE STANDING CONDITION.** The leaf was read back at about ten past five in the evening on the flat of the bench stone at that mole head, in the open, in the ship's own left hand, all four columns including the empty one, **with both definitions on the face of that reading: one hundred and sixty-two at the hour and one hundred and sixty-three at the close; six hundred and eighty-seven at the hour and six hundred and eighty-nine at the close; none; one hundred and twenty-five at the hour and one hundred and twenty-five at the close, with no hundred and twenty-sixth line in it, the column not closed and not struck out, and the reason entered once on the twenty-eighth of August and entered again nowhere.** The woman of no office said one thing four feet off the stone and was not answered and was not improved on. The bag is five hundred and thirty-two pence against a wage of six hundred and forty and is short by one hundred and eight pence, being nine shillings. **There is no flour in that market, there has been no barrel of lamp oil in that harbor since the twenty-ninth day of August, the figure of four hundred and fifty pence is on a board that is not cleared with the new sheet on the same square of wall above it, the paper of four lines in Fish Street is on that door and has been answered by nobody, the nine-line sheet with a seal on it is on the front street wall for thirty-nine days, the light is out, the north berth is out, the hose is dead until the spring, the tide gang is four men short, the hard at Ashtide is unanswered, one berth on the third lay is short, nineteen winters are disputed, and forty-eight weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them. A harbor is poorer on the twenty-second day of September than on the thirteenth and poorer than on the fourteenth of May.**

### The four figures at the close of Chapter 430, and which definition each is

- **AT THE HOUR OF THE READING: ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-TWO / SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-SEVEN / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE. AT THE CLOSE OF THE DAY: ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-THREE / SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-NINE / NONE / ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE.**
- **THE FIRST COLUMN'S FIGURE IS A COUNT OF ENTRIES AND THE FOURTH'S IS A COUNT OF LINES, AND A DAY OF THE FIRST COLUMN CARRIES ONE ENTRY AGAINST IT WHATEVER ELSE THAT DAY PRINTED, SO THAT A STRANGER WITH A LEAF AND A PENCIL CAN COUNT BOTH. THE SECOND COLUMN'S FIGURE IS THAT LEDGER'S OWN AND IS NOT A COUNT OF ANYTHING A STRANGER CAN CHECK FROM A MOLE.** Both definitions are on the face of Chapter 430's own reading, in the ship's mouth, and the thirty-day run is re-derived from the close of Chapter 400: the first column's base is one hundred and thirty-three and takes one entry against each of the thirty days with no day in two of them; the second column's base is five hundred and thirty-nine and takes five a day, three before the hour of that day's reading and two after it; the third takes none and nobody is appointed to it; **the fourth takes no line in this volume and stands where it stands.**
- **THE THINGS THAT CAME OFF THE PANEL AND THE THINGS THAT CAME OFF THE CRATE ARE THE FIGURES OF THIS MOVEMENT AND NEITHER OF THEM IS IN THAT LEDGER.** A cold in the teeth and a taste of iron like a nail and a man not knowing which of two doors he came out of; and the same three things in a man in a bell who could not tell which of two hatches he came up out of. And, out of a mouth and not out of a paper: a date at the head of a notice, a charge at the foot of it, a figure on a board that did not come down, and a sack standing against the back boards of an end stall with a stone on it.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 430

- **Calder and Mara. THE COMMITTED RELATIONSHIP IS UNCHANGED AND UNTOUCHED AND NO WORD OF IT HAS BEEN SAID TWICE.** She was in that harbor and going nowhere, of no office, not on the crew, not restored, not forgiven, forty marks first after food neither reduced nor paid. She was on that mole head from about five on the twenty-second and said one thing four feet off the stone, and said that there is not one figure in that harbor that puts a sheet on a wall and a cold in the teeth together, and that neither of those is going to be settled in that shed this month, and neither of them cancels the other, and she is not going to stand on a Wednesday evening and pretend that one of them is a comfort. **The holder of that writ did not answer that and did not improve on it.** She was not in the room in Fish Street on the nineteenth and did not go up that slip at any hour of that day.
- **Calder and Nessa. She is the pair the record stands on and she read the leaf back in full at about ten past five on the twenty-second with both definitions on the face of the reading, and she wrote the figure of the week against the reason the wage column did not move on the fourteenth and again on the twenty-first. She put the number of the week against a week is a week that came and went and said that is not a complaint. She told a man who cannot read a paper that he must ask for it to be read to him at a counter in front of the man behind it and take somebody with him who can hear him say he has done it, and said that bring me the words. She said out loud that she has got no figure for a cold in a man's teeth and is not going to invent one, and wrote one line in the second column with a reason against it and no name against it, and the holder of that writ is not on any page. She asked Hobb Lee whether a poor man's claim is a different claim from a paid one and wrote his answer down with his reason.**
- **Calder and Alden. UNMOVED. THE FAR BENCH WAS OCCUPIED FROM TEN UNTIL FOUR ON ALL TEN OF THE TEN DAYS AND WAS NOT APPROACHED ON ANY OF THEM, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DID NOT GO OVER TO HIM ON ANY OF THEM, AND NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT, AND THE SHOE BESIDE HIM THAT IS NOT HIS IS ON EVERY ONE OF THEM AND HAS BEEN THERE SINCE THE THIRD OF MAY PAST, AND NEITHER BROTHER WENT NEAR THE OTHER AT ANY HOUR OF ANY OF THE TEN DAYS.** No fragment, no report talk, no second story and no confession. **The partial confession is not paid in these ten days and is owed to a later movement of this volume.**
- **Calder and Bevin. The third column is empty and unappointed on all ten days, the boy's hand is at the head of it and was not scratched out, the name beside it was not said again, his surname is on no page of the ten, and the three nots standing against the eighth of June past are an eleventh week in which nobody in that crew has said one word about them. He was not on the stone on any of the ten days and was put on nothing.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren. SIXTY-ONE ON ALL TEN DAYS, ELEVEN PIECES OF A BOAT ON THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE, A BOAT'S HOOK IN HIS RIGHT HAND, AND HE SAYS NOTHING IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS.** He turned a piece over and stopped the hook in a crack in the stone, turned a fourth piece over twice, sat on a seventh for six hours with his back to the water, got the tenth out and stood it up, stood over a fifth with the hook in his hand and did not use it, set a third and an eighth side by side and left the gap open, sat on the eleventh for the second time and did nothing to it, scraped a lump of old bedding off the sixth with the point of the hook and put it in his pocket, was sat on the second and went and stood looking down the harbour side and came back, **and on the last day got up off the ninth piece at about half past three and went home, which he has not done on any of the thirty days that this leaf has been adding to.**
- **Calder and the ropemaker of the third lay. HE ASKED HER NOTHING AND NOBODY IN THAT YARD WENT UP THAT SLIP ON THE NINETEENTH TO SAY ONE WORD TO HER ABOUT THE TWELFTH. A man of about fifty-eight who takes rents asked her nothing and gave his own reason in his own mouth; she asked him one question; and there is no figure in that yard's leaf against that room, that rope walk, those eleven years, that box or that knee.**
- **Calder and the public book. It is a book and not a document of that yard's, it is on a joiner's table over a shop, and nothing of that yard's figures, its four columns or its method is on it or on any wall. He put a leaf of eleven dates on the bench stone at about half past nine on the twenty-first and said why he had written it, and said he is not going to tell anybody what is on it unless it is read out in that room on a Sunday with his name and the hour under it in the hand of the man at the end of that table. He read the sheet on the wall twice on the fifteenth, found no name in it and no town in it, and did not go up the hill.**

### The power state at the end of Chapter 430

**Line Diver. NO STAGE WAS TAKEN IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS AND NONE WAS IMPROVED, RE-TAKEN OR RENAMED. THE COUNT OF *KEELWRIGHT* IS ZERO AND THE COUNT OF THE WORD *PLATE* IS ZERO AND THE COUNT OF *SEAM* IS ZERO. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND WAS NOT USED, NOT IMPROVED AND NOT NAMED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS; A CRATE OF THREE PIECES OF WORKED GLASS WAS DESCRIBED ON THE FACE OF CHAPTER 428 AND IT TOLD THE MAN IN THE BELL NOTHING, AND IT SETTLES NO ARGUMENT AND CONVICTS NOBODY AND NAMES NOBODY. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE WAS NOT TAKEN AGAIN. NO CHAPTER ENTERED AN ECHO, ENTERED A VESSEL OR SURFACED A PRACTICE TRACE, AND THE COUNT OF EACH IS ZERO. THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE AND PAYING ITS COST IS NOT NAMING IT. THE USE OF THE FIRST OF THE SECOND SEAM'S TWO MARKS REMAINS CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES WITH NO FIFTH, AND NEITHER NINE-MARK SEASON WAS PAID, AND THE SECOND SEAM WAS NOT LOOKED AT BY ANYBODY ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. THE WHOLE FOULING LADDER IS IN ANOTHER MAN'S OWN BOOK AND NOBODY HAS EXPLAINED IT AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE ASKED AND HE IS NOT FISK. NO PERSON OF THAT YARD WAS IN ANY STONE ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS.** What was paid instead of a stage: a room, a berth, a coil of rope, a boy's quarter of an hour, three hours on a hard, a sack carried off a packet and a sheet pasted on a wall.

### The bodies and the dated positions at the end of Chapter 430

- **THE BAG IS FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO PENCE, BEING THREE MARKS FOUR SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, AND THE FIGURE IT IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHT PENCE, BEING NINE SHILLINGS, AND IT IS NEVER ZERO AND NOBODY IS GOING TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER IT SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO PAY IT. THE WHOLE OF WHAT CAME INTO THAT YARD IN THE TEN DAYS IS THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE ON TWO DAYS, BEING THE THIRTEENTH AND THE SEVENTEENTH, AT THE FIGURE IN CHALK ON A SLATE AT AN END STALL. THE WHOLE OF WHAT WENT OUT OF IT IS TWO HUNDRED AND TWELVE PENCE ON TWO DAYS, BEING ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN COIN ON THE FLAT OF THE BENCH STONE AT ABOUT FOUR IN THE AFTERNOON ON THE SIXTEENTH TO A CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE, AND FORTY-FOUR PENCE, BEING THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, ON THE TWENTY-FIRST AT ABOUT HALF PAST TEN IN THE MORNING FOR A LOAF AND A HALF, A CANDLE AND A POT. NOTHING HAS BEEN IN A TIN IN THAT SHED SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH DAY OF APRIL PAST, AND NOT ONE PENNY OF THE WHOLE OF IT CAME OUT OF THE OWNER OF ANY BOAT, OUT OF THE MAN WITH TWO PAPERS, OR OUT OF THE CROWN.**
- **THE WAGE COLUMN IS AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS WITH TWENTY ENVELOPES IN A CHEST, TWO WAGE TUESDAYS FELL IN THE TEN DAYS, BEING THE FORTY-SEVENTH ON TUESDAY THE FOURTEENTH AND THE FORTY-EIGHTH ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-FIRST, THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE ON EITHER, FORTY-SIX WEEKS STOOD FALLEN DUE AT THE OPEN OF THE TEN DAYS AND FORTY-EIGHT STAND AT THE CLOSE OF THEM, THE FORTY-NINTH FALLS ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH, AND NOBODY IS TO WRITE ONE WORD UNDER ANY OF IT SAYING ANYBODY IS GOING TO PAY IT.**
- **THE WALL CAME DOWN BARE TWICE IN THE TEN DAYS, BEING THE SEVENTY-FIRST ON MONDAY THE THIRTEENTH AND THE SEVENTY-SECOND ON MONDAY THE TWENTIETH, AND WENT UP AT THE ANGLE IT HAS BEEN AT SINCE THE TWELFTH ON BOTH OF THEM AND ON THE OTHER EIGHT DAYS AS WELL, AND NOBODY PUT IT BACK. THE CISTERN WAS CHARGED THREE TIMES AND WALKED ON NONE OF IT, BEING THE EIGHTY-FIRST ON THE THIRTEENTH, THE EIGHTY-SECOND ON THE SIXTEENTH AND THE EIGHTY-THIRD ON THE TWENTIETH, AND THE TOP NAME ON THE ROTA BOARD IS STILL OFF IT. THE FOURTEENTH, FIFTEENTH, SEVENTEENTH, EIGHTEENTH, NINETEENTH, TWENTY-FIRST AND TWENTY-SECOND OF SEPTEMBER ARE NOT ROTA DAYS AND NO CHARGE WAS PLACED ON ANY OF THEM.**
- **THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY PAST IS ON ITS WALL IN A DIFFERENT STREET FOR ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-EIGHT DAYS AND HAS NOT BEEN TOUCHED AND HAS NOT BEEN TAKEN DOWN. THE BELLWRIGHT OF THAT HARBOR HAS NOT BEEN ASKED FOR ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY DAYS, THE CHEST IS SHUT, THE EIGHT MARKS AND A DAY OF A BOAT HAVE NOT BEEN ARGUED, AND NO DIGIT OF ANYTHING HE EVER SAID IS ON A PAGE.**
- **A FOURTH PAPER, ON A FOURTH WALL, IN A DIFFERENT STREET FROM THE OTHER THREE: SIX PRINTED LINES WITH A DATE AT THE HEAD AND A CHARGE AT THE FOOT, PUT UP ON THE FIFTEENTH AT ABOUT TEN IN THE MORNING ON THE OUTSIDE OF A FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE, IT HAS BEEN ON THAT WALL FOR SEVEN DAYS, IT NAMES NO PERSON AND NO TOWN, NOBODY HAS ANSWERED IT AND NOBODY HAS KNOCKED IT DOWN, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WHO WAS IN THAT MARKET ON THE FIFTEENTH AND READ IT IS A MAN WHO HAS BEEN TOLD A THING ON THE DAY.**
- **THE PAPER OF FOUR LINES AT THE TOP LEFT OF THE DOOR OF THAT ROOM IN FISH STREET WAS PUT UP ON THE THIRTY-FIRST DAY OF AUGUST PAST AND IS TWENTY-TWO DAYS OLD, ITS FOURTH LINE ENDED ON THE TWENTIETH DAY OF SEPTEMBER PAST, HAS BEEN ANSWERED BY NOBODY AND IS NOT TO BE ANSWERED BY ANYBODY IN THIS VOLUME, AND THE ELEVEN PEOPLE IT NAMES ARE COUNTED, UNNAMED, ON NO SHEET, HAVE BEEN TOLD ONLY THAT THE PAPER IS THERE, AND NONE OF THEM WAS ASKED WHETHER HE WAS IN THAT ROOM ON THE SUNDAY.**
- **THE TWO OBJECTS OF NOBODY'S ARE FOUR HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT DAYS OLD UP THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE, ABOUT NINE FEET APART, UNDER TWO TARPAULINS, ONE WITH A CORNER OFF IT SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF JUNE PAST AND NOT LASHED BACK, AND NEITHER HAS MOVED. THE OWNER OF THE PAGE OF SIX NAMES HAS SAID NOTHING TO ANYBODY FOR SEVENTY DAYS AND HAS BEEN GIVEN NOTHING BY ANYBODY. THE BENCH UNDER THAT PUMP IS BARE FOR THE TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-FOURTH NIGHT.**
- **THE TWO LIGHTS OFF THE POINT HAVE NOT MOVED IN FIFTY-TWO DAYS, COUNTED FROM THE HOUR THEY WERE FIRST SEEN ON THE EVENING OF THE FIRST OF AUGUST PAST. THE NINETY IS CLOSED AT SEVENTY DAYS WITH NO SEVENTY-FIRST DAY AND NO DAY OF IT IS ENTERED IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS. THE CUSTODY ROOM WAS NOT ENTERED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND IS NOT ENTERED AGAIN UNTIL THE LAST MOVEMENT.**
- **A HARBOR POORER ON THE TWENTY-SECOND DAY OF SEPTEMBER THAN ON THE THIRTEENTH AND POORER THAN ON THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY. THE MOLE-HEAD LIGHT IS OUT WITH ITS LENS OUT SINCE THE SEVENTH OF MAY, A BARREL OF LAMP OIL IS FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE, BEING THIRTY-SEVEN SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, QUOTED ON THE FIRST OF JUNE, WITH FEBRUARY'S THREE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING THIRTY-ONE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, STANDING VISIBLE ABOVE IT AND BOTH DATES ON THE BOARD, AND THAT FIGURE DID NOT COME DOWN AND WAS NOT TAKEN OFF, AND THERE HAS BEEN NO OIL IN THAT HARBOR SINCE THE TWENTY-NINTH OF AUGUST AND A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-EIGHT WROTE ONE WORD IN CHALK ON THE EDGE OF THAT BOARD AND WOULD NOT RULE A LINE UNDER THE FIGURE. PHYSIC IS FOURTEEN PENCE AND THERE IS NONE OF IT IN THIS HARBOR. THERE IS NO FLOUR IN THAT MARKET AND NONE IS COMING THIS MONTH. THE NORTH BERTH IS OUT, THE HOSE IS DEAD UNTIL THE SPRING, THE TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT, THE HARD AT ASHTIDE IS UNANSWERED, THE THIRD LAY FILLS ON THE FIRST OF APRIL AND ONE BERTH IS SHORT.**
- **STANDING UNPAID AND UNMOVED AND NONE OF IT ENTERED IN FULL IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS.** Three marks to a man of Ashtide, whose anchor date of the eighth of August past is a legacy of an earlier entry and is ruled not repaired. Seven pence to that yard's own shipwright. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright, unargued, chest shut, not asked in one hundred and thirty days. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid. Forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots a tenth week unasked through Saturday the eighteenth and an eleventh week from Sunday the nineteenth, the third column unfilled and unappointed. **AND STANDING WITH THOSE SIX: a page of six names on a mole with a boat as a price and no figure and a stone in one man's own pocket; a municipal claim on one of the three things in the circuit custody room; a box in an office on the west basin that is no longer empty and another box on the same table that is empty and that a man of about fifty wants left empty; a nine-line sheet with a seal on it in the front street for thirty-nine days, which nobody put up and nobody has answered; a slip of paper with a figure on it and no name on it in a drawer, not looked at, not priced, not headed; and a dash at the end of the third line of the twenty-second head of a public volume in a room over a joiner's shop. NONE OF THE ABOVE IS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS.**

### What is owed and what is not
