### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **391 — Saturday the fourteenth of August, the sixty-first day of the ninety. A SHEET RULED IN THAT SHED WITH A LINE FOR EVERY MAN IN EVERY BOAT AND NO FIGURE IN IT AND NO NAME ON IT BEFORE THE MAN GAVE IT. PAID.** A single sheet folded once, ruled on the bench stone at about seven in the morning with a nick in the rule, a line for a master and a line for every man under him and a ruled column at the right-hand edge for a master's hand and an hour, and eleven is the highest number on it and was written before anybody was asked anything. **Nessa refuses in advance to have a figure put on it.** Five masters are asked in the same words on the said day and three of them say no with a reason and two say yes, and no master is asked twice: a master of about forty-seven of the third lay, who has been in company three times and had it go wrong twice on a Wednesday when a man was not there, and who will not put a Wednesday into a file with his name at the top of it; a herring skipper of fifty-one with papers of his own who has not shown them to anybody in four years and who says a paper with eleven masters' names on it is in a room by Christmas with a box and a date in it; a master of about fifty-eight of the second lay with a boy of nine, who says the part he keeps coming back to is the eleven and that he would rather somebody's list of eleven were a list of things a boat wants. Two say yes: a master of about twenty-nine of the second lay, who came up that hill twice on his own account and was not thanked either time and says a name on a sheet is worth more to him than a warp; and a master of about thirty-six of the second lay who says **he cannot read** before he says yes, and asks for the whole of the sheet to be read to him and for his own men read back to him. **THE COST OF THE FOUR IS SAID OUT LOUD ON THE SECOND SLIP IN THE HOUSE'S OWN FIGURE: four men gave a day apiece, a day is one hundred and sixty-eight pence, four days of it is six hundred and seventy-two pence, being four marks two shillings and eightpence, and none of that goes against the four and none of it came out of the bag, because nobody was paid for being asked. It came out of nobody.** The standing inventory is entered in full, once, on this day, and carried by a short pointer on the nine that follow.
2. **392 — Sunday the fifteenth of August, the sixty-second day of the ninety. A SHEET CARRIED ROUND SEVEN BOATS. PAID.** He goes round the seven berths on foot with the sheet on his forearm and a pencil behind his ear and no slate and no second paper, and every name goes on as the man who owned the boat said it, and where a man said a name twice in two different ways both are written and left side by side with no mark between them. **ONE MAN IN ONE BOAT WOULD NOT HAVE HIS NAME WRITTEN AND HIS MASTER WROTE IT WITH HIS OWN HAND BECAUSE THE MAN IS ABOARD**, and the reason is that a line with nothing against it is a hole and a hole in a sheet like that is a question somebody will ask him in a room in a month. That man does not know his name is on it and nobody in that shed is going to tell him. The master of about thirty-six is read the whole sheet twice, and says the same thing both times and that it is the first time anybody has read him the same thing twice, and asks for the third. **A SECOND WARP** comes out of a fore hatch bought off the west quay out of the master of about fifty-five's own hand, and the figure is in no book and is not on the sheet and is not on the leaf. The man of about fifty-one is not asked for a line and nothing of his goes on it. The man of about thirty-one came down the hill with his bag and went past the shed and was not asked for anything and is not going to be cited anywhere.
3. **393 — Monday the sixteenth of August, the sixty-third day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-SEVENTH WIPE, THE SEVENTY-THIRD CHARGE, AND A PAPER THAT IS A LIST. PAID.** **A MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY OF THAT THIRD LAY COMES UP THE HILL AT NINE IN THE MORNING AND SAYS THE WHOLE OF IT, having worked for men on pieces of paper all his life: *that sheet is a list, and you have told me for twelve days that a list is the boat, and the thing you have just told me not to do you have done, with a rule instead of a pen.*** And Calder says: it is a list. And then he gives the whole of what he has got against it, once: that paper says who is going and does not say who will be there, and that is the difference between those two, and if he had a second sheet with the men who will be on the mole head at four in the morning in it there would be two sheets and the second one would have a name against a man who cannot sleep and a name against a man who is owed forty marks, and he is not going to write it and has not written it. **And it does not make the paper clean and he does not claim that it does.** Nessa enters the master's words and her own against them, unjoined, and the man is entered as having come on purpose and not been sent for and not been thanked. Fell is asked on the Monday for the Tuesday, so that he can say no while there is still a Monday left.
4. **394 — Tuesday the seventeenth of August, the sixty-fourth day of the ninety. THE FORTY-THIRD WAGE TUESDAY. PAID.** The wage of four marks, being six hundred and forty pence, was not paid, the column did not move, and forty-three weeks stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them. Fell is on the mole head at about four in the morning and works the day where he is told to work it, which is the whole of the day, and is paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence in coin on the flat of the stone at about four in the afternoon, **on a morning on which that yard did not pay its own wage, and neither figure is anybody's debt and neither is a gift and the two are not to be added together.** **Nessa prices the Saturday out loud before anybody agrees to it: two days of that man is three hundred and thirty-six pence, being two marks one shilling and fourpence, against three hundred and twenty-eight pence in the bag, so the second day is eight pence more than the yard has, and a yard that has not got a figure has not got a Saturday.** He says he will earn it, at a berth, out of that yard's own figures, and not one penny out of the man with two papers or the owner of any of those seven boats. Fell says ask me again on Thursday. A master of about thirty-three with no papers on him comes up the hill to say he knows about a Saturday he is not on, so that if anybody asks him in a month he can say he knew, and nothing is written about him on the sheet and he is not thanked.
5. **395 — Wednesday the eighteenth of August, the sixty-fifth day of the ninety. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN. PAID.** A day's work with a boat and two men at a berth, on two tides and not one, at the figure in chalk on the slate at the end stall, and there were three men on that work where the want is four and the holder did the fourth thing himself. The man of about nineteen says the figure first, before anybody has said anything about money, and says he is not going to be paid twice for one day by anybody and that if anybody on that quay offers him a second mark and eightpence for carrying a sheet in his pocket he will hand it back. **A HERRING SKIPPER OF FIFTY-ONE COMES UP THE HILL AND SAYS HE HAS BEEN ASKED BY SOMEBODY WHETHER HE WANTS TO TAKE HIS NO BACK, AND WILL NOT SAY BY WHOM AND IS NOT ASKED, AND THAT HE HAS A NEW REASON AND THE NEW REASON IS WORSE THAN THE OLD ONE:** when it happens there will be a record that a man sailed and a record that a man did not, and both will be in the same room, and the one that says a man did not will be the one somebody asks about. At the foot of the mole the man of about fifty-one is on the crown with his page and his stone, and a man of about thirty-eight with no papers stands four feet below him, looks up at it, and goes away, and neither of them is asked for anything.
6. **396 — Thursday the nineteenth of August, the sixty-sixth day of the ninety. THE SEVENTY-FOURTH CHARGE, A ROUTE HE CANNOT USE, AND A SHEET NOBODY PUT UP. PAID.** He sits in the shed with a chart of the reach below the foul and gets no further with it than he got on the thirteenth: three soundings off a hand lead in a man's own boat lengths, a channel he has never been down, and a third channel that is three iron rings on a pinger on a buoy nobody owns, and the pinger went back up that coast on the Tuesday of the thirteenth and has not come down. **AND HE SAYS THE TWO THINGS OUT LOUD: *a thing you can draw is not a thing you have got*, and the man of about thirty-four who keeps the whole fouling ladder in his own book is not going to be asked by anybody in that crew, because he was not asked on the first of August and he told him plainly there is one thing in that book he will not give.** He goes up the mole head at four in the morning and there is nobody on the flat of the bench stone, and a maul on the step, and he stands about two minutes and goes down and does not go back at four in the afternoon and does not ask anybody where the man was, **and it goes in no column of any ledger and nobody is told anything about it at all.** The woman of about fifty-eight tells him, unasked, that there is a sheet up in the front street since Friday with a seal she cannot read and about nine lines in a small hand, and that there is a figure on the other side of the board where the other sheet was, so whoever put it there did not take the figure off first. He reads it at a quarter to four and says nothing at all about it. **IT PROPOSES THAT EVERY CONCERN THAT TAKES WORK OUT OF A HULL AND KEEPS NO ACCOUNT OF IT BE ENTERED IN ONE REGISTER, AND A CONCERN NOT ENTERED IS A CONCERN WHOSE ACCOUNTS ARE NOT TO BE PRODUCED TO ANYBODY. IT NAMES NO PERSON AND NO HARBOR AND PUTS NO FIGURE ON IT AND ASKS NOTHING OF ANYBODY STANDING IN THAT STREET, AND IT IS TRUE ENOUGH ON THE FACE OF IT THAT NOBODY WHO READS IT CAN GO UP THE STREET AND SAY IT IS A LIE, AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS ANSWERED IT AND THIS YARD IS NOT GOING TO.** Fell is asked for the Saturday at half past four and says yes.
7. **397 — Friday the twentieth of August, the sixty-seventh day of the ninety. SEVEN HANDS AT THE FOOT OF A SHEET. PAID.** Between about nine in the morning and about half past two in the afternoon seven masters put a hand at the foot of the sheet in the front room of that shed with an hour against each of them, being a quarter to nine, half past nine, eleven o'clock, twenty past eleven, twenty-five minutes to twelve and half past twelve for six of them, and twenty-five minutes to two for the seventh, who is the master of about thirty-six and cannot read. **The whole sheet is read out to him a third time and he asks for the two names at the top of the first boat to be read again and they are read again and he is not asked why, and he then puts a mark at the foot of it with a pencil that was not sharpened for it, being a cross with one arm longer than the other, and Calder writes the word *mark* against the hand and not the word *signature*.** Every one of the seven was told what was in that sheet and what was not in it before he put anything at the foot of it, and the four blank lines are the four men who said no. At about two the holder goes down to the head of the third lay and names the day out loud in front of about nine men — **Saturday the twenty-first of August, out on the flood at about half past seven, in on the evening's flood at about half past five, seven of them and a sheet between them and a man on the mole head at both ends of it** — and gives the tide as the reason, and the master of about thirty asks him to say the rest of it and he says no, and says he would rather a man be angry with him on a Friday than disappointed on a Monday. The woman of about fifty-eight comes down the front street with her slate and says, in advance, that she is not going to tell one word about a sheet in a boat or a man on a stone to the nine men in her market on Saturday morning, and that she has not done it for that yard.
8. **398 — Saturday the twenty-first of August, the sixty-eighth day of the ninety. THE SENDING, THE ATTACK, AND THE MAN WHO WALKED AWAY. PAID, IN FULL, AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S HINGE.** The seven lie off the point at about a mile at half past six with the sheet folded in the master of about fifty-five's own inside pocket with the seven hands and the seven hours on the outside of the fold. Calder goes out in his own boat of about nineteen tons with the man of about nineteen, past the outer marks at about half past seven, on a breach of the first clause, with no declaration and no paper of that yard's in her. **They do nothing for the first two hours, and that is the work.** At about ten he goes alongside the second of the seven and says out loud in a boat, once, what each boat has and has not got, and that the fifth thing is a man on a mole head at four in the morning and at four in the afternoon who is not on the sheet and not on the leaf and not on a board and not on a list, and that his wage came out of the holder's own figures and not one penny out of the owner of any of their boats, and that it was said on the water so that a man on that water had heard it said. **AT ABOUT TWENTY PAST TEN A TRANSPORT OF ABOUT A HUNDRED AND FORTY TONS WITH ABOUT SIXTY TONS OF FLOUR AND THREE OF HER OWN BOATS IN TOW CAME DOWN THAT REACH ON THE FLOOD, AND THE SMALL BOAT OF ABOUT TWELVE TONS CAME OUT FROM THE DEEP WATER WITH TWO OF HERS, AND THEY CUT HER FORE CABLE WITH A WIRE AND STOVED HER FORE HATCH WITH A MAUL AND PUT A HOLE IN HER GARBOARD WITH A BOAT'S HOOK, AND ABOUT HALF OF WHAT SHE HAD WAS IN THE WATER BY THE TIME SHE WAS INSIDE THE POINT AT ONE O'CLOCK. NOBODY WAS HURT. NOBODY WAS NAMED. NOBODY WAS COUNTED, AND NO FIGURE OF ANYBODY CAME ASHORE WITH HER, AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR HAS LAID A CLAIM FOR ANYTHING.** All seven boats saw it and the only thing that any of them had to make it a record is a sheet of paper with their own names on it, and the master of about fifty-five put his thumb on the fold and said one word out loud and nobody took it down. At about eleven, having said nothing for twenty minutes, the holder puts his own boat across the reach into the middle of the seven and reads **the shape** out loud in a boat — the word, the two columns, the eleven marks against the dates, the two impressions he read neither, and the fourteenth of February cut into the timber — and says that is a shape and not a sheet and that he is not going to say a word about what was in any of those eleven hulls or about any man who was aboard any of them. **THE WORK ON THAT REACH STOPS AT ABOUT ELEVEN AND DOES NOT START AGAIN THAT DAY, THE WAY WORK STOPS, WHICH IS THAT A MAN PUTS A MAUL DOWN AND THEN ELEVEN OTHER MEN PUT THEIRS DOWN OVER ABOUT A QUARTER OF AN HOUR, AND NOT ONE OF THEM WAS BRAVE.** The man with the board under his arm — about thirty-one, a satchel across him, not an officer, a face nobody in that harbor had seen before — steps into the boat's boat of the second of the nine and goes away up the reach at ten knots. **Calder does not ask him, and the master of about forty-one does not go, and the man of about twenty-two does not take the painter out, and the boat's boat is inside the point at about noon and is not seen again that day, and nobody stopped the man and nobody asked him where he was going and nobody thanked him and he is not mentioned again in a room.** "You had him." "I had him." And nothing else is said about it. Fell is paid one hundred and sixty-eight pence at four, and says he was not asked for the Sunday and will not be on here on the Sunday, and says the Thursday is the other, and says he is not going to charge for the two. The seven come in at about half past five on the sixth clause and the sheet goes back into a man's own pocket and no man of that yard says a word about it at any time. **A TENDER OF ABOUT NINETY TONS THAT HAD BEEN AT THE HEAD OF EIGHT BOATS FOR TWENTY-FIVE DAYS WAS NOT THERE, AND A SHIP OF ABOUT SIXTY TONS WITH THE SQUADRON'S OWN BOATS IN COMPANY WENT UP-COAST IN THE NIGHT WITH THE SMALL BOAT OF ABOUT TWELVE TONS IN FRONT OF HER, AND THE MAN WHO HAD THE BOARD WENT WITH HER.** A man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait comes up the quay at ten past six and says what he saw and says he is not here to say what it means and has not come to be thanked. **A SQUADRON HAS LOST A SHIP AND THE MAN WHO HAD IT, AND NOBODY WHO WAS IN A ROOM HAS SAID SO.**
9. **399 — Sunday the twenty-second of August, the sixty-ninth day of the ninety. THE READING, THE ADMISSION, THE QUESTION, AND A THING SAID ONCE. PAID, IN FULL.** A room over the fish market, let out on a Sunday to anybody who wants it, the money in a bowl on the step, no clerk in it and no board on the wall and no list. He reads **eleven dates in the order they were signed** — the eighth of May to the twenty-second of July, ten of them a week apart and the last twelve days after the one before it, and no date moved to make it come out even — and he says four things first, and then reads **the shape after them and not before them**, and gives the reason: if the word had been read first then the word would be what happened in a month and in a year and the eleven hulls would be what was said about it. Eleven hulls, not eleven men, not eleven families, and he does not know who was aboard any of them and will not find out. **THE SLIP OF PAPER DID NOT COME UP THAT STAIR.** At about four in the afternoon, on the flat of the bench stone, with about sixty people on that mole, **HE SAYS IT ONCE, IN HIS OWN VOICE: that he chose the day and knew it was the flood and that nobody made him name it and that he did not ask what else goes down that reach on the flood because he did not want the answer; that a transport came down that reach at about half past ten and had her fore cable cut and her fore hatch stove and a hole put in her garboard, and about half of what she had was in the water by one, and none of that flour is in that harbor and nobody has laid a claim and nobody has been made whole; that two foot of water on a line made by a man who is dead is nobody's arithmetic and is not being put against the flour, and that if it had been his he would be standing there just the same; and that the second seam of that mole is four thousand seven hundred yards long and a mole being long is a thing everybody knows and is not an answer to a boat's fore hatch; and that this harbor is poorer tonight than it was in May and will be poorer in September, and that both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other.** And then he stops, and says he is not going to say it again and is not going to have anybody say it for him and is not going to be told on that mole that he did his best. **HE IS NOT THANKED, NOBODY STANDS WITH HIM, NOBODY PUTS A HAND ON HIM, NOBODY SAYS HE WAS BRAVE, NOBODY SAYS IT WAS NOT HIS FAULT, AND NOBODY SAYS THE PATROL WAS GOING DOWN THAT REACH ANYWAY.** At about half past five a man of about fifty from the office on the west basin says there is a clause in a copy of the terms of the second sitting that is not one of the seven, refuses to hand the paper over because that would be a request, and gives its shape: two named people, one thing out of three, somebody of that office in the room the whole time, an hour that is the end of it and not the middle, and nothing out of the room in any hand; and the third of the three is not on it. **AND AT ABOUT TEN TO SIX THE HOLDER ASKS THE CLERK OF ABOUT SIXTY ONE QUESTION, ONCE, OUT LOUD, IN A ROOM WITH A CLERK IN IT: *If the Navy cannot own the sea by force, is the Crown going to try to own history by making it legally singular?* The clerk says he has not got a book for it, and is not going to say yes or no, and is not going to tell him what the Crown is going to do. Nobody in that harbor has answered it since and nobody anywhere else has answered it either and there is no answer to it on any page of that month.** At about six, on the crown, with the stone bare and neither of them saying one word about it, **the committed relationship begins in a few sentences: he is going to be told before and not after, she is not going to ask, if she does not like it that is what happens and she will not make a scene about it in the shed either, and it is not a rescue and not a reward for a mole, and she has the apology given on the water in July and has not forgiven it and is not going to forgive it tonight, and the forty marks is not what she is standing there for, and the work is not merged and she is not restored and neither of them is paid for the other and nobody in that harbor is going to be told.**
10. **400 — Monday the twenty-third of August, the seventieth day of the ninety. THE LAST PAGE. PAID, IN FULL, AND EVERY ELEMENT OF THE FIXED FINAL IMAGE IS ON ITS FACE.** The sixty-eighth wipe and the seventy-fifth charge, walked on by none, and the top name still off the rota board, and one hundred and sixty pence in the bag, being one mark, short of the wage of four marks by four hundred and eighty pence, being three marks, and **forty-two weeks stood fallen due with no envelope against any of them at the open of the ten days and forty-three stand at the close of them, and the forty-fourth falls on Tuesday the twenty-fourth, which is outside this, and nobody in that harbor has any idea what that yard is going to do about it.** No work was paid for on that Monday and it is said as a fact and not as a fault; Fell is at his own bench on the other end of the garboard that has been open since June and that nobody wanted, and was not asked for it and has not been paid since the Saturday; the man of about fifty-one is on the crown with his page and his stone and is given nothing by anybody. **AT ABOUT TEN PAST FIVE IN THE EVENING, ON THE MOLE HEAD, WITH THE LIGHT OUT AND THE LENS OUT OF IT SINCE THE SEVENTH OF MAY PAST, THE SHIP'S HAND READS THE LEAF BACK IN FULL, ALL FOUR COLUMNS INCLUDING THE EMPTY ONE, IN HER OWN LEFT HAND, AND BOTH DEFINITIONS ARE ON THE FACE OF THE READING: one hundred and thirty-two, five hundred and thirty-seven, none, one hundred and twenty-four at the hour of the reading, and one hundred and thirty-three, five hundred and thirty-nine, none, one hundred and twenty-five at the close, the hundred and twenty-fifth being the last thing in that book and the column not closed.** Then three things on that mole head, none of them asked for: about the water, said by the ship's hand; about the harbor, said by the woman of no office standing four feet off the stone; about that yard, said by the holder. Then at about half past five, **a corridor of the circuit office on that hill, empty, with three doors on it and two open and the third shut, and a paper pinned at the corner of the shut door, not new, not taken down by anybody, naming three people: two as permitted in that room at the hour named, and one as present in it for the whole of it, and under those three lines saying that it is a look at one thing out of three and not a taking, that nothing is to go out of that room in any hand, and that the hour named is the end of it and not the middle of it. The figure on it is a time and a place and an arrival, being ten in the morning on Tuesday the twenty-fourth at that door, and it is the only figure in the whole of that yard's counting that is not a price anybody paid. The third of the three is not on that paper and the claim against it is not withdrawn and no request for it has been made by anybody. At the foot of the paper there is a seal line, and it is not the shape of any other seal line that yard has seen, and the office at the end of it is not one that has ever sent that yard anything: *Sealed and entered at the Morrow circuit office by order of Magister Ilya Serr, Registrar of Recovered Accounts.* NOBODY WAS IN THAT ROOM, HE DID NOT KNOCK, HE DID NOT OPEN THE DOOR AND HE DID NOT GO IN.** The whole standing inventory is entered once and nowhere else in that chapter, and the ninety is at seventy days and there is no seventy-first day.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 400

- **Calder and Mara. THE APOLOGY REMAINS PAID AND UNFORGIVEN AND UNTHANKED, AND THE COMMITTED RELATIONSHIP HAS NOW BEGUN, ONCE, ON THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE ON THE TWENTY-SECOND AT ABOUT SIX, IN A FEW SENTENCES.** It is not a marriage, the marriage is Volume 12's, the work is not merged, she is not restored, and forty marks first after food is neither reduced nor paid at the last page of this volume. She asked one question in that harbor in ten days. **She is not thanked for it and he is not thanked for it, and she says that if either of them starts thanking the other for it she will stop coming up that hill, and it is not the apology and she says so herself, and she has the apology given on the water on the twenty-first of July and has not forgiven it then and has not forgiven it since and is not asking for a second one, and that if he tries to give her one on that mole she will go down that slip.** The yard has entered it in no column and is not going to, and nobody in that harbor is going to be told.
- **Calder and Nessa.** The pair the record stands on, and the last page of the volume is read by her and not by him. **She priced a day out loud before anybody agreed to it at every point where a day was agreed, wrote the master's own words and her own reason against them unjoined, put the fifth answer, which is a person, out of the first column, and on the last page read the four columns back in full and stated both definitions on the face of the reading.** She put her hand on nothing, shut the leaf and put it under her own coat, and neither of them said one word about the figure it gave. Nothing romantic and everything expensive, and on the last page of the volume she is the one who said the thing about the water, and it is about a mark fouled about a foot and seven inches and a ladder in another man's book that nobody has explained.
- **Calder and Alden. DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied from ten until four on all ten days, never approached, nothing on that bench read as a gift, one shoe beside him that is not his and that has been there since the third of May past, and neither brother went near the other at any hour of any of the ten days. NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, NO CONFESSION.
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, **the three nots standing unasked for a sixth week**, third column empty and unappointed on all ten days with his hand at the head of it, and the name beside it not said again and **his surname on no page of these ten chapters.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren. Looked at, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice; lock L27a holds.** On the crown of that mole from ten until four on all ten days, sixty-one, eleven pieces of a boat behind him, a boat's hook in his right hand, and he is not the man on the far bench. **He says nothing at all in these ten days and nobody asks him for anything in any of them, and that is the correct use of him and it is not an improvement on the one sentence he said in Movement 4, which is on the face of Chapter 385 and is not improved on here.**
- **Calder and the wardrobe.** A woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall, her slate and her rule, who told this yard in advance on the Friday what she would not say in her market on the Saturday and who has done nothing for that yard; a man of about fifty in the office on the west basin with two papers, a box no longer empty and a box that is, who told the holder the shape of a clause and refused to hand the paper over; a clerk of about sixty, twenty-two years, owed a quarter, asked nothing and asking nothing until he was asked one question; a chandler of about fifty walked past; a shipwright of about sixty who refused the question; a man of about thirty-two with the dead hose; a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers, who used the sixth clause twice and came on his own account and was not thanked; a master of about thirty-three with no papers on him; a master of about thirty-six of the second lay who cannot read; a master of about thirty of the third lay who says a paper is a list; a master of about fifty-five with a spare warp and a thumb on a fold; a herring skipper of fifty-one with papers of his own; a man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait; a man of about thirty-one of that third lay with a chart in a bag, cited in nothing; a man of about thirty-four of the second lay with a fouling ladder in his own book, not Fisk, not asked; the man of about fifty-one of the six with a page and a stone; the man of about fifty-three who was in a lighter in July and is not on any of these ten days. **NONE OF THE ABOVE IS A WITNESS, A SYMBOL, AN OFFICER, A MEMBER OF ANYTHING OR A COURIER.** And brought in by the last two days and available to Volume 09: **SAUL DRURY, a copying clerk of the circuit office, about forty, named on a paper on a door as the one person who will be present in that room at the hour named**, and nobody in that harbor has seen his face and he is a working man and not a face of anything.

**Line Diver. NO STAGE WAS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH OR IN ANY BATCH OF THIS VOLUME. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED AND WAS NOT TAKEN AGAIN. THE KEELWRIGHT STAGE IS VOLUME 09's AND IS NOT ENTERED, AND THE WORD IS IN NO MOUTH IN ANY CHAPTER OF VOLUME 08. NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH ENTERS AN ECHO, ENTERS A VESSEL, OR SURFACES A PRACTICE TRACE. THE MARK ON THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM WAS NOT USED, NOT LOOKED AT, NOT MEASURED AND NOT NAMED ON ANY DAY OF MOVEMENT 5, EXCEPT IN ONE STATEMENT ON THE LAST PAGE IN WHICH IT IS REPORTED AS UNLOOKED, AND THE USE OF IT REMAINS CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES WITH NO FIFTH AT ANY HOUR OF ANY DAY, AND THE WHOLE FOULING LADDER IS IN ANOTHER MAN'S OWN BOOK AND NOBODY HAS EXPLAINED IT AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE ASKED. NO PERSON OF THAT YARD WAS IN ANY STONE ON ANY DAY OF THIS BATCH.** What he did instead of taking anything was ask eleven masters one at a time, carry a sheet with about thirty men's names on it into company and read a shape out loud in a boat, stop a squadron's work on a reach with his own mouth, say what it cost out loud once on a mole, and walk away from a man with a form in his hand without asking him a single question.

THE MARK FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF IT IS OF A MAKE NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR MAKES. THE SEASON OF BOTH IS NINE MARKS AND NEITHER HAS BEEN PAID AND NEITHER IS GOING TO BE. THE MAN WITH THE BOARD UNDER HIS ARM WENT IN THE BOAT'S BOAT AND WAS NOT STOPPED, WAS NOT ASKED WHERE HE WAS GOING, WAS NOT THANKED AND IS NOT MENTIONED AGAIN IN A ROOM. NOBODY DIED ON THE WATER IN THIS BATCH AND NONE ON THE TWENTY-FIRST, NOBODY WAS NAMED, NOBODY WAS COUNTED, AND NO CASUALTY FIGURE IS ON ANY PAGE. WHAT IS ON THAT REACH IS A LOSS OF FLOUR AND A LOSS OF TIME AND A THING DONE TO A HULL.** Soren Vey's name is on the face of one instrument in Movement 1 and on no other paper in that harbor and in no mouth and in no room and on no mole.
- **ABOUT ELEVEN MASTERS WERE ASKED IN THAT HARBOR ACROSS THESE TEN DAYS, ONE AT A TIME AND IN THE SAME WORDS. SEVEN SAID YES AND FOUR SAID NO, EVERY REFUSAL WITH A REASON GIVEN AND NOT ASKED FOR TWICE, NO NAME AGAINST ANY OF THE FOUR AND NO FIGURE AGAINST ANY OF THE SEVEN, AND THE COST OF THE FOUR IS A MAN'S DAY AND NOT A FIGURE AGAINST HIM. A SINGLE SHEET WENT ROUND SEVEN BOATS WITH A NAME AGAINST EVERY MAN IN THEM AND NO FIGURE AGAINST ANY BOAT, FOUR BLANK LINES THAT STAY BLANK, ONE NAME WRITTEN BY A MASTER BECAUSE THE MAN IS ABOARD, AND ONE MARK MADE WITH A PENCIL THAT WAS NOT SHARPENED FOR IT AND CALLED A MARK. SEVEN BOATS WENT OUT ON A FLOOD AND CAME BACK ON THE SIXTH CLAUSE. SEVEN BOATS ARE SEVEN BOATS AND A FOOT AND NOT A FLEET AND NOT A COMPANY AND NOT A CREW AND NOT THE BEGINNING OF ONE.**

A PAPER ON THE DOOR OF IT IN A CORRIDOR NAMES TWO PEOPLE AS PERMITTED AND ONE AS PRESENT AND GIVES AN HOUR, AND THE THIRD OF THE THREE IS NOT ON THAT PAPER, AND THE MUNICIPAL CLAIM ON THE THIRD IS NOT WITHDRAWN AND NO REQUEST FOR IT HAS BEEN MADE BY ANYBODY.**

AND STANDING WITH THOSE SIX: a page of six names on a mole with a boat as a price and no figure and a stone in one man's own pocket; a municipal claim on one of the three things in the circuit custody room that cannot be taken back without a request nobody in that harbor is going to make; a box in an office on the west basin that is no longer empty, and another box on the other paper that is and that a man of about fifty wants left empty; a municipal paper of the eighteenth of July naming two boats and three men and a tide with a door open four days up that coast and nobody at it; a slip of paper with a figure on it and no name on it in a drawer with a sheet in it, not looked at, not priced, not headed; and a nine-line sheet with a seal on it in the front street of that harbor since the fourteenth of August, which nobody there put up, which nobody has taken down, which nobody there has answered, which names no person and no harbor and puts no figure on it, and which is true enough on the face of it that nobody who reads it can go up the street and say it is a lie. NONE OF THE ABOVE IS PAID, ADVANCED, REDUCED OR IMPROVED ON ANY DAY OF THESE TEN DAYS.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book and paid by this batch: Movement 5 entire and the volume's whole argument, being a convoy of about eleven masters asked one at a time in the same words with a paper between them that names each of them and each of the men aboard, refused by four and carried by seven, every refusal with a reason and no name against it and a man's day as the cost; the eleven weeks of lifts read out in a public room in the order they were signed with the countersigned thing read after them and not before; the attack on a civilian transport carrying flour, which happened because of the hour he chose, and nobody who was in the water says otherwise; him stopping the work on that reach rather than chasing the form, and the man with the form in his hand walking away from it, which is the cost and is not a wound and is not a death; the admission, once, in his own voice, on a mole, in about sixty people's hearing, and not improved on and not comforted; a squadron that has lost a ship out of that reach, reported by a man who was on it and by nobody who was in a room; the inquiry's terms giving two named people a supervised and limited look at one of the three things behind a door with a man standing at it, with the third not on the paper and the claim on it not withdrawn; the new office named once on one seal line at the last page with the word in no mouth and no minister in a room and nobody in a room; the committed relationship begun once and not sealed and not a marriage; the volume's new question asked once in a room with a clerk in it, naming no person, and answered nowhere; the read-back of four columns with both definitions on the face of it; three statements in three voices; the standing inventory once; and the fourth column's hundred and sixteenth through hundred and twenty-fifth lines, one a day, no day in two of them, the hundred and twenty-fifth the last thing in that ledger and the column not closed.**

FOUR THINGS AND A PERSON ARE ON A LEAF AND THE LIST HAS NO MAN ON IT. A CAULKER OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE NAMED ISAAC FELL, WHO HAS BEEN ON A MOLE HEAD STONE AT HALF PAST THREE EVERY MORNING HE CANNOT SLEEP FOR NINE YEARS AND ONCE IN NINE YEARS HAS HAD ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOUR ON IT AT HALF PAST FOUR, WAS PAID ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE, ON TUESDAY THE TENTH IN COIN ON THE FLAT OF THE STONE — AND THAT WAS THE MORNING THAT YARD DID NOT PAY ITS OWN WAGE OF SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, AND FORTY-TWO WEEKS NOW STAND FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE AGAINST ANY OF THEM. THE MONEY CAME OUT OF THAT YARD'S OWN FIGURES AND NOT ONE PENNY OF IT CAME OUT OF THE MAN WITH TWO PAPERS OR OUT OF THE OWNER OF ANY BOAT. SIX MASTERS OF THE THIRD LAY WERE STOPPED AT THE OUTER WATER ON A PAPERS QUESTION BY A SMALL BOAT OF ABOUT TWELVE TONS WITH A LEVER OF NINETEEN AT HER TILLER AND WERE PUT IN ONE AT A TIME: FOUR SAID THEIR PAPERS WERE IN ORDER AND THE FIFTH, THE MASTER OF ABOUT FIFTY-FIVE, SAID SO AND SAT IN HER A QUARTER OF AN HOUR, AND THE SIXTH, A MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE WITH NO PAPERS ON HIM, SAID WHERE THEY WERE AND WAS PUT IN LAST AND HELD. A YARD WITH NO OFFICE AND NO PAPER DID NOT GO OUT AND GAVE TWO REASONS OUT LOUD. A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT WITH A BOAT OF ABOUT THIRTEEN TONS AND NO MUNICIPAL PAPERS OF ANY KIND WENT OUT ON A BREACH OF THE FIRST CLAUSE ON THE NINTH WITH A FOLD OF THE NOTICE IN HIS INSIDE POCKET, TOLD THE FIVE WHAT THE SIXTH LINE SAYS, DID NOT TELL THE SIXTH BECAUSE WHERE THERE ARE NO PAPERS THERE IS NO DOOR, AND CAME BACK IN ON THE SIXTH AND WAS NOT THANKED. THE MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE CAME IN ON THE ELEVENTH ON THE SAME LINE BECAUSE THERE WAS NOBODY AT THE OUTER WATER TO ASK HIM. THE ANSWER IS A FOOT AND NOT A FLEET AND NOBODY'S OWE, LOSS OR GAIN IS PRICED AGAINST IT. A PAGE OF SIX NAMES ON A MOLE WAS SAID BY THREE MEN OF THAT LAY, ABOUT THEIR OWN BOATS AND NOT ABOUT HIM. A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY IN THE OFFICE ON THE WEST BASIN WROTE THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF JULY INTO A BOX IN HIS OWN HAND WITH HIS OWN HOUR AND TOLD THIS YARD SO AND WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION, AND THE FOURTH BOX ON THE OTHER PAPER IS STILL EMPTY AND HE WANTS IT EMPTY. ON THE THIRTEENTH A SMALL BOAT OF ABOUT TWELVE TONS WENT ROUND THE POINT WITH TWO BOATS IN HER AND WENT DOWN-COAST, HAVING ASKED WHERE THE COMPANY OUT OF THAT HARBOR SAILS AND ON WHAT DAY AND BEEN TOLD THE FLOOD, WHICH IS THE ONLY TIDE THAT HARBOR CAN MAKE AND THE ONLY HOUR A LOADED TRANSPORT CAN COME DOWN THAT REACH, AND THE HOLDER SAID HE CHOSE THAT DAY AND KNEW WHAT HE WAS NAMING AND DID NOT ASK WHAT ELSE GOES DOWN A REACH ON THE FLOOD. ### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **381 — Wednesday the fourth of August, the fifty-first day of the ninety. A LIGHTER BROKEN UP IN NINE FOOT AGAINST A WALL, ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN, AND FOUR MEN ASKED ONE QUESTION. PAID.** A lighter of about thirty tons is broken up against that quay's wall in nine foot of water, her frames out by eleven and set along the wall, nothing landed out of her at any hour and no sack and no barrel and no chest in her; the man of about fifty-three who was in her is on the wall at nine, says nothing, and is not said to, and no figure and no claim goes against her. **One hundred and sixty-eight pence comes in, being a day's work with a boat and two men at a berth, and the bag is three hundred and seventy-two pence, being two marks four shillings and fourpence, short of the wage of four marks by two hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark nine shillings.** The holder goes down the third lay at one with a leaf and asks four men one question in the same words four times — what does your boat want before she can lie in company with another boat for a day out and a day back. **A spare warp. A man who can read a clock and not a watch. Somebody awake ashore at the other end at the hour. A hand lead and a line and somebody who can use one.** A shipwright of about sixty refuses the question outright and says that what is wanted is a boat that has been kept and that he does not know how anybody prices being kept. The ship's hand prices two of the three out loud before anybody agrees and says the third cannot be bought at any figure. **THE CONDITION IS ON THE FACE OF IT, IN HIS OWN MOUTH, FROM FOUR ANSWERS: a company of boats is no use at all except in the water somebody is looking after between it and the next tide. The standing inventory is entered in full, once, on this day.**
2. **382 — Thursday the fifth of August, the fifty-second day of the ninety. THE SEVENTIETH CHARGE, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE WITH A CHART IN A BAG WHO IS CITED IN NOTHING. PAID.** The cistern is charged for the seventieth time on a rota day and walked on by none of it and the top name is still off the board. **The man of about thirty-one of the third lay comes up the hill at eleven with a bag in his hand, stands in the doorway, says he is not there to be put on anything and was not sent, and gives the fourth answer: a hand lead, and a lead and a line and somebody who can use one.** The holder refuses to want to know which boats have one, in the same words he gave a man of about thirty-two about a hose in a return on the twenty-sixth of July and about a man's name on a leaf in a drawer on the first of August, and says the fouling man was not asked then and is not going to be asked now. **A man of no office who comes up a hill on his own account and is not written down is not a witness and was not turned into one and may not be cited in a room in this harbor or any other. The holder says no when asked whether he would say so in the room in the front street, and gives the reason: the day anybody in that town asks that question in a room with a clerk in it is the day that man is a person in a matter.** The clerk of about sixty, twenty-two years, owed a quarter, says nothing and is said nothing, and a list on a board in that office binds nobody.
3. **383 — Friday the sixth of August, the fifty-third day of the ninety. A COUNTER WALKED PAST, A BONESETTER'S DOOR, AND THE FIFTH ANSWER, WHICH IS A MAN. PAID.** The chandler's counter is walked past without stopping and no figure is said out loud in that street and the chandler of about fifty is not asked a third time by anybody. **A bonesetter of about fifty at his own doorway looks at the hand of the man of about forty-four from inside it and does not come out, and says he has told that hand what it is twice and is not going to say it a third time to a person who has not asked him.** The holder says the man is not asking him, and that that is why the bonesetter is saying it and not waiting. **The question goes to a fifth man, a master of about forty-one with an anchor over his own stern, and the answer is somebody in this harbor who is there on the day — and it is not written down, and the reason is given out loud: the day a yard writes down who turns up, that yard has a list, and a list is the boat.** The master says he has understood that wrong on purpose and the holder says he has understood it since the twenty-sixth of July and was wrong about it in front of about forty people and is not going to be wrong about it again quietly in a doorway.
4. **384 — Saturday the seventh of August, the fifty-fourth day of the ninety. SIX MASTERS OF THE THIRD LAY TAKEN IN AT THE OUTER WATER ON A PAPERS QUESTION, AND A YARD THAT DID NOT GO OUT. PAID.** A boat of the second lay comes in at two on the sixth clause and a man of about twenty-nine comes up the hill and reports it. **Six masters of the third lay are lying off the point at about a mile and a half with a small boat of about twelve tons alongside the outside one of them, a boat's boat in her, a lever of about nineteen at her tiller, nothing flying and no gun that could be seen at close enough, and no officer seen in her.** She is putting them in one at a time, about half an hour each, and what she is asking is whether their papers are in order. Four hand theirs over and come back in their own boats and say nothing. **The fifth is the master of about fifty-five, who hands his over and sits in her a quarter of an hour.** The sixth is a master of about thirty-three with no papers on him, who says where they are, being a locker in a house in another street, and is put in last and held. **THE HOLDER DOES NOT GO OUT AND GIVES TWO REASONS IN A DOORWAY: this yard has one boat and one man at the tiller and no second such day in the month, and the last time he lay alongside a boat of theirs on a paid day he came off her into a tow of eight and cut his own line and lost a lighter; and a papers question is not a thing a boat can answer, and a boat of this harbor going out with no declaration and no paper of any kind puts this yard's name against a boat of theirs in front of a man of about nineteen with a list.** Six berths on the third lay are empty at five, and the master of about fifty-five will not give his spare warp to that small boat and says why.
5. **385 — Sunday the eighth of August, the fifty-fifth day of the ninety. THE PAGE ON THE MOLE, AND THREE MEN OF THAT LAY, AND ONE TRUE SENTENCE FROM A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE. PAID.** Three men of the third lay come up the crown at four and stand in front of a page of six names and a boat and no figure, and none of them was asked to and none came for it. **The master of about fifty-five says it is a good page and has always said that, and then says he has a board in his own boat of what she wants and what he has not got and what he has got twice of, eleven years old and painted and nearly all gone, and that he has never shown it to a living soul.** The master of about forty-seven says to the water that you cannot read that page, and that he has a list of what he owes in his own head since he was nineteen that nobody on this coast can check a hair of, and that both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other, and that he has had thirty years to want a page of his own and is not going to tell that man he should have. **THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE IS ON THE CROWN THE WHOLE OF IT, SAYS NONE OF IT, AND IS NOT ASKED TO EXPLAIN HIS PAGE.** Tobias Wren, sixty-one, with eleven pieces of a boat behind him and a boat's hook, says one sentence without stopping: the one that was kept was kept by somebody who came on the days he was not needed. Nobody asks which one, it is not written down, and the holder does not improve on it. **And the man of about thirty-eight comes to the door at half past four and says he did not go and look at the line and is not here about the line, and tells them what the sixth clause says and does not ask for anything.**
6. **386 — Monday the ninth of August, the fifty-sixth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-SIXTH WIPE, THE SEVENTY-FIRST CHARGE, A BOAT WITH NO PAPER IN HER, FIVE BOATS IN ON A LINE THAT ASKED THEM NOTHING, AND A CLERK WHO DECIDES BY HIMSELF. PAID.** The wall comes down bare for the sixty-sixth time and goes up at the angle since the twelfth, and the cistern is charged for the seventy-first time and walked on by none. **The man of about thirty-eight goes out past the outer marks at half past seven on a breach of the first clause, alone, with a fold of the notice in his own inside pocket that nobody in that harbor wrote, and lies off the small boat of about twelve tons with his bow on her quarter and holds on to nothing.** He tells a lever of about nineteen that the fifth of the notice is out and the sixth is in and that the sixth has not asked anybody anything since the seventeenth of May; and he says he has no papers and has not had any for four years; and he says the master of about thirty-three has no papers on him and there is no door for him and he is not going to tell him there is one. **The lever goes up his own ladder, brings up his own board, which is the same notice and worn at the folds, reads the sixth line with his thumb on the line and not his finger, and puts six ticks in a list. A tick is not a figure.** Five masters of the third lay come past the outer marks at about half past four under the sixth clause, and nobody in that harbor thanked the man of about thirty-eight and nobody said he had done anything. **And a man of about fifty from the office on the west basin comes up the hill at two and says that the ninth of August is not going into his box because a boat that came in again is not a day, and that he has thought about it and decided it and is not asking whether this yard agrees.** One hundred and sixty-eight pence comes in and the bag is five hundred and forty pence, being three marks five shillings, short of the wage by one hundred pence, being eight shillings and fourpence.
7. **387 — Tuesday the tenth of August, the fifty-seventh day of the ninety. THE FORTY-SECOND WAGE TUESDAY, AND A CAULKER PAID A DAY ON IT. PAID, AND IT IS THE CENTRE OF THE MOVEMENT.** The wage of four marks, being six hundred and forty pence, was not paid and the column did not move and forty-two weeks now stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them. **At about four in the morning Isaac Fell, a caulker of about twenty-three, of no boat, of no crew, of no lay's crew and not on the stone and not one of the six, is standing on the flat of the mole head stone and has been there since half past three.** He says he has been on that stone at half past three every morning he could not sleep for nine years and that there has not been one single morning in nine years when anybody in that harbor was on it at half past four, and that that is not a fault of theirs because there is no morning when anybody in that harbor has anything to be on it at half past four for. **HE SAYS THE FIRST THING ANY PERSON IN THAT HARBOR HAS EVER BEEN ABLE TO TELL IT ABOUT A COMPANY OF BOATS: it is never the warp, and it is always a day when somebody who was going to be there was not there, and the boats do not know.** And that is the fifth thing and it is not a thing: you cannot buy it, bolt it on, find it in a shop in a street, or write it on a board, and the day you do write it on a board is the day a man has a job in that harbor and every other man who was going to be there is somewhere else, and both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other. **Nessa prices the day out loud before anybody agrees to it, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, for eight hours of a man who would otherwise be on a bench of his own, with no line and no fathom and no night's food in it, and it goes in the second column and not the first, with the reason that a man standing on a stone at four in the morning cannot be checked by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil.** It is paid at four in the afternoon in coin on the flat of the stone, and he is not thanked and he is not put on a board, and he says he has been on a board once and would rather be on a day. **A master of about thirty asks whether the holder is going to take a company out on the flood and back on the flood, and the holder says no, and says he will not take a company out on a day when the man whose day it is has not been asked for it by name, and will not take one out on a flood because a flood is the only tide that harbor can make.** The bag is three hundred and seventy-two pence again and the figure short of the wage is two hundred and sixty-eight pence.
8. **388 — Wednesday the eleventh of August, the fifty-eighth day of the ninety. A BOX THAT IS NO LONGER EMPTY, SIX MASTERS ASKED ONE AT A TIME, AND ONE WHO SAID NO. PAID.** **A man of about fifty comes up the hill at eleven and says it is in, being the twenty-seventh of July in the box on his table in his own hand with his own hour against it, written on Monday morning at about nine, and that he wrote what he knows and did not write who was in the boat, and that he had been waiting eleven days to find out whether this yard would ask him anything and had not, and that the other paper on that table has a box in it which is still empty and is the only box in that office he has never once wanted to fill, and he said so out loud in a doorway to one person and it goes no further than that doorway.** The holder says it does not go further and that he will not put it in any column because he could not check a hair of it. At two the holder stands at the counter of the office on the west basin and says nothing, and the clerk of about sixty says nothing to him, and a list on a board there is a list and binds nobody. **At half past three six men of the third lay are asked one at a time, in the same words, what a company of boats out on a flood and back on a flood with a paper between them naming each master and each man would be.** Four say yes in the first hour; the master of about fifty-five says yes and then says the second half of it, that a spare warp in six boats is one spare warp and he would have to buy a second; the master of about thirty, the master of about forty of the second lay, and the master of about forty-one say yes. **THE MASTER OF ABOUT THIRTY-THREE SAYS NO, and gives a reason, and is not asked for it twice, and the no is on the leaf in the same hand and in the same place as the yeses.** Five boats are five boats and five is a foot. **And the master of about thirty-three comes past the outer marks at about half past four on the sixth clause with nothing in his hand, because the small boat of about twelve tons was at the other end of the tow a mile off the point and there was nobody at that harbor's outer water at all, and nobody thanked him and nobody asked him where his papers were, because there was nobody in that harbor who had been asked to ask him.**
9. **389 — Thursday the twelfth of August, the fifty-ninth day of the ninety. THE SEVENTY-SECOND CHARGE, A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-FOUR BACK ON THE WATER AT A TILLER, AND FORTY-FOUR PENCE FOR HIS FOOD. PAID.** The cistern is charged for the seventy-two time and walked on by none. **The man of about forty-four, the second of the six men of that harbor who are ashore with no boat, with the top of two fingers of his left hand gone since the twelfth of July past and the binding off for the first time on the first of August and the hand stiff across the stumps and unable to close on a maul or hold a caulking iron, stands at the tiller of a boat of about twenty-one tons from half past five in the morning until six in the afternoon and is not paid and is not asked to pay, and the terms were said out loud on that quay by the master of about thirty and not by this yard.** He is a boat's man and not a master and is put to a tiller and not to a caulking iron. **He brings the pot back to that shed himself and stands in the doorway with it and says forty-four pence came out of that bag and there is no figure against him, and the holder says it is not a wage and is not against his name and is not going in a return and that there is no return, and says he would not have told him at all if the man had not brought the pot back.** And the man says this yard still has not written his name on a leaf in a drawer, that he asked on the first of August and was refused and has thought about it for eleven days and has come to tell this yard it was right and not to ask again, and the holder says he is going to keep saying no and is not going to thank him for it, and that if there is a day and a boat and a wage one day he is going to come and find him and he is going to say no, and that will be the third time. Forty-four pence goes out and the bag is three hundred and twenty-eight pence, being two marks and eightpence, short of the wage by three hundred and twelve pence, being one mark twelve shillings and eightpence.
10. **390 — Friday the thirteenth of August, the sixtieth day of the ninety. THE SENDING, THE OCCASION, THE TIMING HE CHOSE, A ROUTE OUT HE DOES NOT HAVE, THE SHAPE OF A THING ON A BOARD SAID IN A SHED, THE READ-BACK, AND THE MOLE HEAD. PAID, IN FULL.** **A master of about fifty-five comes up the hill at two and says that a small boat of about twelve tons came round the point at about eleven with two boats in her and went down-coast, and that before she went round the point she came to the six of that harbor on the water and a man in a dinghy asked where the company out of that harbor sails and on what day, and that he told him the flood, and that he did not say the holder's name and nobody said the holder's name, and that he is not taking his yes back, and that he would rather the holder heard it off him than off a sheet.** The holder shuts the shed door, which he does not do, and says the thing: **a flood is the only tide this harbor can make and a flood is the only hour a loaded transport can come down that reach going that way, and he chose the day, and he knew it was the flood when he chose it, and nobody made him name it and he did not ask what else goes down a reach on the flood because he did not ask.** **HE KNOWS A ROUTE OUT AND DOES NOT HAVE IT:** the reach below the foul, a channel in it he has never been down, three soundings off a hand lead in a leaf a stranger could take again, a third channel that is nobody's measurement, a pinger that went up that coast on the Tuesday of the thirteenth and has not come down, and the one thing in the man of about thirty-four's own book that he did not name and was not asked for and is not going to be. The ship's hand says that knowing where a route is and not having it are two different things, and the holder says both of those are true and neither of them cancels the other. **AND IN A SHED HE SAYS WHAT A THING ON A BOARD IS, about a shape and not about a sheet: a board of about a yard wide under a sloping canvas, one word at the head of it in block capitals, being UNSEALED, two ruled columns, eleven marks in the right-hand one from the eighth of May to the twenty-second of July, two impressions at the foot of which he read neither, and a date cut into the timber above the head, being the fourteenth of February, ninety-two days before the notice went up. He has not got the form and has not got a copy and no document of anybody's changed hands on the water. He said it once and is not going to say it again in that shed.** **READ-BACK at four: one hundred and twenty-two, four hundred and eighty-seven, none, one hundred and four; AT CLOSE: one hundred and twenty-three, four hundred and eighty-nine, none, one hundred and fifteen, the hundred and fifteenth the last line in that ledger and the column not closed. Both definitions on the face of the reading.** The woman of no office asks one question and it is the only question asked in that shed that day — will you take them out on it — and he says no, and says that if it comes to it he will not take them out on a flood and will say why on the quay in front of the boats, and that the reason will be the tide and will be true and will not be the whole of the reason, and she says that is a decision and not a finding and the reason against the line is that he knows the hour and is not going to be at it, and he says that is the reason. At ten past five the mole head: the light out, the notice at eighty-eight days, the bellwright not asked for ninety days, the objects four hundred and twenty-eight days, the bench the hundred and ninety-fourth night, the second seam not looked at on any of the ten days, the two lights unmoved in twelve days, seven boats of a tow of eight with about twenty-six tons of flour and no sack ashore and no claim, and a tender at the head of eight boats inside the line for eighteen days that nobody was told anything about.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 390

- **Calder and Mara. THE APOLOGY IS PAID AND IT IS NOT SOFTENED, NOT FORGIVEN, NOT THANKED AND NOT IMPROVED ON BY ANYBODY, AND THE COMMITTED RELATIONSHIP DID NOT BEGIN IN THIS BATCH.** She came up that hill on the fourth and sat on the bench at the back and asked nothing at all, on the eleventh and stood in the doorway and listened to what a man of about fifty said and asked him nothing and asked the holder nothing, and on the thirteenth she was in that shed at four for the reading and asked the only question asked in it, which was whether he would take them out on the day he named. **She asked nothing at all on any of the three days she came up that hill and that is what she has done every time since the twenty-eighth of July, and the yard entered it and improved on nothing.** Forty marks first after food is neither reduced nor paid. **The committed relationship is the last movement's and is not a marriage, and the marriage is Volume 12's, and the work is not merged and she is not restored and forty marks is neither reduced nor paid at the last page of this volume.**
- **Calder and Nessa.** The pair the record stands on, and this batch is the first time in the volume that the asking is a rule and not an incident. **She priced a day of a man out loud before anybody agreed to it, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence, for eight hours of a man who would otherwise be on a bench of his own, with no line and no fathom and no night's food in it, and said the figure is the figure in chalk on the slate at the end stall and is not this yard's figure.** She entered it in the second column with the reason, being that a man standing on a stone at four in the morning cannot be checked by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil. She put the fifth answer, which is a person, out of the first column, and said she was not going to hand him the third list of men. On the thirteenth she said that knowing where a route is and not having it are two different things, and on the third of August she asked whether seven thousand is money, and nothing romantic and everything expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied from ten until four on all ten days, never approached, nothing on that bench read as a gift, one shoe beside him on that bench that is not his and has been there since the third of May past, and neither brother went near the other at any hour of any of the ten days. NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, NO CONFESSION.
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, the three nots standing unasked on all ten days and now for a fifth week with nothing said about them by anybody in that crew, third column empty and unappointed on all ten, his hand at the head of it and the name beside it not said again and **his surname on no page of these ten.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **Looked at, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice; lock L27a holds.** On the crown of that mole ten until four on all ten days, sixty-one, eleven pieces of a boat behind him, a boat's hook in his right hand, and he is not the man on the far bench. **He said one sentence on the eighth of August, to nobody, without stopping, and it was that the one that was kept was kept by somebody who came on the days he was not needed; nobody asked him which one, nobody said anything to him about it, he did not say it again, and it was not written down, and the holder did not improve on it and did not repeat it.** That is the correct use of him and it is the first true thing a man of sixty-one has said in this volume.

- **And brought in by this batch and available to the last movement: ISAAC FELL, a caulker of about twenty-three, of the third lay, of no boat, of no crew and of no office, the person who is there on a Tuesday, who is on a day and a wage and an hour and on nothing else.** And a man of about nineteen at a tiller who read the sixth line of a naval notice off his own board with his thumb and wrote six ticks, and did not say a word to anybody.
