### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **371 — Sunday the twenty-fifth of July, the forty-first day of the ninety. A FIGURE PUT ON A SLATE THAT CANNOT BE TAKEN OFF, AND A MAN WITH TWO PAPERS WHO WANTS TWO BOATS. PAID.** **The woman of about fifty-eight puts the price of a boat and a man for a day on her slate in chalk with the day beside it — one hundred and sixty-eight pence, being one mark and eightpence — and gives the reason herself: three men asked her in one week and she is not saying it a fourth time out loud.** A figure put on a board cannot be taken off again and this one is not going to be, and this yard did not put it there and cannot take it off. The ship's hand prices the day before anybody agrees to it, being eight hours of a man of nineteen, a fathom of line, a night's food for two, and two tides and not one. **A man of about fifty from the office on the west basin comes up at about two and says he wants two boats, three men and a tide out and in under the municipal paper of the eighteenth of July, and that he will sign and pay and it will be in a return before the month is out. HE IS REFUSED, and the reason given is that the three men have not been asked and that a paper which needs a refusal to be true is a paper and not a return. He does not argue. He says one thing on going — that nobody has ever asked him for the fourth box on the other paper, and that it has been empty since the fifth of July — and nobody improves on it.**
2. **372 — Monday the twenty-sixth of July, the forty-second day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-FOURTH WIPE, THE SIXTY-SEVENTH CHARGE, A DEAD HOSE, AND A DAY'S BOAT AGREED ON A BOLLARD. PAID.** A man of about thirty-two with the hose asks this yard to put the fire party's hose in a return of the office on the west basin and is refused, the reason being that a figure against that standpipe is a figure against that man, and a figure against a man in a return of that office follows the man to a hard. **The hose is nobody's and is dead until the spring and no figure is put against it.** A man of the tide gang with a hod says the gang is four short and that the want of four goes in this yard's first column and in no return of any office, because a leaf in a drawer can be read and cannot be answered for. **At about one Calder goes down to the quay and agrees a boat of perhaps eighteen tons and a man in her for a day out and in, at the slate's figure, in coin at the mole head before she sails. The man of nineteen says the same figure without being asked what this yard would pay, says he will not be paid twice for one day by anybody, and says a man who does not ask is a man he will take out for. NOTHING MOVES.**
3. **373 — Tuesday the twenty-seventh of July, the forty-third day of the ninety. THE FORTIETH WAGE TUESDAY, THE WATER, THE BOARD, THE SLIP, TWO FOOT OF WATER, AND A CUT LINE. PAID, THE MOVEMENT.** **One hundred and sixty-eight pence goes out of that yard in coin on the flat of the mole head stone at about a quarter to seven, and the bag is thirty-six pence, being three shillings, and the figure short of the wage of four marks is six hundred and four pence, being three marks and ten shillings and fourpence.** The boat goes out past the line at about eight with no declaration, in breach of the first clause, and no other boat of that harbor goes out and nobody was sent. **At about half past ten, inside the line, up-coast, the tender of about ninety tons is at the head of eight boats, and the outer water is empty, and a young man of about twenty-three is on her roof, and nobody tells him what she is for and he does not ask.** Eight work boats in company, nothing flying, no man-of-war. **A mate of about forty-one refuses him his boat — no room, and he is not on her list, and there is no paper in this harbor that puts him on this boat — and does not report that a boat came alongside.** A man of about twenty-six with a slate asks whether a hull lifted twice is one hull or two and is told no, and puts one stroke down, and says he asked a man in a boat instead of asking nobody. **THE BOARD: about a yard wide under a sloping canvas on an after thwart, one word at the head of it in block capitals — UNSEALED — two ruled columns, eleven marks in the right-hand column against dates from the eighth of May to the twenty-second of July, two impressions struck side by side at the foot, and the fourteenth of February cut into the timber above the head. HE DOES NOT GET THE FORM. HE DOES NOT GET CLOSE ENOUGH TO EITHER IMPRESSION AND DOES NOT ASK. NO DOCUMENT OF ANYBODY'S CHANGES HANDS. **THE ONE THING THAT COMES OFF THAT WATER IN A MAN'S HAND IS THE PIECE OF PAPER, WHICH THE SAME MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-SIX CUT OFF THE BACK OF HIS OWN PAD IN THAT BOAT AT ABOUT NOON, WROTE ON IN PENCIL, AND PUT INTO THE HOLDER'S HAND WITHOUT SAYING WHAT IT WAS AND WAS NOT ASKED, AND NOBODY IN THAT BOAT KNEW IT HAD CHANGED HANDS, AND THE HOLDER DID NOT LOOK AT IT UNTIL THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF JULY.**** The tally hand's own account: *nobody in my boat has taken a thing out of anybody's boat by force. A man in a boat goes alongside and asks the master, and the master gives it, because there is a form with a word at the top of it, and the case goes into a lighter and the lighter goes somewhere, and I have not been told where.* **At about one the mate says four words — *Hold that* — and Calder works the chest of the water for two hours and twenty minutes, half a day's work for four men where there is work for six, and is not paid and is not asked to pay, and is not thanked, and the mate does not report him.** At about ten to five his boat comes up two foot where his book says eleven and she finds nine, and there is a tow of eight boats and about forty feet coming down the fairway on the ebb at five. **HE CUTS HIS OWN STERN LINE. THE TOW TAKES HIS LINE AND NOT THE OTHER WAY ROUND. THE PAINTER PARTS. ELEVEN MINUTES. SIX FOOT.**
4. **374 — Wednesday the twenty-eighth day of July, the forty-fourth day of the ninety. FOUR THINGS SAID OUT LOUD, AND A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT TOLD NOT TO GO AND LOOK. PAID.** He writes the four things on a leaf in his own hand and puts it on the bench for the woman of no office to read where she sat and does not read it out. **The slip of paper goes in the same drawer: about two inches by an inch, seven thousand on it in pencil in a hand that is not the hand on the board, no name on it and nothing else on it.** Nessa reads it and says: if that were money this shed would write it out in pence and in marks and shillings and pence, and it is not written out in any hand on the boat it came off, so it is not a sum of money to a shed that keeps a book — **and it is entered as a slip of paper with a figure on it and no name on it, with no column head and no name, and not paid and not invoiced.** **At about half past ten he says the four things out loud in that shed and does not improve on them and does not offer it against anything, and Mara Venn says nothing about it at all.** A man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers says he means to lie off the point on Saturday and look at the line lying out there; he is told no, and the reason is that a boat of thirteen tons with one man in her and no paper is the first thing any office would put a name to, and the man says he came to tell and not to ask and that he would do it again, and his boat goes out on Saturday and comes in under the sixth clause.
5. **375 — Thursday the twenty-ninth of July, the forty-fifth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-EIGHTH CHARGE, AND A WORD AT THE HEAD OF A COLUMN IN A ROOM OFF THE MARKET. PAID.** He stands in the doorway of the copyist's room and does not go in. **On a fair copy on her desk there is a ruled head, two columns, a clean margin, and at the head of the left-hand column one word — the same word, in a small fair hand, and not in block capitals filled in. A fair copy in a room off a market is made from something somebody sent in, and nobody in that harbor sent anything into that room, and nobody in that harbor keeps a case with a word at the top of it in a market room.** The copyist of about fifty-nine, with twenty-two years in it, moves the sheet half an inch towards the near edge of the desk with her left hand and does not look up. **He wants to know who sends work into that room and who pays for it and is not going to ask, and gives the reason: a copyist who has never been asked what she is copying is the only kind of person in that town who can keep doing it, and the day anybody asks her is the day she is a person in a matter.** The want goes in the second column with the reason that he saw it and did not act on it. **The woman of about fifty-eight tells him, unasked, that there is no flour in that market and none coming, and that she has no figure for it because there is nothing to price.**
6. **376 — Friday the thirtieth of July, the forty-sixth day of the ninety. A MAN OF THE SIX WHO ASKS A SECOND TIME, AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE. PAID.** **He comes down and says he is not going to ask for a page of anything, and asks for a day.** There is no day's work and the bag is thirty-six pence and a second man in that boat could not be paid and could not be told he could not be paid. **And the second reason is worse and is not about money: one of six on a boat and five of six on a stone becomes a word and a figure in a month, and the figure will be in a return and nobody will be able to find out who made it.** The man says *ask me when you have nothing to spend and no boat, and I will take what there is, and if there is nothing there will be nothing and I will not have been promised it.* **He will be asked and is not asked on that day.** He goes up the mole and takes the stone off the corner of his own page and puts it in his pocket, which he had not done before, and nobody on that crown asks him why. A boy of about seventeen brings a word in and is not paid and does not know what it is: a herring skipper of fifty-one wants a day of a man and a boat on Saturday at the slate's figure.
7. **377 — Saturday the thirty-first of July, the forty-seventh day of the ninety. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN, A LIGHTER WITH WATER IN HER, AND THE OIL FIGURE SAID BY THE MAN WHO SELLS IT. PAID.** Nine hours of caulking and painting on a boat of about thirty-one tons by the holder and a man of about twenty-nine with a caulking iron who brought his own bread and his own water out of his own hand. **The herring skipper of fifty-one puts one hundred and sixty-eight pence on the bench stone at about four and the bag is two hundred and four pence again.** He says that if the yard is busy in the autumn he would send work to whoever is not looking for it, and is not asking for anything to be held, and the holder says he will not be busy in the autumn. **At about eleven the chandler of about fifty says the price of a barrel of lamp oil out loud in the road to a man who does not buy — four hundred and fifty pence, being thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, quoted on the first of June, with February's three hundred and seventy-eight pence, being thirty-one shillings and sixpence, left visible above it and both dates on the board — and nobody in that yard says one word to that chandler and he is not asked a third time.** A lighter of about thirty tons is lying at the quay with a foot and four inches of water in her and two tons of wet flour in her bottom, in on the night of the twenty-seventh on her own account. **A man of about fifty-three in her says *that is what happened*, and says he is not going to call it anything else, and asks for nothing and is given nothing. HE IS NOT COMFORTED AND WAS NOT THANKED AND WAS NOT FORGIVEN, BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING TO ASK FOR AND NOBODY ASKED FOR ANYTHING.**
8. **378 — Sunday the first day of August, the forty-eighth day of the ninety. THREE SOUNDINGS OFF A HAND LEAD, ONE OF THEM THAT CANNOT BE CHECKED, AND THE SAME ANSWER GIVEN TWICE. PAID.** **A man of about thirty-four of the second lay, who is not Fisk and who keeps the whole fouling ladder of that harbor in his own book and has never been asked for a copy of it, sounds three places at the edge of the fairway with a hand lead: four foot and no more at the edge of the stone, six foot and three inches a boat's length inside that, eight foot and nine inches at the third place where the lighter went on the twenty-seventh. The first and the third are in the first column because a man with a lead can go and get them again; THE SECOND IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN BECAUSE THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THE PLACES IS IN A MAN'S OWN BOAT LENGTHS AND NOT IN FEET.** He says he will give the whole fairway and will not give the other thing and did not name it, and that if he is asked he will put his book in his pocket and go home, and that the day a harbour asks a man for that figure is the day somebody in an office has decided what the answer is for. **He is not asked and has not been asked.** A man of about forty-four of the six, the top of his left hand out of the binding for the first time since the twelfth of July, asks to have a name put on a leaf in a drawer so that he would be the first asked and not the last, and offers to take a week's wage and says he is not asking for the day on the twelfth of July. **HE IS REFUSED WITH THE SAME REASON AND THE SAME WORDS AS THE HOSE, AGAINST THE YARD'S OWN INTEREST, and the reason is that a list becomes the boat and everybody not on it is not asked and everybody on it has a figure, and the page of six names has said a boat and no figure since the eighth of July and a list would finish it. He says he had known the answer before he came.**
9. **379 — Monday the second day of August, the forty-ninth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-FIFTH WIPE, THE SIXTY-NINTH CHARGE, AND A DAY GOING INTO A MUNICIPAL BOX. PAID, AND IT IS THE COST THE MOVEMENT PAYS BEYOND THE FLOUR.** The man of about fifty says he is going to enter Tuesday the twenty-seventh in the box on his table for days a boat of that harbor has gone out past the line without a declaration, which has been empty since the fifth of July. **He is telling, not asking. Calder asks him nothing, and the reason is given out loud: a question from this yard about a boat would be a request, a request is a claim, and this yard is not entitled to the answer.** The man says he will write what he knows and will not write who was in the boat, because he does not know and has not asked, and says *a person in this town who is not asked anything is a person who cannot be got to answer anything*, and that there is one box in that office he would rather be empty than full. **At about two Calder goes to the office on the west basin and stands at the counter and asks the clerk of about sixty nothing, and the clerk asks him nothing, and they stand there for a minute and a half and say nothing to each other, and the list on that board is a list and is not a schedule and binds nobody and the hose is not on it.** The far bench, Mara, Tobias. At ten past five, **two lights out at about a mile that were not there on Wednesday and have not moved.**
10. **380 — Tuesday the third of August, the fiftieth day of the ninety. THE FORTY-FIRST WAGE TUESDAY, THE READ-BACK WITH BOTH DEFINITIONS, ONE QUESTION ABOUT SEVEN THOUSAND, AND THE HUNDRED AND FIFTH LINE. PAID, IN FULL.** **READ-BACK at four: one hundred and twelve, four hundred and thirty-seven, none, one hundred and four; AT CLOSE: one hundred and thirteen, four hundred and thirty-nine, none, one hundred and five, the hundred and fifth the last line in that book and the column not closed.** The first column's one hundred and three at the close of the twenty-fourth plus ten is one hundred and thirteen, one entry against each of the ten days and not one day in two of them. The second column's run is three hundred and eighty-nine plus five a day, three of the day's entries before the reading and two after it, and the figure is that ledger's own and is not checkable from a mole; the first's one hundred and twelve and the fourth's one hundred and four at the hour ARE checkable by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil, and both definitions are on the face of the reading. **The third column is none on ten consecutive days, nobody has been appointed, the boy's hand at the head of it was not scratched out, the name beside it was said once on the thirteenth of May past and is not said again, HIS SURNAME IS ON NO PAGE, and the three nots of the eighth of June past were not asked about on any of the ten days and there has been a fourth week in which nobody in that crew has said one word about them.** **Mara Venn asks one question and it is the only question asked in that shed that day: *is seven thousand money.* He says he does not know, that nobody on the water said, and that he is not going to guess. She says then it is not money in this shed, and that is a decision and not a finding, and it goes in the second column with the reason that nobody said.** At ten past five the mole head: the light out, the notice at seventy-eight days, the tender's seventeen days at the outer water and eight at the head of the line, two lights at about a mile, the objects at four hundred and eighteen days, the bench bare for the hundred and eighty-fourth night, the second seam not looked at, the bellwright not asked in eighty days with no digit printed.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 380

- **Calder and Mara. THE APOLOGY IS PAID, IN HIS OWN VOICE, IN FRONT OF HER, ONCE, ON THE TWENTY-FIRST OF JULY, AND IT IS NOT SOFTENED, NOT FORGIVEN, NOT THANKED AND NOT IMPROVED ON BY ANYBODY.** She is in that harbor and going nowhere, of no office, not on the crew, not restored, not forgiven, forty marks first after food neither reduced nor paid. **In these ten days she is on the bench at about nine on the twenty-eighth to read a leaf he wrote and does not ask him a question about any part of it, which is what she has been doing for a week and which costs him more than a question would; she is on the bench at about four on the third of August for the reading and for nothing else, being the tenth time she has come up that hill since she came down that coast, being the twenty-second for his leaf, the twenty-third for her answer in writing, the twenty-fourth for the first reading, the twenty-sixth, the twenty-eighth for four things said out loud, the twenty-ninth, the thirty-first, the first of August and this one for the reading.** On the twenty-eighth **she says nothing at all about the four things and the next time she comes up that hill she asks him about a procedure and not about a tow, and nobody in that shed improved on what he said.** On the third of August **she asks the one question of the day and it is about seven thousand, and the answer is that nobody said, and the result is that the slip has a decision against it and not a finding.** **The committed relationship is the last movement's and is not a marriage, and the marriage is Volume 12's, and the work is not merged and she is not restored and forty marks is neither reduced nor paid at the last page of this volume.**
- **Calder and Nessa.** The pair the record stands on. **She priced the day before anybody agreed to it on the twenty-fifth, being eight hours of a man, a fathom of line, a night's food for two and two tides, and she said that if the slate is wrong then the slate is wrong and not the day. She read the slip on the twenty-eighth and said that a figure not written out in pence is not a sum of money to a shed that keeps a book, and entered it with a reason against the line and no column head and no name. She put the fouling man's middle figure in the second column on the first of August because the distance between the places is in his own boat lengths and not in feet.** She is the only person in that yard who is asked to say what a thing costs before anybody agrees to it, and this is the first time in thirty chapters that the asking is on the page as a rule and not as an incident. Nothing romantic, everything expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied from ten until four on all ten days, never approached, nothing on that bench read as a gift, one shoe on that bench beside him that is not his and has been there since the third of May past, and the claim that one shoe is named in this ten days for the first time since Volume 06 IS WITHDRAWN, because no chapter of 371 to 380 names it: it is on the face of `chapter-0360.md:55` and `chapter-0370.md:57` and on no page of this batch, and nobody has moved it and nobody has asked on any of the ten days. **Neither brother went near the other at any hour of any of the ten days, and the yard entered both of them and entered no reason for either.** NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, NO CONFESSION.
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, the three nots standing unasked on all ten days and now for a fourth week with nothing said about them by anybody in that crew, third column empty and unappointed on all ten, his hand at the head of it and the name beside it not said again and **his surname on no page of these ten.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **Looked at, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice; lock L27a holds.** On the crown of that mole ten until four on all ten days, sixty-one, eleven pieces of a boat behind him, a boat's hook in his right hand, and he is not the man on the far bench. **He said nothing in this batch and that is the correct use of him, and in Chapter 380 the two men of sixty-one are on one page again, the one on that far bench from ten until four and the one on the crown of that mole from ten until four with eleven pieces of a boat behind him and a boat's hook in his right hand, and the yard has entered both of them and has entered no reason for either, and neither brother went near the other at any hour of the said day. THE SENTENCE THAT STAGED THEM AS TWO MEN WORKING A CROWN FORTY FEET APART IS `chapter-0370.md:55`, WHICH IS CHAPTER 370'S AND IS NOT CHAPTER 380'S, AND IT IS NOT RESTATED HERE AS CHAPTER 380'S.**
- **Calder and the wardrobe.** A woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall and a slate and a figure that cannot come off; a man of about fifty in the office on the west basin with two papers and a box that has been empty since the fifth of July; a man of about thirty-two with a dead hose; a man of the tide gang with a hod; a man of about forty-one of a pressure house at Ternwatch, hired by the yard for the day and never asked one question about what he does at the outer water; a man of about forty-one in a boat of the line who refused him and then put him to work; a man of about twenty-six with a slate and a pencil; a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons and no papers; a herring skipper of fifty-one with papers of his own; a man of about fifty-one of the six with a page on a mole; a man of about forty-four with two fingers gone and a hand out of the binding; a man of about thirty-four of the second lay with a hand lead and a fouling ladder in his own book, not Fisk; a man of about fifty-three in a lighter; a man of about fifty-six at a teller who said eleven minutes twice; a man of about twenty-nine with a caulking iron; a man of about twenty-eight's neighbour, the copyist of about fifty-nine, the chandler of about fifty, a clerk of about sixty, a boy of about seventeen. **NONE OF THE ABOVE IS A WITNESS, A SYMBOL, AN OFFICER, A MEMBER OF ANYTHING OR A COURIER.**
- **And on the water, unnamed and uncounted and available to nothing: eight work boats in a line, a man at a tiller, a man on a roof with a telescope, and whoever sent the tender to the head of that line on the morning of the twenty-seventh.**

### The power state

**Line Diver. NO STAGE WAS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH AND NONE BEFORE IT. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED AND WAS NOT TAKEN AGAIN. THE KEELWRIGHT STAGE IS VOLUME 09's AND IS NOT ENTERED HERE, AND THE WORD *KEELWRIGHT* IS IN NO MOUTH IN THIS VOLUME. NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH ENTERS AN ECHO, ENTERS A VESSEL, OR SURFACES A PRACTICE TRACE, AND THE MARK ON THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM WAS NOT USED AND WAS NOT LOOKED AT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND NO PERSON OF THAT YARD WAS IN ANY STONE ON ANY OF THEM.** He was in a boat on the water on one of the ten days and on no other, on a paid day, with a man of nineteen who was not asked anything. What he did instead of taking anything was get his hands on eight cases for two hours and twenty minutes and come back with eight fathoms of line gone.

ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE WENT OUT ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH AND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE CAME IN ON SATURDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST, AND NOTHING ELSE CAME IN OR WENT OUT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS. A BOAT WITH A MAN IN HER FOR A DAY IS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE, SO THAT BAG IS A DAY AND A PIECE OF A DAY AGAIN. NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL PAST.**
- **THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS, BEING SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY PENCE, IS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS AND NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, AT THE CLOSE OF THE SAID TENTH, RECOMPUTED FROM THAT CLOSE AND NOT CARRIED FORWARD, AND NOT TO BE PAID, NO WORD UNDER IT. IT WAS SIX HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, BEING THREE MARKS AND TEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, on the twenty-seventh, the twenty-eighth, the twenty-ninth and the thirtieth, being the four days on which the bag was thirty-six pence, being three shillings, and it moved on the thirty-first and did not move after that.**
- **THE WAGE COLUMN AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS, TWENTY ENVELOPES, FORTY-ONE WEEKS FALLEN DUE.** Two wage Tuesdays in the ten, the twenty-seventh for the fortieth week and the third of August for the forty-first, the column unmoved on both.
- **THE WALL BARE TWICE (64th, Monday the twenty-sixth; 65th, Monday the second of August), AND IT WENT UP AT THE ANGLE SINCE THE TWELFTH BOTH TIMES AND NOBODY PUT IT BACK; THE CISTERN CHARGED THREE TIMES AND WALKED ON NONE (67th, Monday the twenty-sixth; 68th, Thursday the twenty-ninth; 69th, Monday the second of August), THE ROTA BEING A MONDAY AND A THURSDAY, THE THIRTIETH BEING A FRIDAY AND THE THIRD OF AUGUST A TUESDAY AND NEITHER BEING A ROTA DAY, AND THE TOP NAME ON THE ROTA BOARD IS STILL OFF IT; THE FAR BENCH OCCUPIED ALL TEN DAYS TEN UNTIL FOUR, NEVER APPROACHED, AND THE HOLDER WAS IN THAT HARBOR ON ALL TEN.**
- **THE LEAF AT CLOSE: ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTEEN, FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE, NONE, ONE HUNDRED AND FIVE; AT READ-BACK: ONE HUNDRED AND TWELVE, FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN, NONE, ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR.** Second column the ledger's own; first and fourth at the hour are counts of entries and of lines and are checkable; both definitions are stated on the face of Chapter 380's reading. **The hundred and fifth line is the last line in that book and the column is not closed.**
- **THE BENCH UNDER THAT PUMP BARE FOR THE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FOURTH NIGHT; THE TWO OBJECTS OF NOBODY'S FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHTEEN DAYS UP THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE, ABOUT NINE FEET APART, TARPAULINS AS THEY WERE, ONE CORNER OFF SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF JUNE PAST AND NOT LASHED BACK, AND ABOUT FOUR FEET FROM A PAGE OF SIX NAMES IN A HAND NOBODY CORRECTED AND ABOUT FOUR FEET FROM A STONE THAT IS NOW IN A MAN'S OWN POCKET. THE SECOND SEAM FOULED ABOUT A FOOT AND SEVEN INCHES ON THE WEATHER SIDE AND NOTHING ON THE OTHER, WHERE IT WAS ON THE NINETEENTH OF MAY, NOT LOOKED AT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, USE CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES WITH NO FIFTH AT ANY HOUR OF ANY DAY, LADDER IN ANOTHER MAN'S BOOK, NOBODY TO EXPLAIN IT, NOT FISK, AND THE MARK FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF IT OF A MAKE NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR MAKES AND ITS SEASON ALSO NINE MARKS, NEITHER PAID AND NEITHER GOING TO BE.**
- **A TENDER OF ABOUT NINETY TONS LAY AT THAT HARBOR'S OUTER WATER FROM THE TENTH TO THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF JULY, SEVENTEEN DAYS, TWO LINES OUT, A LAMP AT HER MASTHEAD FROM THE TWENTIETH, NO OFFICER ASHORE, NO PAPER ASHORE, NOBODY HAILED, AND NOBODY WENT ABOARD HER OR SPOKE TO ANYBODY IN HER; AND ON THE MORNING OF THE TWENTY-SEVENTH SHE WAS AT THE HEAD OF EIGHT BOATS INSIDE THE LINE. THAT IS TWENTY-FIVE DAYS ABOUT THAT WATER AND EIGHT OF THEM INSIDE IT. NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR WAS TOLD WHAT SHE IS FOR AND THIS YARD DID NOT ASK AND IS NOT GOING TO. INSIDE THE LINE AND ON A QUAY SEPARATE FROM HER, A LEVER OF NINETEEN ON A VESSEL OF PERHAPS EIGHTEEN TONS, WHO WAS PAID A DAY'S MONEY IN COIN AT THE MOLE HEAD AND TOLD THAT HE WOULD NOT BE ASKED ONE WORD, AND WHO CARRIED HIM OUT AND BACK AND ASKED HIM NOTHING.**
- **EIGHT BOATS IN A LINE INSIDE THE LINE, CARRYING CASES, AND A TENDER AT THE HEAD OF THEM, AND NO MAN-OF-WAR IN COMPANY AND NOTHING FLYING; ELEVEN MARKS IN A COLUMN ON A BOARD IN ONE OF THEM, WHICH IS ELEVEN HULLS AND IS NOT ELEVEN MEN; A TOW OF EIGHT BOATS AND ABOUT FORTY FEET CARRYING FLOUR, HELD ELEVEN MINUTES ON TUESDAY THE TWENTY-SEVENTH, OF WHICH SEVEN ARE LYING OFF THE POINT AT ABOUT A MILE WITH TWO LIGHTS, FIRST SEEN ON THE EVENING OF SUNDAY THE FIRST OF AUGUST AND NOT THERE ON THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH, AND THEY HAVE NOT MOVED IN TWO DAYS; A LIGHTER OF ABOUT THIRTY TONS AT THAT QUAY WITH A FOOT AND FOUR INCHES OF WATER IN HER AND TWO TONS OF WET FLOUR IN HER BOTTOM, OUT OF WHICH NO SACK HAS COME ASHORE AND NO FIGURE HAS BEEN WRITTEN; AND THE BAG UNCHANGED. A HARBOR POORER ON THE THIRD OF AUGUST THAN ON THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY, AND THE CHEAPEST OIL WENT UP SIX SHILLINGS ON THE FIRST OF JUNE AND DID NOT COME BACK DOWN, AND THE MOLE-HEAD LIGHT IS OUT, ITS LENS OUT SINCE THE SEVENTH OF MAY, AND THE FIGURE OF FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE WAS SAID OUT LOUD IN THE FRONT STREET ON THE THIRTY-FIRST BY THE CHANDLER WHO SELLS IT AND DID NOT MOVE.**
- **SIX MEN OF THAT HARBOR WITH NO BOAT AND NO REPLACEMENT, AND A PAGE OF THEIR OWN ON THE HARBOR'S STONE SAYING A BOAT AND NO FIGURE, THE STONE NOW IN ONE OF THEIR OWN POCKETS. THE SECOND OF THEM IS BACK ON THE WATER AS A BOAT'S MAN AND NOT A MASTER, NOT PAID AND NOT ASKED TO PAY, AND ON THE FIRST OF AUGUST THE TOP OF HIS LEFT HAND CAME OUT OF THE BINDING FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE TWELFTH OF JULY, AND HE ASKED TO HAVE A NAME PUT ON A LEAF IN A DRAWER AND WAS REFUSED WITH THE YARD'S OWN REASON AGAINST THE YARD'S OWN INTEREST. THE OTHER FOUR HAD NOTHING AND WERE NOT TOLD THERE WAS ANYTHING. THE FOUR OF THEM HAVE NOW BETWEEN THEM ASKED FOR WORK TWICE IN A FORTNIGHT AND BEEN REFUSED TWICE FOR FIGURES THAT ARE NOT THEIR FAULTS.**
- **STANDING UNPAID AND UNMOVED: three marks to a man of Ashtide since the eighth of August, unsent for; seven pence to that yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, chest shut, NOT ASKED IN EIGHTY DAYS, no digit printed; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure; forty marks first after food to a person of no office; forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, third column unfilled and unappointed. AND CARRYED FORWARD AND STANDING: a page of six names on a mole with a boat as a price and no figure, and a municipal claim on one of the three things in the circuit custody room that cannot be taken back without a request nobody in that harbor is going to make, and a municipal paper of the eighteenth of July naming two boats and three men and a tide with a door open four days up that coast and nobody at it.**
- **THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY PAST HAS BEEN ON ITS WALL IN A DIFFERENT STREET FOR SEVENTY-EIGHT DAYS AND HAS NOT BEEN TOUCHED AND HAS NOT BEEN COMPARED WITH ANYTHING BY ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR. THE FIFTH CLAUSE IS A BREACH AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE IS FREE, AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE HAS BEEN THE REASON THAT HARBOR IS OPEN SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY, AND IT WAS WRITTEN BY AN OFFICE THAT DID NOT WRITE IT FOR THAT HARBOR, AND A BOAT OF THAT HARBOR WENT OUT ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH ON A BREACH OF THE FIRST CLAUSE AND CAME IN UNDER THE SIXTH.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book and paid by this batch: Movement 3 entire, the volume's midpoint — a Crown convoy of eight work boats and a tender at the head of it inside the line, eleven weeks at about a hull a week under a form, a board with the word *unsealed* at the head of it and eleven marks in a column and the fourteenth of February cut into the timber above the head and two impressions struck side by side at the foot, of which he reads neither; a fair copy of the same word in a small hand with a ruled margin in a room off that market, and nobody in that harbor sent anything into that room; a slip of paper with seven thousand on it and no name on it that is entered as a slip and is not entered as a sum; the absence, stated once and in a man's mouth, that no master in this country has ever been given a form saying what a man outside an officer's company may be asked for; the cost in flour, paid in a lighter of about thirty tons on the ground in about six foot and two tons of wet flour in her bottom and seven boats that have not come in and no sack that has come ashore; the fourth column's ninety-sixth through hundred and fifth lines, one a day, and the hundred and fifth is the last line in that book and the column is not closed; the labour of the ten days on the page, each item on one day and not on two, the harbor authority's list not a schedule, the hose dead, the tide gang four short, the copyist not asked, the chandler's counter not approached, the fouling man not asked, the man of the six not given a wage, the boy of seventeen not written down; and the read-back of four columns with both definitions on its face.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **361 — Thursday the fifteenth of July, the thirty-first day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-FOURTH CHARGE, A PAPER OF TWO LEAVES DOWN THAT COAST IN THE COAL, AND AN INQUIRY IN A CITY. PAID.** The cistern charged and walked on none, the sixty-fourth. **A paper of two leaves comes down in the coal in the inside pocket of an ordinary boat's own boy of about seventeen, who is not paid and does not know what it is and did not ask, the way the sheet of thirteen lines went up it on the Saturday, folded twice and not sealed, with six words on the outside in a hand nobody in that shed knew: *for the holder of that writ*.** It says an inquiry will sit in Veyr in a room off a street behind the fish market there, on terms drawn by the Crown; the terms are seven lines on the second leaf and **no line in them names anybody and no line says what anybody had done or what anybody was to answer for**; a line in the middle says a clerk will sit in a room off the room and write the hour and what was said and that it will be read back and not given out. **The two people on that coast who can be shown the thing the terms are about are the holder of that writ and a woman of no office, and a boat will wait at Ternwatch for three days and will not wait longer.** Calder says he is going, and that a room in Veyr is a room and not anything else, and that he will not stand on a hill and refuse a room he has not seen. She says she will go, and not because it asks, because a thing that can be shown ought to be looked at by somebody who is not being paid by the person who wants it looked at. **He is not answering for her in a shed and nobody improved on either of them.** A man of about fifty-one of the six asks whether there was a day's work and is told there was not. The tide gang is four men short and the reeve's office has nothing on its list, and the list is a list and not a schedule and binds nobody. The hose at the standpipe is dead. Nothing in, nothing out.
2. **362 — Friday the sixteenth of July, the thirty-second day of the ninety. UP THAT COAST ON AN ORDINARY BOAT THAT CARRIES COAL, INTO A ROOM WITH A TABLE AND SIX CHAIRS AND SEVEN LINES UNDER GLASS. PAID.** Not the boat that waits at Ternwatch, because a man asked to a room does not get to send for a boat at a price he has not got. **They come into Veyr from the sea at about two, and nobody meets them and nobody asks their names.** A room off a street behind the fish market, up one flight of stairs, a window onto a yard where a pump stands, a table, six chairs, a bench against the wall, and nothing on the walls but the seven lines under glass. **A man of about fifty keeps the room and not the inquiry, has no title in it and no seal in it, and sits at the end of the table and not at the head of it, with a leaf on the table in front of him with a day and an hour on it. NOBODY ELSE IS IN THE ROOM, NO TITLE IS SAID IN IT, AND NO SEAL LINE IS ON ANY FACE IN IT AT ALL EXCEPT THE TWO LEAVES IN HIS COAT, WHICH HE DID NOT TAKE OUT.** A clerk of about sixty in a room off it, door open, writes the hour and the two names as they gave them and asks nothing and is asked nothing, and the pen goes on after they have stopped speaking. They give their names as they are — the holder of that writ, and a woman of no office — and the clerk does not ask what office she is not of. **THE ROOM PAYS FOR NOTHING AND NOBODY IN IT IS PAID BY ANYBODY**, and they find a lodging behind the market at twelve pence in all, being one shilling, at six pence a night each, out of their own hands and out of nothing in that yard. Nothing in, nothing out.
3. **363 — Saturday the seventeenth of July, the thirty-third day of the ninety. SEVEN LINES READ OUT IN ABOUT SIX MINUTES, AND A FIFTH LINE THAT REQUIRES A MEASURING ORDERED AND NOT DONE. PAID, THE PLATE NOTE, IN ONE INSTRUMENT ONLY.** Standing at the end of the table, not reading as if they were his, not improving on one of them, read once and not twice, because twice is a conversation a man can join. **ONE — the room sits to look at how a harbor on that coast uses its own papers when it sends a boat out and brings one in. TWO — it may write down what it is shown and nothing else. THREE — nobody in the room has a title and nobody will be given one in it. FOUR — the clerk will write the hour and what was said and will read it back and give out nothing. FIVE — the room requires a particular work to be ordered, being a foundation survey of that harbor's own mole where it stands in eleven feet, and the ordering is the whole of what the room does about it, and THE WORK HAS NOT BEEN DONE. SIX — no person in that harbor is to be paid by the person who wants the thing looked at. SEVEN — the room convicts nobody and takes nothing and closes nothing.** There is no eighth line, no schedule, no enclosure and nothing on the back. On the stairs she says one sentence to the stairwell and not to him: *they have ordered it and they have not done it, and nobody in that harbor wants it done.* **THE MEASURING IS NOT REACHED, NOT MEASURED, NOT TOUCHED, NOT ASKED ABOUT AND NOT CLOSED, AND NO PERSON OF THAT YARD WAS IN ANY WATER ON THE SAID DAY AND NONE IN ANY STONE, AND THE ONE PAPER THAT CARRIES IT IS THE TERMS ON THE WALL IN THAT ROOM, AND THAT MOLE'S CROWN AND THAT YARD'S DRAWERS CARRY NOTHING.** Nothing in, nothing out.
4. **364 — Sunday the eighteenth of July, the thirty-fourth day of the ninety. A MUNICIPAL PAPER NAMING TWO BOATS AND THREE MEN ON THE TABLE BESIDE EIGHT LINES, AND THE SIXTH LINE'S DOOR OPEN TO A CIVILIAN CONVOY. PAID, THE SPINE.** **The notice of the seventeenth of May past, copied out in a clerk's hand, all eight lines of it, the fifth and the sixth marked at the side with a stroke of the pen, and nobody reads it out loud.** A municipal paper from the office on the west basin, brought down in a coat by a man off the west quay who was given it to carry and not to read, who carried it to Veyr on the ordinary boat, asked for nothing and was thanked for nothing; it names two boats and three men and a tide, and the name at the foot of it is that of the clerk of that office, being the clerk of about sixty who has been twenty-two years in it and is owed a quarter and has no book and no power. **THE ROOM-KEEPER SAYS THAT ANY PERSON MAY PUT A PAPER IN FRONT OF THE ROOM, THAT THE QUESTION ON THE SECOND ONE WAS WHETHER IT MADE ANY DIFFERENCE TO THE FIRST, THAT THE ROOM WILL ANSWER ONLY WHAT THE LINES SAY, AND THAT THE MAN WHO LEFT THAT PAPER ON THAT TABLE WAS NOT IN THE ROOM AND HAD GIVEN NO NAME AND WOULD NOT BE ASKED FOR ONE IN IT.** Calder: *what the sixth line says is that in is free. It does not say in what. It says in.* Mara Venn: *what the municipal paper says is that two boats under it are a civilian convoy going out together on a tide and coming in on a tide. A civilian convoy under municipal papers is not a vessel returning from beyond the line. The sixth line's door is open to it as well as to the others.* The clerk writes it and reads back the hour and the two sentences and asks nothing. **THE ROOM WRITES THAT THE DOOR IS OPEN TO SUCH A CONVOY WHERE THE PAPERS ARE IN ORDER, THAT WHERE THERE ARE NO PAPERS THERE IS NO DOOR, THAT A PAPER ON A TABLE IS A PAPER ON A TABLE AND NOTHING MORE, AND THAT IT BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT USE IT. IT IS THE FIRST THING ANYBODY HAS COME OUT OF A ROOM WITH THAT IS A DOOR AND NOT A REFUSAL, IT IS A FOOT AND NOT A FLEET, IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT OF ANYBODY'S, IT BINDS NOBODY WHO DOES NOT USE IT, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM SAID ANYBODY WAS IN THE WRONG FOR NOT USING IT.** Neither asked for anything more, because a foot is a foot. Nothing in, nothing out.
5. **365 — Monday the nineteenth of July, the thirty-fifth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-THIRD WIPE AT A DIFFERENT ANGLE, THE SIXTY-FIFTH CHARGE, AND A DEMAND THAT A COST BE SAID OUT LOUD IN A ROOM WITH A CLERK IN IT. PAID.** The wall came down bare for the sixty-third time and went up again at the angle it has been at since the twelfth and nobody put it back. The cistern charged and walked on none, the sixty-fifth, and the top name on the rota board is still off it. **In that room at ten she says it: *then show it what a refusal costs. Not in a shed. Here. In a room with a clerk in it. Say it out loud.*** He looks at her because she had not told him she was going to say it, and because a thing asked for in a room has to be answered in that room or not at all. *I will say it tomorrow. I will not say it today without having thought about it, because a man who says what a thing costs without thinking is a man inventing a figure, and I have no figure.* **She does not argue with the day: *you have no figure. I have no figure and I will not invent one. Say what it is and not what it is worth.*** The man of about fifty says the room will hear it tomorrow at ten, and the clerk writes the hour for tomorrow and asks nothing. In that shed the ship's hand is the only one of the yard in it and puts the wall up and enters the wipe and the charge with the figures and the hours. A man of about forty-four of the six comes past at about two, the seventh day off the water of his nine, with his hand in a sling, and asks for nothing and is asked for nothing and is given water at the door. Nothing in, nothing out.
6. **366 — Tuesday the twentieth of July, the thirty-sixth day of the ninety. THE THIRTY-NINTH WEEK AND A WAGE NOT PAID, AND FOUR THINGS SAID OUT LOUD STANDING IN A ROOM. PAID.** The wage of four marks, being six hundred and forty pence, was not paid, the column did not move, and **thirty-nine weeks now stand fallen due with no envelope against any of them.** He stands, because a thing said out loud in a room is said standing. **ONE — eleven leaves in six hands stay where they are, five of them are her hand, they are not given up and they are not protected, and they can be asked for again. TWO — a sheet of thirteen lines stays with a name and an hour on all thirteen and a price and a payer on eleven and two places and no price and no payer, and no fresh copy on any of its five places because of anything said in this room. THREE — six men with no boat get nothing out of a refusal, one of them had a day's wage and one of them lost two fingers off his left hand and paid five shillings and sixpence, being sixty-six pence, out of his own hand for it, and the other four had nothing and were not told there was anything, and none of that is changed by saying no. FOUR — this room writes down that the door is open to a convoy with papers and binds nobody who does not use it, and nobody in this harbor is paid by the person who wants the thing looked at, and the cheapest oil stays at four hundred and fifty pence, being thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, and the mole-head light stays out.** He sits down. Nobody improves on four things said without improvement. **From the bench, to the room and not to him: *I have no figure for what a refusal costs. I am not inventing one.*** The clerk reads back the hour and the four things and her sentence and asks nothing and the pen stops. **A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE IS IN THAT ROOM AND IS NOT ON THE CREW AND IS NOT RESTORED AND IS NOT FORGIVEN AND HER FORTY MARKS FIRST AFTER FOOD ARE NEITHER REDUCED NOR PAID.** Nothing in, nothing out.
7. **367 — Wednesday the twenty-first day of July, the thirty-seventh day of the ninety. ON THE WATER DOWN THAT COAST, A MAN SAYING HE IS SORRY IN HIS OWN VOICE, IN FRONT OF HER, ONCE. PAID, THE MOVEMENT'S RELATIONSHIP BEAT, AND IT IS NOT SOFTENED.** An ordinary boat that carries coal, sitting amidships where the coal dust is thinnest; the boy who minds the sheets does not know what boat he is minding them for; the master at the tiller asks them nothing, because two people paying nothing for a passage down a coast are not owed a conversation. **At about eleven, with Ternwatch behind them, he turns on the thwart and says it to her and not to a market and not to a room and not to forty people:** that he is sorry he did not ask her; that on the eleventh he said out loud he would hand five leaves over and she told him five of the eleven are her hand and a hand is not a thing; that she told him he had not asked her one question in four days and had been sitting on that bench since the first of May waiting to be asked; that he said he had not asked because he had thought there was nothing she could be asked that was any use, and she said that was the answer to a question she had not asked; **that she was right, and that he owed her an apology before he owed her anything else, and that he is not asking her to forgive it and is not going to improve on it.** **He does not say he had hidden anything to keep her safe. He does not say he had been protecting her. He does not hold the hiding of another year as an excuse, because a hiding in one year is not an excuse for not asking in another.** She looks at him a long time with the water moving under them. **She does not forgive him and she does not thank him.** *I am not forgiving you. I am not thanking you. What I want instead is a procedure.* **THE PROCEDURE, ASKED FOR INSTEAD OF FORGIVENESS: before any paper using her hand is shown in any room, he puts what the room wants it for in writing on a leaf and gives it to her a day before, and she answers in writing or she does not, and there is no asking out loud in a room. It costs him a day and a leaf and the asking, it is entered on the face of that day, AND IT IS NOT A RESOLUTION OF ANYTHING ELSE IN THE BOOK.** They said nothing more about it all the way down that coast, because once said is once. Nothing in, nothing out.
8. **368 — Thursday the twenty-second of July, the thirty-eighth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-SIXTH CHARGE, THE PROCEDURE USED FOR THE FIRST TIME, A MAN BACK ON THE WATER, AND A SKIPPER WITH PAPERS WHO WILL NOT USE THEM FOR A CONVOY. PAID.** The cistern charged and walked on none, the sixty-sixth. **At about nine he takes a leaf out of the drawer and writes on it in his own hand, because the procedure asks for writing and not for talking: what the room in Veyr wrote about a convoy with papers, and that he wants to show one of the five leaves in that room if the room asks for it again, and that he is asking a day before as the procedure says, with the day and the hour. He puts it on the bench in front of her and does not read it out, because there is no asking out loud.** She reads it where she sat and says she has it and that she will answer in writing or not and that tomorrow is soon enough. **He writes it in his own hand and not in hers, because the procedure is his and not hers, and puts nothing against her name on it, and does not ask her whether the day is enough; and he puts the leaf face down on the bench and she turns it back up and neither of them says why.** A man of about forty-four of the six goes back on the water the day after his nine days, as a boat's man and not as a master, not paid and not asked to pay, told the terms before he went and saying he knew them; he comes past the shed at two with a coil of line and says he had been nine days on the stone and had not been asked by anybody to do anything on any of the nine. A shipwright of about sixty says the binding would hold for a boat's work and not for a buoy's; a bonesetter of about fifty looks at it from three paces off, says it is not a bonesetter's work, has not done it and will not touch it; neither asked for anything and neither asked. **A herring skipper of fifty-one with papers of his own says he is not going to use them for a convoy, because his boat goes out alone and comes in alone, AND NOBODY SAID HE WAS WRONG. AND NOBODY IN THAT HARBOR WAS SHOWN TO BE IN THE WRONG FOR NOT USING IT, AND THE ROOM IN VEVR WROTE NOTHING ABOUT HIM AND NOBODY ASKED IT TO.** A chandler of about fifty has his counter shut to one man in the front street, a man comes to it and goes away without arguing, and nobody says anything to him, because a man who has said twice that he has nothing to say has said it twice. Nothing in, nothing out.

PAID.** At about nine she puts a leaf on the bench in her own hand and does not read it out. **The leaf says she has read his leaf of yesterday, that no paper using her hand will be shown in any room on the strength of it this week, and that she will keep the five leaves where they are, and that is the whole of the answer.** He reads it where he sat, puts it in the drawer with the sheet in it, says he has it and that a day waited is a day waited: **the procedure has made him wait a day and write a leaf and not ask out loud, and it has not given him anything.** **SHE DID NOT FORGIVE HIM ON THE LEAF AND SHE DID NOT THANK HIM ON IT, AND WHAT IS ON IT IS A PROCEDURE AND NOT A PARDON, AND NOBODY IN THAT SHED IMPROVED ON IT. HE DID NOT HOLD THE HIDING OF ANOTHER YEAR AS AN EXCUSE AND HE DID NOT SAY HE WAS PROTECTING HER.** The ship's hand prices nothing, because there is nothing to price, and says one sentence about the week: **a door found open in a city has not fed this harbor by one penny and has not brought down the cheapest oil by one penny and has not lit the mole-head light, and that is not a defeat and is not a failure and is a harbor in July.** The cheapest thing in that town is still four hundred and fifty pence with February's three hundred and seventy-eight above it and both dates on the board. A man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons mends a warp and says he has no municipal papers and wants none, and nobody said he was wrong, because a man with no papers is not a man with papers unused. Nothing in, nothing out.

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **351 — Monday the fifth of July, the twenty-first day of the ninety. A SECOND PAPER ON ONE TABLE WITH THE FOURTH BOX NOT FILLED, THE SIXTY-FIRST WIPE, THE SIXTY-FIRST CHARGE WALKED ON, AND A SEALED INSTRUMENT OFF A LIGHTER. PAID.** A man of about fifty puts a second paper on the table in the office off the west basin at a quarter past nine, the man already at that table is a man off the west quay and is not this man, neither spoke, the clerk of about sixty wrote both names in one register. **Garron Fisk, about thirty-four, of a pressure house at Ternwatch, of no office and not a courier and not a servant and not a face of anything, comes ashore off a lighter at ten with the instrument in a wet leather pocket; it goes on the bench with a bulkhead brace against it; Nessa Pike reads it out in about four minutes.** Two seals, one signature — *Magister Ilya Serr, senior Registry examiner* — and *Admiral Soren Vey, fifty-two, of the closed-sea squadron* printed small at the foot, on the face of that one instrument and on no other paper in that harbor. **THE FOUR PRICES: five leaves of the public provenance record, the sheet of forty lines itself with its five places on the outside of the fold, the four copies of that sheet, and a leaf carrying one correction and one date — eleven leaves in six hands in all — AND A LAST PARAGRAPH THAT ASKS FOR A NAME UNDER A SENTENCE.** Calder does not answer it in a shed. He writes the four prices on the back of the leaf in his own hand and puts them in front of the woman of no office, who does not say no and says that a leaf is a thing and a person is a person. Nothing in, nothing out.
2. **352 — Tuesday the sixth of July, the twenty-second day of the ninety, the thirty-seventh week and a wage not paid. A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY-ONE WHO CANNOT READ, AND A RULE THAT STOPS THE YARD ASKING HER. PAID.** The wage column does not move; thirty-seven weeks fallen due. **A stall two in from the end, a paper in a box eleven days old and unopened, and four sentences read to her in a market in about eleven people's hearing and then nothing else, because nobody in that yard is to tell any of them anything and that rule is the yard's own and was made in May after a boy of seventeen carried a word up a hill in front of a woman.** She says it is in her box and she is not taking it to anybody to be got rid of. The sixth of the eleven is a man of about forty-four on a hard whose refusal is the first line on the sheet of forty lines, and he comes and says he has only got the one no. A chandler of about fifty asks a second time to have it recorded that he has nothing to say about it, and it is recorded once, and the yard will not ask him a third time. **THE RULE ON THE FACE OF THE DAY: AN INSTRUMENT THAT WANTS ELEVEN PEOPLE TO SIGN ONE SENTENCE CANNOT BE ANSWERED HONESTLY BY ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR, BECAUSE ONE OF THE ELEVEN CANNOT READ IT AND NOBODY IS PERMITTED TO READ IT TO HER, AND A SIGNATURE OBTAINED FROM A PERSON WHO DOES NOT KNOW WHAT SHE IS SIGNING IS WORSE THAN NO SIGNATURE BECAUSE IT CAN BE PRINTED.** The man of about thirty, two days down that coast, was not sent for. Nothing in, nothing out.
3. **353 — Wednesday the seventh of July, the twenty-third day of the ninety. THE INSTRUMENT READ IN FULL, FOUR PRICES PRICED IN HOURS AND MATERIAL, ONE DAY'S WORK AT THE NORTH BERTH, NINETY-TWO PENCE OF NEW CHAIN. PAID, AND THE MONEY OPENS.** Five leaves valued at two months of one woman; the sheet valued at a drawer with five places on the outside of the fold; four copies valued at twenty-two years of a room off a market, a coal locker four days up the coast, a thwart in this harbor and a coil of line; the corrections leaf valued at a drawer in a shed anybody can walk into for nothing. **THE LAST PARAGRAPH PRICED AT ELEVEN CONVERSATIONS AND ABOUT FORTY DAYS AND ONE OF THEM THAT CANNOT HAPPEN AT ALL, AND NO FIGURE OF MONEY PUT AGAINST IT.** The woman of no office says the last paragraph is the only part anybody will remember in a year and that its being the last line is what makes it an offer and not a demand. The north berth's fouled ground chain comes up with nineteen feet and a shackle that was cut, not parted. One mark and eightpence in, seven shillings and eightpence out.
4. **354 — Thursday the eighth of July, the twenty-fourth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-SECOND CHARGE, SIX NAMES ON A PAGE ON THE MOLE, A BOY WITH A WORD NOBODY WROTE, AND TWENTY-SIX WORDS FROM A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE. PAID.** The cistern charged and walked on, the sixty-second. **A man of about fifty-one of the six puts their six names, the nineteenth of June, twenty minutes to six, off the south end, and the price, being a boat, and no figure, on the back of a reeve's office docket on the dry stone of that mole's crown, in his own hand, in about half an hour, with two spellings nobody in that shed corrected and no copy kept and nobody asked for one.** He is one of the six with no boat. Calder goes up at half past eleven, stands in front of it two minutes, does not put a hand on it, was not asked for it, and says one sentence to nobody: it is on the harbor's stone and not on his wall and he is not going to move it. A boy of about seventeen carries a word ashore off a coal boat, unsigned, off no office's table, about a steamer and a second vessel at Ternwatch and a building with a door that has no glass in it. At ten past four the man of sixty-one on the crown says twenty-six words about a paper on a boat of his in Veyr twenty-six years ago, and is asked nothing and improves on nothing. Nothing in, nothing out.
5. **355 — Friday the ninth of July, the twenty-fifth day of the ninety. A FISH MARKET AT THE END OF THE END STALL, NINE REFUSALS IN NINE WORDS, ONE ANSWER THAT WAS NEITHER, AND A HOLE. PAID.** Four sentences said once, in about forty people's hearing, at the end of the end stall on the woman's own board. **The woman of about fifty-eight holds no copy; she holds a slate, a board and a wall with the notice on it and this yard's own fourth return under one sheet, and her refusal is that a leaf this yard cannot get at has already been read by a person this yard has never met and put up where strangers can stand in front of it, and she has no figure for it and will not put one on her board.** A copyist of about fifty-nine, one hand, one copy, off the wall and not out of the room. A herring skipper of fifty-one. A man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons, whose no went on the slate. The ship's hand, in her own left hand, on a leaf of her own. Two in a market on this coast. **A boat's man of about forty-one of the second lay, in about nine people's hearing, after four questions and ten minutes: he has a boat and a wage of four marks and is on none of the eleven and cannot read the leaf, and he will not put his name under a sentence he has not seen, and it is entered as what it was, neither a refusal nor a yes.** A man of about thirty-six a day up that coast had not answered and his line was empty and was not a hole. In a town four days up that coast nobody answered at all. **The owners of the eleven leaves are about six people in five towns, and the instrument does not say how many subscribing parties it means, and that is the eleventh thing about that leaf that is not on the leaf. Three elevens stand in that harbor in one week — eleven leaves, about eleven who cannot read, eleven conversations — and they are three different numbers and none of them has been confused with another.** Nobody proposed a body. Nothing in, nothing out.
6. **356 — Saturday the tenth of July, the twenty-sixth day of the ninety. A SHEET OF THIRTEEN LINES, THREE RULES AT THE HEAD AND A REASON UNDER THEM, AND A TENDER AT THE OUTER WATER. PAID, THE TURN.** The sheet is one leaf, the back of a docket, the woman of no office's hand, about an hour and a half. **The same three rules as the sheet of forty lines, copied and not improved on. Under the third rule, before the first line, a fourth thing which is not a rule: the price against a line is what the man said he was paying, the payer against a line is the man himself, and where nobody was asked there is a place and no price and no payer and the place is the price of not asking. THIRTEEN LINES, A NAME AND AN HOUR ON ALL THIRTEEN, A PRICE AND A PAYER ON ELEVEN, THE PRICE ON ALL ELEVEN BEING THE WORD *NOTHING* AND THE PAYER BEING THE NAME OF THE MAN WHO GAVE IT, AND TWO LINES WITH A PLACE AND NEITHER — THE MARKET WALL FOUR DAYS UP THAT COAST, AND A TABLE IN A CORRIDOR OF THE MORROW CIRCUIT OFFICE WHERE TWO OF THE THREE THINGS ARE AND WHERE ONE OF THE TWO CANNOT READ AND WHO WAS NOT ASKED AND NO REQUEST WAS MADE.** Line one is his own answer in his own hand and it is four sentences and the last of them is that a thing needing eleven men has ten and a hole. It went up that coast in the coal of an ordinary boat at about two in the afternoon, in the inside pocket of that boat's own boy of about seventeen, who was not paid and did not know what it was. **THIS YARD WROTE TO NONE OF THE FIVE TOWNS AND CHARGED NOBODY FOR ANY PART OF IT.** At half past two a small steam tender of about ninety tons lies at the outer water with two lines out, a young man of about twenty-three in her own wheelhouse with a telescope who came out on the roof twice, and a man of nineteen levering a boat's hook round a bollard who was patient and did not cut it. She came no closer. No officer came ashore, no paper came ashore, nobody hailed anybody. Nothing in, nothing out.
7. **357 — Sunday the eleventh of July, the twenty-seventh day of the ninety. ELEVEN LEAVES READ ONE AT A TIME, A BOY COPYING, AND A WRONG SENTENCE SAID OUT LOUD. PAID.** Four in the shed at four in the afternoon: the holder of that writ, the woman of no office, the ship's hand, and a boy of twenty-two who is not on the stone and has not been since the fifteenth of May and was asked to copy headings and numbers and hours and no prose. **The hand at the head of the third column is his and has been since the fourth of April and was not scratched out; the third column is empty and nobody has been appointed; the name beside his hand was said once on the thirteenth of May past and has not been said since.** The five leaves, in her order, and then the sixth thing that is not a leaf: two months, not in her working hours, nobody has ever paid her for a day of it, and there is a line in that yard's second column for the first of July with a reason and no name, **AND SHE KNOWS WHAT THAT LINE IS AND SAID SO OUT LOUD ON THE ELEVENTH OF JULY IN THAT SHED AND WAS NOT ASKED ONE QUESTION ABOUT IT AND NO NAME WENT ON IT AND NONE IS TO BE PUT THERE BY HER OR BY ANYBODY IN THAT YARD.** The two in the drawer; the sheet not taken out and not read a third time. The six hands and the five places. The corridor: a woman of about seventy and a man of about forty, mother and son, on a bench on a Tuesday and a Friday, a municipal claim on one of the three things, the man cannot read, not asked, nobody sent, no request made, and the claim cannot be taken back without a request. **And at about half past five in the evening he said the wrong thing out loud — *if it came to it I would hand the five over* — and she told him that five of the eleven are her hand and that a hand is not given away by a man standing near the box it is in, and that he has not asked her one question in four days and that she has been sitting on that bench since the first of May waiting to be asked, and he said he had not asked her because he had thought there was nothing she could be asked that was any use, and she said that was the answer to the question she had not asked and that she would not have been thanked for it. HE DID NOT ASK HER. THE APOLOGY IS OWED AND IT IS NOT PAID IN MOVEMENT 1; IT IS PAID IN MOVEMENT 2.** A fire party's hose dead since before the spring, tried and dead. Nothing in, nothing out.
8. **358 — Monday the twelfth of July, the twenty-eighth day of the ninety. THE SIXTY-SECOND WIPE AT A DIFFERENT ANGLE, THE SIXTY-THIRD CHARGE, A BUOY OFF THE FOUL, THREE CHANNELS, AND ONE OF THE SIX ON A WAGE. PAID.** The wall put up at an angle it has not been at since March and nobody put it back. A mooring buoy adrift since the spring, the second of two items on the harbor authority's list, up off the foul from half past ten until three. **A man of about thirty-four of the second lay, who keeps the whole fouling ladder in his own book and is not Fisk and has never been Fisk, asked to be in the boat, was not asked, was not thanked for asking, and came ashore with a borrowed pinger: a pinger puts down two channels and is not reading anything, and there are three, and the third is not fouling, and fouling grows the way the water goes round a thing and this goes the other way, and he did not measure it, did not time it, did not go back and is not going to. NOTHING WAS MEASURED, NO INSTRUMENT WAS LEFT IN THAT WATER, AND THE INSTRUMENT WENT BACK UP THAT COAST ON THE TUESDAY IN THE ORDINARY WAY AND THE MAN IT IS BORROWED FROM HAS NOT BEEN ASKED ABOUT IT AND IS NOT GOING TO BE.** A man of about fifty-one of the six took the whole of the day's wage, one mark and eightpence out of a tin, counted it on a bollard, did not say thank you and was not thanked. **The second of the six, a man of about forty-four, was in that boat on his own account, was not paid, was not asked to pay, and was told the terms before he went out and said he knew them; the other four were not in the boat and were not asked and were not told there was work.** Forty pence out on a shackle and a fathom of line. **THE BAG IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHTPENCE, AND THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE IS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS AND NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHT PENCE, AND THAT IS THE STANDING FIGURE FROM HERE.** A man of about twenty-six with a hod of lime read the notice out to his wife in a kitchen on the Sunday and she asked him what a *breach* was and he said he did not know, and nobody in that harbor said anything to either of them.
9. **359 — Tuesday the thirteenth of July, the twenty-ninth day of the ninety, the thirty-eighth week and a wage not paid. TWO FINGERS OFF A LEFT HAND AND FIVE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE OUT OF HIS OWN HAND, AN ANSWER DOWN THE COAST ROAD, AND NINE WORDS ON A MOLE STEP. PAID.** The column does not move; thirty-eight weeks fallen due. **The man of about forty-four, the second of the six, worked the Monday for nothing and at half past two in the afternoon the shackle of the adrift buoy took the top of two fingers off his left hand; he was not in the water and did not go in; there is no bonesetter on that coast on a Monday afternoon, so a shipwright of about sixty set it at about four with a strip off a leech and a needle in about forty minutes, and a bonesetter of about fifty came on the Saturday, said it was not a bonesetter's work, had not done it and would not touch it; the bill was five shillings and sixpence, being sixty-six pence, out of his own hand, said twice and not a third time, and no part of it came out of that yard and none out of the list of the harbor authority and nothing in that office put it on anything; he is off the water nine days; and the wife of the shipwright said at her door that he is one of about eleven people of that harbor who cannot read the notice, and two people heard it and one of them wrote it down and he was not added to the count because nobody asked.** A man of about thirty-six's no came down the coast road in the coal at about six in the morning: his father wrote the spelling and not him, and a man does not give up his father's book because a piece of paper came ashore in the coal. **The empty line on the sheet of thirteen lines was filled in with his name and the hour, neither of the two lines carrying a place and no price and no payer was touched, and the sheet was not recopied and none of its five places has a fresh copy on it.** A man of about thirty-eight would rather a chart were read out in a market than carried in a bag for nine years, and the man of about thirty-one with the chart has not changed his mind, and neither of them is going to be cited in a room in this volume or any other. At ten past five on the third step from the bottom of that mole a man of about thirty-four of a packet out of Bramble Strait, four days down that coast on his own account, not paid, said nine words about the tender: *she asks at Ternwatch whether a boat has a man in her.* Nothing in, nothing out.
10. **360 — Wednesday the fourteenth of July, the thirtieth day of the ninety. THE READ-BACK WITH BOTH DEFINITIONS ON THE FACE OF IT, THREE STATEMENTS ABOUT THREE THINGS, THE WHOLE STANDING INVENTORY ONCE, AND A TENDER STILL AT THE OUTER WATER. PAID, IN FULL. THE MOVEMENT'S LAST PAGE.** **READ-BACK at four: ninety-two, three hundred and thirty-seven, none, eighty-four; AT CLOSE: ninety-three, three hundred and thirty-nine, none, eighty-five, the eighty-fifth the last thing in that book and the column not closed. Second column the ledger's own and three of the day's entries go in before the reading and two after it, which is a habit of that shed and not a rule and is not checkable from a mole; the first's ninety-two and the fourth's eighty-four at the hour are counts of entries and of lines and are checkable by a stranger with a leaf and a pencil; and both definitions are printed on the face of the reading.** Three counts on the face: TWO wipes (61st, 62nd), THREE charges walked on none (61st, 62nd, 63rd), TWO wage Tuesdays (37th, 38th weeks), THIRTY-EIGHT WEEKS FALLEN DUE. MONEY: 0 + 168 + 168 − 132 = 204. Three statements about three things; the mole head at ten past five; the whole standing inventory once and nowhere else; the tender of about ninety tons still at the outer water with a lamp at her masthead; the two objects of nobody's at 398 days and about four feet from a page of six names; the second seam a foot and seven inches where it was on the nineteenth of May and not looked at. **THE THIRTIETH DAY OF THE NINETY, the yard having taken the figure of ninety on the fifteenth day of June, being the day six men were told to stand by. And the volume's new question was not asked on any of the ten days and is not asked at the mole head and no body and no committee and no assembly and no fleet and no wing and no guard was proposed by anybody in that harbor, and the naming of them is a naming of a kind and a kind is not a thing anybody here has got.** Nothing in, nothing out.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 360

- **Calder and Mara.** **THE APOLOGY IS OWED AND IS NOT PAID.** On the twenty-fifth of June he asked eleven men who had boats and did not ask six who had not got one, and he said so on his own feet and was not comforted. On the seventh of July he read four prices to a woman of sixty-one in a market and did not ask her one question because of a rule he made himself. On the eleventh he said out loud that if it came to it he would hand five leaves over, and she told him that five of the eleven are her hand and that a hand is not a thing and cannot be handed over, and that he has not asked her one question in four days and that she has been sitting on that bench since the first of May waiting to be asked. He said he had not asked her because he had thought there was nothing she could be asked that was any use, and she said that was the answer to the question she had not asked and that she would not have been thanked for it. **HE DID NOT ASK HER AND HE IS ENTERED AS HAVING SAID IT AND NOTHING IS PUT UNDER IT.** She is in that harbor and goes nowhere, of no office, not on the crew, not restored, not forgiven, forty marks first after food neither reduced nor paid, and she came up that hill ten times this month for readings and for nothing else. Not resolved, and not to be resolved in this movement.
- **Calder and Nessa.** The pair the record stands on. She read the instrument out in full in about four minutes in her left hand, she priced all four things in hours and material before anybody was asked anything, she wrote the sheet of forty lines into a drawer, and she filled in the one empty line on the sheet of thirteen lines and touched neither of the two blanks. **The first of the six hands, the woman's, being five leaves, is not hers, and the hand beside hers, the sheet and the corrections leaf, is.** Nothing romantic, everything expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on all ten days ten until four, never approached, nothing on the bench read as a gift, one shoe on that bench beside him that is not his and has been there since the third of May past. Neither brother said why. **NO FRAGMENT, NO REPORT TALK, NO SECOND STORY, NO CONFESSION IN THIS BATCH. THE PARTIAL CONFESSION IS VOLUME 09'S AND THE ORIGINAL REPAIR LOG IS VOLUME 15'S.** **The far-bench man is not in this yard's book at all and the man on the crown of that mole is not him.**
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, the three nots standing unasked on all ten days, third column unfilled and unappointed, his hand at the head of it and the name beside it not said again. **HE WAS IN THAT SHED ON THE ELEVENTH OF JULY AND WAS ASKED TO COPY HEADINGS AND NUMBERS AND HOURS AND NO PROSE, AND THAT WAS SAID OUT LOUD, AND HE WAS NOT PUT ON THE STONE AND WAS NOT PAID AND WAS NOT ASKED FOR ANYTHING.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **Looked at, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice; lock L27a holds.** On the crown of that mole ten until four on all ten days and on it again at ten past five, with a boat's hook in his **right** hand, the bandaging having come off after the second of June, and eleven pieces of a boat behind him. **He said twenty-six words on the eighth of July about a paper on a boat of his at Veyr twenty-six years ago, and the paper was for leaving and the boat went on being theirs about two years after the paper came off her and he never found out by what right and did not ask, because he was thirty-five and wanted the winter's work. IT WAS SAID OUT LOUD, NOT TO HIM, IT WAS NOT IMPROVED ON BY ANYBODY, HE WAS NOT ASKED A SECOND QUESTION, AND HE IS NOT A TEACHER AND NOT A DOOR AND NOT THIS YARD'S INJURY.** **HE IS NOT ALDEN MARR, IS NOT THE MAN AT THE FAR BENCH, AND THE TWO ARE NOT ONE MAN, AND THE ONE PLACE IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS WHERE THE TWO MEN OF SIXTY-ONE STAND IN ONE SENTENCE IS CHAPTER 360'S APPARATUS AND IT IS AN ASSERTION THAT THEY ARE TWO.**
- **Calder and the wardrobe.** Garrow Fisk of about thirty-four, of a pressure house at Ternwatch, who carried a paper he did not want, said one sentence at the top of the south-end steps and went down them, and is not a courier, not a servant, not a villain, not a teacher and not a face of anything, and was shown nothing of the last paragraph; a man of about fifty with two papers on one table and the fourth box not filled; a man of about forty-four on a hard whose refusal is the first line on the sheet of forty lines and who says he has only got the one no; a man of about thirty-one of the third lay with a chart in a bag for nine years; a man of about thirty-eight with a boat of about thirteen tons who has said three sentences in that market in a month and said a fourth on the third of July and would not give a name, and who on the ninth of July said one more thing about a chart and not in a market; a man of about thirty-four of the second lay who keeps the whole fouling ladder in his own book, is not Fisk, and who found a third channel with a borrowed instrument and measured nothing; a woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall and her slate and her rule and a quart of something priced on her board with the date on it; a copyist of about fifty-nine with one hand on one copy, off the wall and not out of the room; a herring skipper of fifty-one with a hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November past; a man of about thirty-six with a coaster of about thirty tons and eleven weeks of a season and his father's book in his house and a coal locker four days up this coast; a man of about twenty-six with a hod of lime who read a notice to his wife in a kitchen; a man of about forty-one of the second lay with a boat and a wage of four marks and no figure of his own in any of it; a woman of about sixty-one with a paper in a box eleven days old; a woman of about seventy and a man of about forty on a bench in a corridor; a young man of about twenty-three in a wheelhouse with a telescope; a man of nineteen at a wheel with a boat's hook; a man of about thirty-four of a packet out of Bramble Strait; a boy of about seventeen with a word in his pocket; a shipwright of about sixty; a bonesetter of about fifty; a chandler of about fifty; a clerk of about sixty; and a girl of about nineteen at the steps of the pilot's house.

### The power state

**Line Diver. NO STAGE TAKEN IN THIS BATCH AND NONE BEFORE IT. THE FAULTREADER STAGE IS SPENT AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE IS NOT IMPROVED AND WAS NOT TAKEN AGAIN. THE KEELWRIGHT STAGE IS VOLUME 09'S AND IS NOT ENTERED HERE, AND THE WORD *KEELWRIGHT* IS IN NO MOUTH IN THIS VOLUME. NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH ENTERS AN ECHO, ENTERS A VESSEL, OR SURFACES A PRACTICE TRACE. The third channel on a borrowed pinger is an instrument reading and not a discovery: a pinger counts what the iron on the other side of a hull is doing to a note, it is not reading anything, a man with it on the wrong side of a plate gets a figure and not a truth, and nothing was measured, nothing was left in the water, and the instrument went back up that coast on the Tuesday in the ordinary way and nobody asked the man it is borrowed from about it.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE BAG IS TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE, BEING ONE MARK AND THREE SHILLINGS AND EIGHT PENCE. 0 + 168 + 168 − 92 − 40 = 204. ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN ON WEDNESDAY THE SEVENTH, BEING A DAY'S WORK WITH A BOAT AND TWO MEN AT THE NORTH BERTH; NINETY-TWO PENCE OUT THE SAME DAY, BEING NINE FEET TWELVE INCHES OF NEW STUD CHAIN; ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE IN ON MONDAY THE TWELFTH, BEING A DAY'S WORK OFF THE FOUL; FORTY PENCE OUT THE SAME DAY, BEING A SHACKLE AND A FATHOM OF LINE. NOTHING ELSE MOVED IN TEN DAYS. A BOAT WITH A MAN IN HER FOR A DAY IS ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT PENCE, SO THAT BAG IS A DAY AND A PIECE OF A DAY, AND IT IS THE MOST MONEY THAT HAS BEEN IN THAT BAG SINCE THE EIGHTEENTH DAY OF MAY PAST. NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL PAST.**
- **THE FIGURE SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS IS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS AND NINE SHILLINGS AND EIGHT PENCE**, not to be paid, no word under it. It was five hundred and sixty-four pence, being three marks and seven shillings, from the seventh to the twelfth of July.
- **THE WAGE COLUMN AT TWENTY-SIX LINES AND ONE HUNDRED AND FOUR MARKS, TWENTY ENVELOPES, THIRTY-EIGHT WEEKS FALLEN DUE.** Two wage Tuesdays in the ten, the sixth and the thirteenth, column unmoved on both; the next falls due on Tuesday the twentieth of July, being the thirty-ninth week, outside the batch.
