- **THE LEAF AT CLOSE: NINETY-THREE, THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE, NONE, EIGHTY-FIVE; AT READ-BACK: NINETY-TWO, THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN, NONE, EIGHTY-FOUR.** Second column the ledger's own; first and fourth at the hour are counts of entries and of lines and are checkable; both definitions are stated on the face of Chapter 360's reading. The fourth column's eighty-fifth is the last thing in that book and the column is not closed.
- **THE BENCH UNDER THAT PUMP BARE FOR THE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-FOURTH NIGHT; THE TWO OBJECTS OF NOBODY'S THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-EIGHT DAYS UP THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE, ABOUT NINE FEET APART, TARPAULINS AS THEY WERE, ONE CORNER OFF SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF JUNE PAST AND NOT LASHED BACK, AND ABOUT FOUR FEET FROM A PAGE OF SIX NAMES IN A HAND NOBODY CORRECTED. THE SECOND SEAM FOULED ABOUT A FOOT AND SEVEN INCHES ON THE WEATHER SIDE AND NOTHING ON THE OTHER, WHERE IT WAS ON THE NINETEENTH OF MAY, NOT LOOKED AT ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS, USE CLOSED AT FOUR FIGURES WITH NO FIFTH AT ANY HOUR OF ANY DAY, LADDER IN ANOTHER MAN'S BOOK, NOBODY TO EXPLAIN IT, NOT FISK.**
- **A TENDER OF ABOUT NINETY TONS AT THE OUTER WATER FROM THE TENTH TO THE FOURTEENTH OF JULY, OUTSIDE THE LINE, TWO LINES OUT, A YOUNG MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-THREE IN HER OWN WHEELHOUSE WITH A TELESCOPE, A LEVER OF NINETEEN ON A VESSEL OF PERHAPS EIGHTEEN TONS PATIENT WITH A BIGHT OF LINE AND NOT CUTTING IT, NO OFFICER ASHORE, NO PAPER ASHORE, NOBODY HAILED, A GIRL OF ABOUT NINETEEN SAYING SHE HAS HAD TWO STEAMERS ALONGSIDE HER AT TERNWATCH FOR FOUR DAYS AND CAME NINETY MILES ON A TIDE, AND NININE WORDS ON A MOLE STEP ABOUT WHAT SHE DOES.**
- **SIX MEN OF THAT HARBOR WITH NO BOAT AND NO REPLACEMENT, AND A PAGE OF THEIR OWN ON THE HARBOR'S STONE SAYING A BOAT AND NO FIGURE; ONE OF THEM TOOK A DAY'S WAGE ON THE TWELFTH, AND THE OTHER OF THOSE TWO WORKED THAT DAY FOR NOTHING AND LOST THE TOP OF TWO FINGERS OF HIS LEFT HAND AND PAID FIVE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE FOR IT OUT OF HIS OWN HAND AND IS OFF THE WATER NINE DAYS; AND THE OTHER FOUR HAD NOTHING AND WERE NOT TOLD THERE WAS ANYTHING. A HARBOR POORER ON THE FOURTEENTH OF JULY THAN ON THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY, AND THE CHEAPEST OIL WENT UP SIX SHILLINGS ON THE FIRST OF JUNE AND DID NOT COME BACK DOWN, AND THE MOLE-HEAD LIGHT IS OUT.**
- **STANDING UNPAID AND UNMOVED: three marks to Ashtide since the eighth of August, unsent for; seven pence to the yard's own shipwright; eight marks and a day of a boat to the bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, chest shut, not asked in sixty days, no digit printed; eight shillings and tenpence to a woman with her name on the figure; forty marks first after food to a person of no office; forty marks whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, third column unfilled. And NEW IN THIS BATCH AND STANDING: a page of six names on a mole with a boat as a price and no figure, and a municipal claim on one of the three things in the circuit custody room that cannot be taken back without a request nobody in that harbor is going to make.**
- **THE NOTICE OF THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY PAST HAS BEEN ON ITS WALL IN A DIFFERENT STREET FOR FIFTY-EIGHT DAYS AND HAS NOT BEEN TOUCHED, HAS NOT BEEN COMPARED WITH ANYTHING BY ANYBODY IN THAT HARBOR, AND HAS NOT BEEN COMPARED WITH THE PAGE ON THE MOLE. THE FIFTH CLAUSE IS A BREACH AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE IS FREE, AND THE SIXTH CLAUSE HAS BEEN THE REASON THAT HARBOR IS OPEN SINCE THE SEVENTEENTH OF MAY, AND IT WAS WRITTEN BY AN OFFICE THAT DID NOT WRITE IT FOR THAT HARBOR. THE TWO OLDER NAVAL NOTICES FURTHER ALONG THE SAME WALL ARE STILL ON IT.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book and paid by this batch: Movement 1 entire — a sealed instrument with two seals and one signature and four named prices and a fifth thing that is not a thing; the four prices priced in hours and material before anybody was asked anything; the refusal of the eleven leaves by their six holders in five towns and one market, nine of them out loud in nine words of their own, and one answer that was neither a refusal nor a yes and is entered as what it was; a woman of about sixty-one who cannot read and whom a rule forbids this yard to ask, and the sentence on the face of the day that an instrument wanting eleven signatures has ten and a hole; a sheet of thirteen lines with the same three rules at the head of it, a name and an hour on all thirteen, a price and a payer on eleven with the price on all eleven being the word *nothing*, and two places and no price and no payer with the reason printed above the first line; the sheet carried up a coast in the coal of an ordinary boat by a boy of seventeen who was not paid and did not know what it was; this yard's own written refusal to write to any of the five towns; a man of fifty-one's six names on a page on the harbor's own stone in a hand nobody corrected with two spellings nobody fixed and no figure; a tender of about ninety tons at the outer water for five days and no officer and no paper and no hail; a third channel on a borrowed instrument and nothing measured; two days of paid work after two months of none, one mark and eightpence a day, and a bag that is one mark and three shillings and eightpence and is a day and a piece of a day; two fingers off a working man's hand who worked the day for nothing, a shipwright's forty minutes with a strip off a leech, a bonesetter who would not touch it, five shillings and sixpence out of his own hand said twice, and nine days off the water; a wrong sentence said out loud in a shed about handing over a hand, and the correction, and the two people not asking each other a question; and the read-back of four columns with both definitions on its face and the whole standing inventory once.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **341 — Friday the twenty-fifth of June. THE ELEVENTH DAY OF THE NINETY, ELEVEN MEN ASKED ONE QUESTION IN ELEVEN ROOMS, TEN YES AND ONE NO, AND ONE OF THE TEN SAID YES AND THEN NO AND THEN YES AGAIN WITH ALL THREE HOURS ON A SHEET. PAID.** The two prices named out loud to every man before he was asked: the soundings are of a coast that has moved, no figure for how far; the Ternwatch road, about eleven tons to a lighter for the season. Eleven men, each with one trade and one boat, named on the page for the first time: Elias Voke of the *Anna Ray*, Iver Sallow of the *Ashtide Rose*, Roy Kettle of a coaster of about thirty tons, Peder Lund of about thirteen tons, Ivor Pride of about forty-five tons, Alban Pree of about thirty tons, Tam Rundle of the packet *Mary Rend*, Jens Ower of a lighter of about eleven tons, Adam Slee of about twenty-six tons. Josiah Mear of about twenty-four tons said no, in the same words as in May, and his refusal was carried on to the sheet. Hamo Birt said yes at eleven, no at four, both hours. Calder tells a woman of no office in plain words, and she does not come, and asks for it in a book a stranger can pick up. Nothing in, nothing out.
2. **342 — Saturday the twenty-sixth. THE REFUSAL ENTERED FIRST, THREE RULES AT THE HEAD OF THE SHEET, FOUR COPIES, TEN BOATS OFF AT HALF PAST SEVEN, AND NOBODY HAILED. PAID.** Mear's no at about ten on the front street with his own name, his own hour and his own reason, first on the sheet, at his asking. The three rules: a decision goes on at the moment a man says it; a man may take it back and both go on; it stops when somebody says it stops and not one line after. Four sheets ruled on the back out of the drawer and the five places written on the outside of the fold, one of them a market wall in a town four days up that coast. Birt comes alongside at eight and says yes again. Eleven boats let go on the flood at half past seven and pass the mole head and the fifth-clause line without a declaration. A boat of the squadron at the outer marks with one man and a book; he does not hail. Nothing in, nothing out.
3. **343 — Sunday the twenty-seventh. THE THIRTEENTH DAY OF THE NINETY, THE NIGHT, THE STRAIT, TWO FOOT, TWO FINGERS, AND A SHEET THAT STOPPED AT FOUR O'CLOCK. PAID, THE CLIMAX.** The eleven spellings read out on the water with the year against each; no page says which is right and none supplied; a line on a page is a thing a person left and the person is not out there. Lund's boat finds two foot more on the oldest page than that page carries and goes on. Coll Mabry, forty-five, third lay, loses two fingers of his left hand off a warp at one in the morning, and says on the water that he has a girl of eleven and asks for the hour to be against it; no bonesetter on that coast at that hour; bound with a strip off a leech. The *Anna Ray* takes three women in. In at half past five under the sixth clause. Nothing in, nothing out.
4. **344 — Monday the twenty-eighth. THE SIXTIETH WIPE, THE FIFTY-NINTH CHARGE, THE LANDING, AND A COPY GOING UP THAT COAST FOR COAL. PAID.** The wall bare for the sixtieth time, counter not restarting, no sitting; the cistern charged and walked on none, the fifty-ninth. Four boxes of physic given away in the market before eleven by the woman of about fifty-eight, who refused money twice in the same words; about four tons of flour in a shed with a slate and no name; about eleven tons of oil in a lighter a ton light; three women of about sixty-two, fifty-eight and fifty-five off a crossing, one sentence each, no second question. A man of about fifty-one of the six watches ten boats land and says three sentences, and the third is that four ton of flour is worth nothing at all to him, and that he is going to lose a berth on the Monday and has no figure for what a berth is worth. Four copies written out in four hands; one goes up the coast in the coal of an ordinary boat; nobody was charged for it. Nothing in, nothing out.
5. **345 — Tuesday the twenty-ninth. THE THIRTY-SIXTH WEEK, A COLUMN THAT DID NOT MOVE, AND A MAN ON HIS OWN FEET IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING. PAID, THE ACCEPTANCE.** A wage Tuesday, four marks not paid, **thirty-six weeks fallen due**. Calder stands on the floor of that fish market on his own feet and says once, and is not asked about it and it is not improved on: that he asked eleven men who had boats and did not ask six men who had not got one, and that the choice is his, and that he is not going to say it was the right thing, and that the eleven were in a position and the six were not and a man is not brave for being in a position. **Not comforted by anybody; about a minute and three-quarters in which anybody said anything to him.** The sentence of the twenty-third is not re-said. Nobody proposed anything; the man of about thirty-eight stood at the end of the aisle for forty minutes and said nothing. Nothing in, nothing out.
6. **346 — Wednesday the thirtieth. THE SHEET READ BACK IN FULL, FORTY LINES, ONE DISPUTE, AND SIX THINGS THAT ARE NOT ON IT. PAID.** The rule of the first of May read out first. All forty lines read aloud with the head and the places of the copies. One correction, at the asking of the man whose name is on it: a price entered as *nothing* entered as one hundred and eight pence, being a slip at three shillings a week for three weeks, and the wrong figure is not scratched out. A man of about thirty-four of that harbor's own second lay says one sentence from the back of the shed and is asked nothing. **Six things happened after four o'clock in the morning and are not on the sheet and were not written on it, because a rule bent the first time it is inconvenient is not a rule.** Nothing in, nothing out.
7. **347 — Thursday the first of July. THE SIXTIETH CHARGE, THE STAGE AS A TRADE, AND A DAY LOST. PAID.** The cistern charged and walked on none, the sixtieth. The Storm-Reader stage entered in the first column with the whole of its cost and what it is not for: a trade and not a power, a thing four people did together on a night that stopped when they stopped, the soundings of a coast that has moved, a line on a page commanding nothing, a seam identifying difference and not truth, the mark of the second seam not looked at and its use closed at four figures, **its season still nine marks and not paid**, the faultreader stage spent, the bellwright stage not improved. A woman of no office makes him say what a power is and what a trade is and he says both. **AND A DAY WAS LOST: he set himself a day of ordinary work and did not do it, and the reason against the line is that he was not able to, and no name is in it, and a lost day carries no figure, and the ship's hand says out loud that no name is to be put there by her and that it is not a stage.** Nothing in, nothing out.
8. **348 — Friday the second of July. THE OIL, THE FIGURE THAT DID NOT MOVE, A WORD DOWN A COAST ROAD, AND A HARBOR POORER. PAID.** Eleven tons of oil standing on a quay and a woman with a slate who has no figure for what came in and will not put one there, and a figure of four hundred and fifty pence with the February figure visible above it and both dates, and the mole-head light out and not coming back. A word comes down on the coal boat: there is a sheet of forty lines on a market wall in that town and it went up the previous night and nobody paid for it. A lighterman without a road, a shipwright with nothing on his bench, a man of fifty-one four days into working out what a berth is worth, a man of about thirty-four of the third lay going down to the hard with a glass and telling nobody what he saw. Nothing in, nothing out.
9. **349 — Saturday the third of July. THE SIXTH CLAUSE READ ALOUD, AND NINE MEN SAYING WHAT AN OPEN ROAD IS. PAID, THE RESOLUTION IN OTHER MOUTHS.** The sixth clause read once out of a copy in a coat, written out by the reader's own hand on the twenty-seventh of May past, offered unasked, and he says he cannot make it do anything on its own and that it is doing both things at once. **Elias Voke: an open road is not a freedom.** **Iver Sallow: a thing on the water has to be looked at by somebody who is not being paid by the person who wants it looked at.** A man of the second lay of about thirty-eight, who has had three sentences in that market in a month, says a fourth in nineteen words, and it is in no book and he would not give a name. The notice stands and was not touched and nothing was put on it and no one stood in front of it. Nobody proposed anything. Nothing in, nothing out.
10. **350 — Sunday the fourth of July. THE TWENTIETH DAY OF THE NINETY, THE READ-BACK WITH BOTH DEFINITIONS ON THE FACE OF IT, THE MOLE HEAD AT TEN PAST FIVE, AND THE WHOLE STANDING INVENTORY ONCE. PAID, IN FULL. THE VOLUME'S LAST PAGE.** **READ-BACK at four: eighty-two, two hundred and eighty-seven, none, seventy-four; AT CLOSE: eighty-three, two hundred and eighty-nine, none, seventy-five, the seventy-fifth the last thing in that book and the column not closed. Second column the ledger's own; the first's eighty-two and the fourth's seventy-four at the hour are a count of entries and a count of lines, a day of the first column carrying one entry against it whatever else that day printed, and both definitions are printed on the face of the reading. THREE COUNTS ON THE FACE: ONE wipe (60th), TWO charges walked on none (59th, 60th), ONE wage Tuesday (29th, thirty-sixth week), THIRTY-SIX WEEKS FALLEN DUE. MONEY: 0 + 0 − 0 = 0.** Three statements about three objects; the mole head at ten past five; the whole standing inventory once and nowhere else; **the twentieth day of the ninety, the yard having taken the figure of ninety on the fifteenth, the day the six were told to stand by.** Nothing in, nothing out.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 350

- **Calder and Mara.** He told her in plain words on the twenty-fifth, without softening a figure and without putting it in a book first, which is what he did on the sixteenth of June and was caught at for on the nineteenth. She said four things, none of them kind, and asked for the second of them written down before she said the other three: **it is not his and he is going anyway.** She is not going, because there is a man of about thirty-four two days down that coast who cannot read and one more person in the town who knows is a thing she can do without. She asked for it to be heard out of a book a stranger can check, and said that that is the only difference between a man and a notice. She is in that harbor on all ten days and goes nowhere, of no office, not on the crew, not restored, not forgiven, forty marks first after food neither reduced nor paid. **Not resolved, and not to be resolved in this volume.**
- **Calder and Nessa.** The pair the record stands on. She writes the sheet left-handed on a thwart with a coat under it, entered a day lost with a reason and no name, and says out loud in that shed that if a name is ever put against that line it will be put there by somebody who is not her. He reads the rule of the first of May out first and states what a power is and what a trade is and what the difference is. He gave her the crossing in a boat that is not his on a man's own hook and did not thank her for it. Nothing romantic, everything expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on all ten days ten until four, never approached, nothing on the bench read as a gift, one shoe on that bench beside him that is not his and has been there since the third of May past. The holder was in that harbor on nine of the ten and was out of it from half past seven on the evening of the twenty-sixth to half past five on the morning of the twenty-seventh, and went up no coast road on any of them. Neither brother said why. **The far bench man is not in this yard's book at all.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **321 — Saturday the fifth of June. FOUR OLD BOOKS IN A DRAWER, AND THE FIRST PRICE. PAID.** Cobb Terrell down on a crutch, eight days without weight, carrying word of a man of thirty-one with a chart in a bag. Four vessel books laid out unopened past the first page: *Morrow Lass*, *Gull's Rest*, *Tern's Debt*, a stitched book. The man with the bag goes past the slip, asked nothing. First price in the first column before any use: the soundings are of a coast that has moved, no figure for how far to be approached. Nothing in, nothing out.
2. **322 — Sunday the sixth. A MAN GOING PAST A SHOP, AND THE SECOND PRICE. PAID.** The man of about thirty-six goes past the chandler's counter with an empty basket; the wife counts sixty candles at fourpence being four shillings and calls it a price of nought. On the crown he says his father spelled one rock three ways and a spelling is a year. Second price in the first column: the route can be used only if a crew gives up the Ternwatch road inside the line, about eleven tons to a lighter, for the season. Nobody has said yes. Nothing in, nothing out.
3. **323 — Monday the seventh. THE FIFTY-SEVENTH WIPE, THE FIFTY-THIRD CHARGE, A CHART FROM A DOORWAY. PAID.** The wall bare for the fifty-seventh time; the cistern charged and walked on none, the fifty-third. The holder stands in the reeve's office doorway about a minute and looks at the framed Crown chart of about nine years: Bramble Strait with soundings both shores and nothing across the middle. Neither of the harbor's two copies held, no custody entered. The man of fifty with a form in his coat stands at the slip, asked nothing. Nothing in, nothing out.
4. **324 — Tuesday the eighth. THE THIRTY-THIRD WEEK, THREE NOTS UNASKED, TWO BOOKS OPENED. PAID.** A wage Tuesday, four marks not paid, thirty-three weeks fallen due; the boy not on the stone, the three nots against this day not asked about. Cobb puts weight on the foot, the ten days up with the seventh, in the water on the eleventh. *Morrow Lass* and *Gull's Rest* opened: *Skur Deep, Scurr Deepe, Skere Depe*, nine, nine and a half, eight and three quarters fathom, eleven, seventeen, twenty-three years past. A difference in two books, not a truth about a sea. Nothing in, nothing out.
5. **325 — Wednesday the ninth. A BOAT'S NAME IN A MAN'S MOUTH, FOUR MINUTES ON PURPOSE. PAID.** In about nine people's hearing the man of thirty-one names her himself: *Ashtide Rose*, coaster out of Ashtide, about forty tons, nine years his, chart bought fair at Ternwatch six years past with no storm route on it, bag shut, not opened, not asked for. The yard stands four minutes on purpose and asks nothing, as on the twenty-third of May. *Tern's Debt* opened: *Skower Deep, Skour Deap*, nineteen years past. Two men of about thirty-one told apart and entered. Nothing in, nothing out.
6. **326 — Thursday the tenth. THE FIFTY-FOURTH CHARGE, FOUR BOOKS OPEN, A MINUTE LOOKED AT. PAID.** The cistern charged and walked on none, the fifty-fourth. The stitched book opened: *Skorr Depe, Skor Deep, the depe off the Skore*, twenty-seven and nine years past. Four books, eight spellings, one water, seven hands. On the crown the holder looks at **Tobias Wren** for about a minute and does not go over; the far bench is a different man and is not looked at. The fouling ladder stands at a foot and seven inches, not looked at by this yard, nobody to explain it, and the keeper is not Garrow Fisk. Nothing in, nothing out.
7. **327 — Friday the eleventh. NINE PEOPLE, A FATHER'S BOOK READ OUT LOUD, FOURTEEN DAYS UP. PAID.** Cobb walks plainly, fourteen days off the water up, back to warps and not in a boat. In about nine people's hearing the man of thirty-six reads his father's square-hand soundings: *Skar Deep, Skarre Depe, Skar Deap*, eight and three quarters, nine, nine and a half fathom, twenty-one, fifteen and eight years past. Five books, one water, every book disagreeing by a quarter to three quarters of a fathom. The man of sixty-one not in the market. Nothing in, nothing out.
8. **328 — Saturday the twelfth. ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE, FIVE BOOKS AND A CHART OPENED BY ITS OWNER. PAID, THE FINDING.** About forty in the market hear the father's three read again, the ship's hand say this yard's **eight further** spellings out loud, and the man of thirty-one lay his own chart open himself, hand on the empty middle water, fold it himself, bag it himself, touched by nobody but him. A storm route across Bramble Strait no current chart includes; the chart that omits it a Crown chart of about nine years this harbor holds two copies of, neither held by this yard. **Tobias Wren** on the crown all morning, not in the market, not sent for; he is not the man at the far bench and is not Alden Marr. Nothing in, nothing out.
9. **329 — Sunday the thirteenth. ABOUT FORTY ON A CROWN, FOUR MINUTES, A REFUSAL. PAID, THE REVERSAL.** Five open books on two sailcloths; the man of thirty-six gives the opportunity out loud and asks nobody. **Tobias Wren steps forward from his own work bench, looks about four minutes, touches nothing, refuses both things he could say — neither of them in this yard's book and not going in it — and says instead, because he has seen it before: *I have seen that water*, eight words, of *Skorr Depe*. Looked at by forty, asked by none. The holder never went over. Nobody agreed in a room, nobody refused in a room, no stage taken. Nothing in, nothing out.
10. **330 — Monday the fourteenth. THE CLOSE: FIFTY-EIGHTH WIPE, FIFTY-FIFTH CHARGE, READ-BACK, THREE STATEMENTS, WHOLE INVENTORY ONCE. PAID, IN FULL.** **READ-BACK at four: sixty-two, two hundred and five, none, fifty-four; AT CLOSE: sixty-three, two hundred and eight, none, fifty-five, the fifty-fifth last in the book. Second column's figure the ledger's own, not a paragraph count; first's sixty-two and fourth's fifty-four at the hour paragraph counts and checkable. THREE COUNTS ON THE FACE: TWO wipes (57th, 58th), THREE charges walked on none (53rd, 54th, 55th), ONE wage Tuesday (33rd week, column unmoved). MONEY: 20 + 0 − 0 = 20.** The route restated book by book with spellings and dates; the two prices standing before any use; the whole standing inventory once and nowhere else. **A man of about fifty with a form in his coat stands at the foot of the mole's steps at about half past four and does not come up, and the standing is not one of the three afternoon lines and is not going to be.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 330

- **Calder and Mara.** She is in that harbor on all ten days and goes nowhere, mends cuffs on the bench, asks nothing about the books, is told nothing she does not ask. Of no office, thirty, not on the crew, not restored, not forgiven, forty marks first after food neither reduced nor paid. The concealment is spent and not told.
- **Calder and Nessa.** The pair the midpoint stands on. She opens books one at a time, enters every spelling, figure and date exactly as it stands, writes the difference-line five times, says **eight** of this yard's spellings out loud in about forty people's hearing — **eleven in all across the five books** — and reads the leaf back in full in her own left hand. He names both prices before any use and refuses the old refusal and the free acceptance alike. Nothing romantic, everything expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied all ten days ten until four; not asked on any, asking nothing on any, no fragment, no report talk, no second story; the holder did not go over on any of the ten, was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any, neither brother said why. **The minute on the tenth and the four minutes among forty on the thirteenth belong to Tobias Wren and NOT to Alden Marr; this file previously credited them to both men, which was the merge the chapters had already separated. See `outline/volume-07.md` § *Divergences from this outline's own Movement 3*, item 1.** Nothing on the bench read as a gift.
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks whole, the three nots of the eighth standing unasked on that day and after, third column unfilled and unappointed, hand at its head with the name beside it not said again.
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **Looked at, never asked, never thanked, never sent for, never a teacher, door or sacrifice; lock L27a holds and is not improved on.** Given the opportunity before forty people, refused both things he could say, said eight true words because he has seen that water. Not the injury this volume costs, not the sacrifice this volume costs, not to be spent. **Bandaged in the right hand on every one of the ten days, which is why the hook is in his left, and the divergence from the outline's *bandaged until the second of June* is recorded on the face of the outline and at `state/continuity.md` item 1.6.**
- **Calder and the wardrobe.** Cobb mended and back to warps; the man of thirty-six with his father's book and no candles; the chandler and his counting wife, counter shut to one man; the man of fifty with a form unfilled, unadvised; the man of thirty-one with a chart in a bag, unasked, untouched, uncited; his double of no lay told apart; the ladder-keeper of thirty-four, unnamed, unexplained, not Fisk; the hod-of-lime man answered by nobody.

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **311 — Tuesday the twenty-fifth. THE THIRTY-FIRST WEEK WITH NO ENVELOPE, AND THE GOVERNING SENTENCE SAID OUT LOUD IN A CHANDLER'S. PAID.** A wage Tuesday, four marks not paid, the column does not move, **thirty-one weeks fallen due.** A man of about sixty of the first lay comes back into the shop he said he would come back into, and **says out loud, in about nine people's hearing, a sentence of twenty-one words, being *a restriction that arrives in a sentence and not in a boat is a thing a man cannot be angry at*, and then the second half of it unnumbered, being *and a man who cannot be angry at it will be angry at something else by Friday*.** He has counted both, and says he counted the sixteen-word sentence of the twenty-first too, in his own house, on the Friday night. He says out loud that he did it in nine people's hearing on purpose and noticed in about the fourth word that he was doing the very thing he had warned about, and did it anyway, and gave the reason: **a true thing said only to a man in his own house is worth nothing to anybody else.** A chandler says that a man of fifty-one with a stove on his afterdeck stood at his counter on the Saturday for a quarter of an hour and bought no candle at fourpence, and that he has watched this three times on this coast and has never been able to tell afterwards which was which. Neither improved on; both in the second column. Nothing in, nothing out.
2. **312 — Wednesday the twenty-sixth. THE DECLARATION'S FOURTH LINE, AND A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WHO DOES NOT CHOOSE. PAID.** In a fish market in about nine people's hearing a man of about forty-three reads the fourth line off his own form twice, being *whether she carries material which is the subject of an unsettled claim*, and asks a man of about fifty what to put in the box. **A yes is a handing over and a no is a lie** — twelve words, counted out loud by the woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall, who says she has a figure for a candle and none for a yes. The man of fifty gives two reasons and says he will go out on the Friday with the box empty and that **that is the absence of a plan and not a plan.** The man of about forty-three asks the holder of that writ for an opinion in a market, and is refused, and the refusal is given out loud in five parts, being that this yard does not draft and does not copy and does not witness and does not countersign and does not advise. **The ninth boats of the third lay are lying off where there were eleven on the twenty-fourth.** Nothing in, nothing out.
3. **313 — Thursday the twenty-seventh. THE FIFTIETH CHARGE WALKED ON NONE, AND THE OFFICE WITH NO SEASON USED AGAIN AND THE USE IS WORSE. PAID.** The cistern charged and walked on none, being the fiftieth. **Two men go into the harbor authority's office on the west basin separately and are not in the room together and neither is sent by anybody.** The man of fifty-one of the eighteenth is in there twenty minutes and comes out and stands in the sun. Then **a man of about thirty-six of the third lay** puts a form on the clerk's table and is refused in the same three sentences in the same order, and the clerk refuses to unsay or improve on the four words he said on the eighteenth, and adds a fourth thing that is not one of the three: **he is not going to hold it**, because in about four years somebody will want to know where that sheet was on the twenty-seventh of May and there is one answer to that. **The man of thirty-six says out loud that he has eleven weeks of a season, has not been out since the seventeenth, is not going out on the Friday, and that that is a day — and says it to the room and not to the clerk. And the clerk says out loud, unprompted, that he has been owed a quarter by his own office since the first of April and has not mentioned it to a living soul, and that nothing has been taken off him.** The holder of that writ is on the west basin walk for a quarter of an hour and does not go in, and gives the man of thirty-six the price of a boat and the fact that a party with no instrument may be hired by a private person, and the man does not ask for a reason and the yard wrote down that he did not. Nothing in, nothing out.
4. **314 — Friday the twenty-eighth. MARA VENN RETURNS, AND THE FIRST MONEY INTO THAT YARD SINCE THE FIFTH OF MAY. PAID.** **THE FAR BENCH OCCUPIED FROM TEN UNTIL FOUR AND NOT APPROACHED.** A woman of thirty comes up the mole on her own back with a crate and says out loud that she came back because she said she would and not because anybody asked her to, and asks **one** question, once, about the round of glass in a drawer four days up that coast, being **who is the second hand on it**, and it is not answered, and the same answer is given as on the twentieth of May: one address in this country, no second, a party of one is not a custody. He says the sentence of the twenty-fourth of April about a page and a drawer **and says it is about the sheet on that wall and is not about her drawer and is not going to be used about it, including by her.** Then at about half past two, at a box on the corner of the mole, **one mark and eightpence, being one hundred and sixty-eight pence, comes into that yard's own book for the first time since the fifth of May: a boat of about thirty tons with a man in her for a day, hired by a boat's owner of about fifty-five, on his own account and for his own purpose, to get his own hook and chain out of about nine feet of mud off the west quay inside the harbor's own line.** Said out loud that it is not salvage, not a claim, not a claim window, not a charter and not a way of getting past anything, and **that the notice governs leaving the port and passing the line and does not govern one shackle of chain in nine feet of mud.** The man in her is **Cobb Terrell, about forty-one, of that harbor's own second lay, a hired hand, and he gives his name out loud and it went in**, and the boat's owner says all five things to him and not the yard, before the painter went and not after. **At about half past three a broken stud on the end of that chain comes through the mud and takes Cobb Terrell across the top of the left foot.** He does not go in the water. Nobody from that yard was in the boat or on the water at any hour of that day.
5. **315 — Saturday the twenty-ninth. THE CHANDLER IS NAMED IN A MARKET, AND WHAT IT COSTS THE MAN WHO NAMES HIM. PAID.** Eight boats of the third lay lying off. **A man of about thirty-six of the third lay says out loud in a fish market in about nine people's hearing a sentence of fifteen words, being *the chandler of the front street put a sentence into this harbor on Tuesday morning*, and says that he carried it four days and put those four words on the front of it at his own table on purpose on the Thursday night, and says the whole of the twenty-one-word sentence and the *by Friday* half of it, and says out loud that it is the day after Friday and that there is nothing in this harbor he can be angry at that has a hull on it.** The chandler listens twice, says nothing, shuts his door and does not open it again that day. **On the Sunday his wife counts the sentence out loud at fifteen words at her own counter and says the first four of them are her trade and that she did not put them there, and says her husband is not going to sell that man candles again, and that a candle at that harbor is fourpence and has been for as long as she has been in that shop, and that about sixty of them between that day and the end of June is four shillings, and that it is a price of fourpence and it is going to be a price of nought.** **Nobody in that yard went and told the chandler to sell to him, nobody went and told the chandler not to, and nobody went and told the man he was wrong or that he was right**, and the holder of that writ says out loud that he is not going to write four shillings against a man's anger, and is not going to put a candle in a wheelhouse out of a bag, and gives the reason: the moment this yard does that it is a party to a quarrel between two men in this harbor, and it has paid that three times this month for other people and is not paying it a fourth time for itself. Nothing in, nothing out.
6. **316 — Sunday the thirtieth. THE FAR BENCH OCCUPIED FROM TEN UNTIL FOUR AND NOT APPROACHED, AND A MAN IN A BOAT THIS YARD PAID IS ASKED A QUESTION. PAID.** **Cobb Terrell says his own figure out loud twice on his own account**, being two marks, seven shillings and fourpence, being four hundred and eight pence, ten days without weight on that foot and fourteen off the water. **A man in a blue coat, about fifty, with a book, who is not an officer and has no rank and is not named and is a working man and not a face of anything, comes up the mole and asks him one question: what is that yard doing on this harbor. The holder of that writ gives the standing reason out loud BEFORE the man answers** — a man in a boat this yard has paid is a man this yard can be asked about, the rule of the first of May, given to the asker and not to the man asked — **and then Cobb Terrell answers: *I am not going to tell you what you should have said*. Nobody improved on it and nobody argued with it and about nine people heard it, and the holder of that writ gives out loud on the mole the reason it is said a second time: a man who has a sentence when it is easy and a better sentence when it is not has a chosen sentence, and that is what the first of May is for.** The man in the blue coat then says three things out loud, and none of the three is a threat and none is a lie: **he has not got a room with men in it deciding this, he has got a notice and a form and a desk and a line from a mole-head to a can upon a stake and a master who will not tick a box and a man in an office who cannot write anything down; he does not know whether that is right and would like to go on not knowing; and a restriction that gets a man's paper into a room he cannot reach is a bad instrument, which he does not say is a false one, and he has been using it for nine days and has watched a boat of about thirty tons lie off that mole with a stove out of her wheelhouse while it was bad.** Nothing in, nothing out.
7. **317 — Monday the thirty-first. THE FIFTY-SIXTH TIME THAT WALL CAME DOWN, THE FIFTY-FIRST CHARGE WALKED ON NONE, THE NEW-VOLUME QUESTION ASKED ONCE, AND THE SECOND MONEY IN. PAID.** The wall bare for the fifty-sixth time, the cistern charged and walked on none, being the fifty-first. **A man of about sixty of the first lay says out loud at a mole head in about nine people's hearing a sentence of sixty-three words, being: *the day a man in this harbor works out that it is cheaper to be angry at a boat than it is at a sentence, this harbor will get a captain, and it will be one of ours, and it will be a good one, and it will be a man who is angry and who is telling the truth about being angry*.** He counted it four times and says so. He says that being careful with it for ten days has got a chandler's counter shut and a man of thirty-six with no candles and a man of forty-one with a bone in his foot. **A man of about thirty-eight begins to say, in about nine people's hearing, that this harbor wants somebody to speak for it, and the holder of that writ stops him about four words from finishing — in front of all of them, so that the unfinished thing is on a mole and not in a drawer — and says that he is not going to tell the man what should come next and is not going to refuse it either, and that he is going to leave a space on that mole where it was going to go.** He is asked for a name, has not got one, will not go and look, and says this is the third thing and the correct number is three and not four. He leaves the two unlit candles on the stone and the chandler comes up for them. **At about four in the afternoon the man of about thirty-six hires the same boat for the same figure, one mark and eightpence, to shift about nine tons of salt off a lighter inside the harbor's own line**, and the man in her is about twenty-six and gives his name and it went in, and the five things are said to him by the hirer and not the yard before the painter went and not after. **The question is not answered and may not be answered, and no person on that mole named a body and no person on that mole proposed one.**
8. **318 — Tuesday the first of June. THE THIRTY-SECOND WEEK WITH NO ENVELOPE, AND THE PRICE RISES. PAID.** A wage Tuesday, four marks not paid, **thirty-two weeks fallen due**, the next on Tuesday the eighth of June for the thirty-third. **A sheet dated the twenty-ninth of May, a bill of an agent at Ternwatch and not a quotation, is read out loud at the end stall in about forty people's hearing, and ONE FIGURE CHANGES: a barrel of lamp oil, three hundred and seventy-eight pence in February being thirty-one shillings and sixpence, and four hundred and fifty pence today being thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, a rise of seventy-two pence, being six shillings exactly.** It goes on the slate the day it is quoted to her and not the day she heard it, with the February figure left visible above it and both dates on the board. **The other eight figures do not move, and the small bottle of physic at fourteen pence with *none in this harbor* against it does not move, on purpose.** She says that nobody in this harbor set it, that a man in a city four hundred miles off wrote it on the twenty-ninth and has never been to this quay, and that she has said *I have none* to about two hundred people since the ninth of April of whom about forty had money, and that from today she can say a figure instead of a sentence and that she has lost the only thing she had. She says out loud that a barrel at the February figure means the mole-head light is out in October and that seventy-two pence is a fifth more oil and a light is not a fifth more light. **A man of about twenty-six with a hod of lime says in about nine people's hearing in that market that the man of about thirty-six is not to be trusted with anything, and the man he says it to does not answer him and looks at the two figures on the slate instead.** A doctor of about fifty-five says at that table that a man in a bed at Ashtide has been on days since the seventh of May and that today is the twenty-fifth day. **The holder of that writ refuses to say the rise is the notice and refuses to say it is not, and says so out loud, and says he is not going to invent a figure for a market's anger so that a shed has something in it.** Nothing in, nothing out.
9. **319 — Wednesday the second of June. A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE BACK ON THE WATER, AND THE BONESETTER'S BILL. PAID.** **The far bench occupied from ten until four and not approached.** **Tobias Wren is on the crown of that mole at about half past eight in the morning with a bandaged right hand and a boat's hook in his left, and nobody sent for him, nobody met him, nobody said good morning, and he worked.** He is not this yard's injury and not this yard's sacrifice and this yard knows the difference and has entered it and is not going to spend him. **At about two in the afternoon a bonesetter of about sixty, in that trade thirty-one years and about four hundred things, comes down that hill because he does not go up one, and two marks, seven shillings and fourpence, being four hundred and eight pence, goes out of that yard's own book at a counter over a chandler's — the largest figure to leave that book since the ninth of April past, and a shade under twice what the same trade charged on the eighth of May past for a hand.** He does not say no, and says he does not want to know the trade's business, and says that a man angry at a foot is a man who has not yet worked out what else he is angry at. **The holder of that writ puts the whole price of the fortnight out loud: a party with no instrument may be hired by a private person for a private purpose, one mark and eightpence is the price of it, a yard that has three marks standing to a man of Ashtide since the eighth of August past, and seven pence standing to its own shipwright, and eight marks and a day of a boat standing to that harbor's own bellwright, has gone and been the thing that moves things inside a blockade, and the answer is that it is exactly like the other things and is not going to be made into anything else, and a man in a boat this yard has paid is a man this yard can be asked about, and that was true before the money was taken and is exactly as true after a bonesetter and is four hundred and eight pence more expensive.** A woman of no office asks one question, being where the money came from, and is answered in full, and says two words and asks nothing else.
10. **320 — Thursday the third of June. THE CLOSE, AND THE FIFTY-SECOND CHARGE WALKED ON NONE. PAID, IN FULL.** **The cistern charged and walked on none, being the fifty-second, which is the last of the three in this batch.** **THE READ-BACK, AND THE BATCH'S OWN COUNT PRINTED ON THE FACE OF IT: fifty-two entries in the first column at the hour of it and fifty-three at the close, one for every day from the twenty-fifth of May to the second of June and not one day in two of them; one hundred and seventy-four lines in the second at the hour of it and one hundred and seventy-seven at the close, being one hundred and forty-three, thirty-one and three; none in the third, with the boy's hand at the head of it and the name beside it not said again; forty-four in the fourth at the hour of it and forty-five at the close, and the forty-fifth is the last thing in that book. The second column's figure is the ledger's own and is not a count of paragraphs, and the first column's fifty-two and the fourth column's forty-four are paragraph counts and are checkable.** **THE THREE STANDING FIGURES OF THE TEN DAYS, COUNTED BY THIS YARD AND PRINTED ON THE FACE OF THE LEDGER AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANY OTHER BOOK: ONE wall wipe, being the fifty-sixth on Monday the thirty-first; THREE cistern rota days charged and walked on none, being the fiftieth, the fifty-first and the fifty-second; TWO wage Tuesdays, on neither of which the column moved, so THIRTY-TWO WEEKS STAND FALLEN DUE.** **THE THREE THINGS, about three different objects, all true, none improved on: the notice and the price, which this yard will not put in one sentence in either direction; the harbor, which is seven boats of the third lay where there were eleven on the twenty-fourth, a chandler's counter shut to one man, and a second Tuesday on which nothing happened; and the yard itself, which took two hires and paid a bonesetter and cannot tell afterwards whether that was a good afternoon or a bad one.** Then the whole standing inventory, once, and nowhere else.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 320

- **Calder and Mara.** **She came back up the mole on Friday the twenty-eighth with a crate on her own back because she said she would, and he did not go down to the slip and she did not look up the hill, and it was not a goodbye in May and is not an arrival in June and neither of them has called it anything.** She asked one question, once, about the round of glass, being who is the second hand on it, and it was not answered and is not going to be. **He said the sentence of the twenty-fourth of April out loud and then said it is about the sheet on the wall and is not about her drawer and is not going to be used about it, including by her.** On the second of June she asked one question about the money, was answered in full including the man's name, the day, the figure and the fact that the bag has twenty pence in it, and **asked nothing else, and the ship's hand entered that it was the first time in eleven days that a person in that street had heard money accounted for and then said one word, and that this yard has a rule about saying everything and has never had a rule about somebody saying nothing and is not going to get one now.** **She is of no office, she is not on the crew, she is not restored, she has not been forgiven, her forty marks stand first after food and were not reduced by a crate and are not paid, and the concealment is spent and is not told again for nothing and is not told at all in this batch.**
- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair this batch changed most and neither of them says so.** She counted a sentence at twelve words in a market, read a bill out loud in about forty people's hearing and entered the new figure on a slate and put no word against it, carried four hundred and twenty-eight pence in an envelope up the front street to a counter and put it down, and entered that a person said one word and then nothing. **He said out loud that a party with no paper in this country has one advantage, which is that nothing anybody does for it is a party to anything, and that he is not going to give that up for a box in a market, and that this is the third time this month he has refused a market in about nine people's hearing and the third time it cost somebody else.** She is twenty-seven, four stitches in a right hand since the twentieth of February, writing in her own left hand, and nothing in these ten days is romantic and everything in it is expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on three of the ten days, being the twenty-eighth, the thirtieth and the second, and not at any hour on the other seven; not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story; **the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** Nothing was put on that bench and read as a gift.
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May 2026, forty marks standing whole, the three nots of the eighth of June standing and now five days off, the third column unfilled and unappointed, his hand at the head of it with a name beside it that is neither his nor the holder's. **That name was said out loud once in a boat on the thirteenth of May and has not been said since and is not going to be said in this volume. He was not on the stone on any of the ten days and no name of his is in any column of that book and none has ever been.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **Back on the crown of that mole at half past eight on the second of June with a bandaged right hand and a boat's hook in his left, not sent for, not met, not thanked, and not going to be.** **He is not this volume's injury and is not this volume's sacrifice and is not the man in the boat this yard hired, and the yard knows the difference and has entered it and is not going to spend him.** One line in the second column is the whole of what is on the page about him.
- **Calder and Elias Voke.** Carried and not on the page of these ten days. Fifty-one, nineteen winters disputed and unpaid, a hard at Ashtide unanswered since the ninth of November, a season of nine marks that is not going to be paid, and a stove on an afterdeck of a boat of about fifty tons. **A chandler in a market on the twenty-ninth said out loud that this man stood at his counter for a quarter of an hour on the Saturday and bought no candle at fourpence, and that the chandler did not ask him what he had, and that this is what he has instead of a reason.** He may not be made a symbol.
- **Calder and Cobb Terrell, the man of about thirty-six, the chandler of the front street and his wife, the man in the blue coat, the bonesetter, and the man of about sixty.** **The batch's cost landed on seven people, none of whom owed anything to this yard and all of whom were not thanked:** a man of about forty-one who gave his name out loud and was hurt in a boat this yard paid and said his own figure out loud twice of his own accord; a man of about thirty-six who named a trade in a market and bought no candles at fourpence; a chandler and his wife who lost a customer of nine years and did not ask and were not asked; a man in a blue coat with a book who asked one question and was answered once; a bonesetter of about sixty who came down a hill he does not go up; a man of about fifty who has a box in a form that is not filled; and a man of about sixty who has carried two unlit candles for ten days and has said three things and is stopping.

**Line Diver. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH AND NONE IN VOLUME 07 BEFORE MOVEMENT 5. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND IS NOT RE-TAKEN, NOT IMPROVED AND NOT RENAMED. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED. THE STORM-READER STAGE IS NOT TAKEN AND IS NOT TO BE TAKEN IN MOVEMENT 3.** What this batch pays is not a stage and is not a power: **the price of a party with no instrument that has been hired by a private person for a private purpose, which is that it is now the thing that moves things inside a blockade, and the answer is that it is exactly like every other thing that does, and it is not going to be made into anything else.** A seam identifies difference and not truth. **The word *seam* on a page of this batch is the mole's own second and fifth seams and is not the perception. The mark on the face of the second seam was fouled about a foot and seven inches when it was last looked at, on the nineteenth of May past, and NO PERSON OF THAT YARD WAS IN THE WATER ON ANY OF THE TEN DAYS AND THE MARK WAS NOT LOOKED AT, AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF THAT HARBOR'S OWN SECOND LAY WHO KEEPS THE WHOLE FOULING LADDER IN HIS OWN BOOK WAS NOT ASKED FOR A FIGURE AND IS NOT GOING TO BE.** **AND THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH AND NOTHING IN THESE TEN DAYS IS CHARGED AGAINST IT AND NO DAY OF THE TEN WAS LOST TO IT, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN, and a later volume may not go back and enter a day of this batch against it after the fact.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THESE TEN DAYS.** Nothing is charged against it and no day was lost to it, and the batch ran ten days on a body that was not asked anything and was not charged once.
- **The bag is twenty pence, being one shilling and eightpence.** It was ninety-two pence, being seven shillings and eightpence, on the twenty-fourth of May. **THE WHOLE OF WHAT CAME INTO THAT YARD IN THE TEN DAYS IS THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS, ONE SHILLING AND FOURPENCE, AND IT IS TWO PRIVATE HIRES AT ONE MARK AND EIGHTPENCE ON FRIDAY THE TWENTY-EIGHTH AND MONDAY THE THIRTY-FIRST. THE WHOLE OF WHAT WENT OUT IS FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHT PENCE, BEING TWO MARKS, SEVEN SHILLINGS AND FOURPENCE, TO A BONESSETTER OF ABOUT SIXTY, AT A COUNTER OVER A CHANDLER'S, ON WEDNESDAY THE SECOND OF JUNE. 92 + 336 − 408 = 20, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF IT.** Neither hire was salvage, a claim, a claim window, a charter or a way of getting past anything, and every person in each of those boats was told all five of those things before the painter went and not after. **NOT ONE PENNY OF LINE WENT OUT OF THAT BAG IN THESE TEN DAYS, AND NOTHING WENT OUT OF IT ON ANY DAY BUT THE SECOND.**
- **The figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks is six hundred and twenty pence, being three marks, eleven shillings and eightpence**, and it is not going to be paid and nobody is to write one word under it saying anybody is going to.
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, twenty envelopes on a bench, and THIRTY-TWO WEEKS HAVE FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE.** There were two wage Tuesdays in these ten days, the twenty-fifth of May and the first of June, and the column did not move on either. The next falls due on Tuesday the eighth of June for the thirty-third week and will not move on it either.
- **The slate wall came down bare once in the ten days, the fifty-sixth on Monday the thirty-first, the counter not restarting, the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting held in that room on any day of this yard's life. The cistern was charged on three rota days and walked on none of them, the fiftieth, the fifty-first and the fifty-second.** No figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the twenty-eighth, the thirtieth and the second of June, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of them.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for the hundred and twenty-third night. The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and fifty-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June past and not lashed back, and neither has moved.** Nine feet of chain on a nail in that shed wall and a bar of square iron in the drawer, neither sold nor given away, and nobody has asked whose either is.
- **A man of about forty-one of that harbor's own second lay is not to put weight on the left foot for ten days and is not to be on the water for fourteen.** Seven boats of the herring third lay were lying off that mole on the third of June where there were eleven on the twenty-fourth of May, with not one of them past the line and not one of them breaking any rule of that harbor.
- **A CUPBOARD OF PLACES, AND NOT ONE OF THEM HAS A HANDLE ON THE INSIDE, AND THE BATCH ADDED ONE AND DID NOT FIND A HANDLE ON THAT EITHER:** a drawer in a house four days up that coast, held by one person, whose second hand cannot be named without making a second address in this country. **That is the tenth place and this yard has a handle on the inside of none of them.**
- **Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved, and nobody was sent for him. Seven pence to that yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May past, unargued, the chest not opened, the bellwright not asked in twenty days and no digit of anything he said printed. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots of the eighth of June standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed. Nothing in a tin in that shed since the twenty-eighth of April past.**
- **A BARREL OF LAMP OIL AT THAT MARKET IS FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY PENCE, BEING THIRTY-SEVEN SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, WHERE IT WAS THREE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT PENCE, BEING THIRTY-ONE SHILLINGS AND SIXPENCE, IN FEBRUARY, AND THE CHEAPEST THING IN THAT HARBOR WENT UP SIX SHILLINGS ON TUESDAY THE FIRST OF JUNE AND IS NOT COMING BACK DOWN.** A mole-head light with its lens out since the seventh of May was going to be out in October on the February figure. **There are two figures and two dates on the back of a slate at an end stall and nobody is going to improve on them.**
- **AND A HARBOR POORER ON THE THIRD OF JUNE THAN ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, WITH FOUR FIGURES THAT ARE NEW TO IT: a barrel of lamp oil at four hundred and fifty pence where it was three hundred and seventy-eight in February; a candle at fourpence that a man with no work is not buying; thirty-two weeks of a wage of four marks with no envelope against them; and four hundred and eight pence out of a bag that held ninety-two.**
