### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **301 — a crate for a fourth day, and a tender all night. PAID.** Saturday the fifteenth. **A Crown tender of about sixty tons lay off the south end from about ten o'clock on Friday night until first light, and nobody in that harbor went out to her and nobody came in and nothing was landed.** A glazier of about forty-four says on a street four streets off the front that he has paid a boy of nineteen on every Friday since the sixth of March and is not going to be the man who does not. **A boat's owner of about fifty-five comes up the hill at about eleven and at about half past four, and at about half past four there has been a man in a blue coat on his boat at the slip with a book, and a line on the ring bolt, and a minute looking at the water with his face to it, and no question asked of anybody.** And he is told, twice, in the same words, at eleven and at half past four, why this yard is not going to go and look at his boat. The last true thing of the chapter is his: **you are a fool if you have not.**
2. **302 — nine words, and a man who counted them. PAID.** Sunday the sixteenth. **A chandler was asked on Saturday, in about nine people's hearing in his own shop, what boats had been out of this harbor in a fortnight and where they had gone, and gave nine words and no list, and says out loud that the same nine words would have been given on any Tuesday in the year.** A copper pipe is four days away at Ternwatch, a day's water has about four hours in a month, a boat's man is four marks a day, a slip is three shillings a week, and none of it is paid. At about five a tender of about sixty tons lies off the north side with about forty people on that mole, and **a boat's man of about forty goes out in a dinghy and comes back at about half past five and says a man on her asked him one question, being whether a crate had gone off that mole on the fourteenth of May, and that he said he had not been there and did not know and was not going to say, and that the man said, *then you will want to hear it again from the man who wrote it*. HE COUNTED THE NINE WORDS BECAUSE HE CAME OFF THE WATER WITH NOTHING IN HIS HEAD BUT THEM.** And the holder of that writ says out loud in about forty people's hearing that he is not going to tell that man what he should have said, and has not been asked, and is not going to be asked, and the reason is a rule from the first of May.
3. **303 — eight clauses, and a door four lines from a lock. PAID.** Monday the seventeenth. **The wall came down bare at eight for the fifty-fourth time, and at about a quarter past nine a notice of the closed-sea squadron in eight clauses was put up on the outside of whatever was there, on a stretch of wall the yard's own fourth return had come off at four the previous afternoon, and the other two papers on that wall — naval notices of the second of December past and the twenty-second of June past, further along the same wall and not on the same square of it — were not taken down, and neither was this one.** The clerk who wiped the wall and put the notice up **is about sixty and has been a clerk twenty-two years, gave no name, was not asked for one, and is not the clerk of the circuit office**, which is a second column line on the page. **The cistern was charged and walked on none, being the forty-seventh. A person of no office carried a crate up a hundred and forty feet of stone on her own back at about a quarter to seven and gave her reason once on the steps, and he did not go down to the slip and she did not look up the hill, and it was not a goodbye and neither of them called it anything.** The notice is read in a market in about forty people's hearing by a man of about thirty-four who says he cannot tell what four of the lines mean and is not going to guess, and a woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall says the sentence of the whole notice: **a closure has a door in it and this has got a door in the sixth line and no handle on the inside**, and gives the first price of the volume, being a barrel of lamp oil at thirty-one shillings and sixpence in February, and says the mole-head light will be out in October. And a man of about thirty-two asks, in a market, where a man lodges a declaration.
4. **304 — a clerk with a quarter owed him, and a Tuesday on which nothing happened. PAID.** Tuesday the eighteenth, **a wage Tuesday, four marks not paid, no envelope, the column does not move, and THIRTY WEEKS HAVE NOW FALLEN DUE.** A master of fifty takes a properly made declaration to the harbor authority on the west basin and the clerk of it, **who is about sixty, has been a clerk twenty-two years, is unnamed, gave no name, and is not the clerk of the circuit office**, tells him three true things: **the season of that office ended on the thirty-first of March with nothing issued, there is no book into which a paper can be put, and he has had no power to receive anything since the first of April.** And says the words *I do not know* out loud, and asks the man not to decide about his boat in that room, because four people in that harbor will be told where he was. **The boat of about seventy tons goes out at about eleven with no declaration and is not asked for one and is not stopped and is not followed, and comes in at about six and takes her berth, and one of her men stops at a chandler's and the other goes to his house, and the ship's hand says out loud that in nine months this harbor will have a record of a Tuesday in May on which nothing happened and that nobody can check it.** The round of glass is in a house four days up that coast and this yard did not send anybody there.
5. **305 — two marks and one shilling, and three soundings. PAID.** Wednesday the nineteenth, **the far bench occupied from ten until about four and not approached.** A plasterer of about thirty-eight asks at the head of the slip, in about nine people's hearing, for a boat to carry a chest up that coast for his wife, and says out loud that he has two marks and one shilling, being three hundred and fifty-two pence. **He is refused, with the reason given in two parts out loud: a party with no instrument cannot give a hirer a paper to produce, and a man of this yard carrying a thing for a person in a house makes this yard a man in that house's business.** He says that a boat of about thirty tons goes up on the Saturday for eight marks, being one thousand two hundred and eighty pence, and that neither figure is going to change. **A doctor of about fifty-five says at the foot of the steps that there is no physic in this harbor and that he has been putting nine days on a chest since the seventh and is not saying it to anybody in particular.** Then the yard spends its last hireable money, **and spends it once: a boat of about thirty tons at one mark and eightpence and a penny of line, on this yard's own account, and three soundings inside the harbor line, and the mark on the face of the second seam is fouled about a foot and seven inches on the weather side and nothing on the other side, and the bottom under the crown is sand and not rock.** A man of about thirty-four of that harbor's own second lay took the soundings, **came out in the hire and cost that bag nothing beyond the hire and gave his name to nobody, and is not Garrow Fisk**, and **three people went out in that boat off that yard's account and not four**. He has the whole fouling ladder in his own book on the day, from four inches on the twelfth of March to a foot and seven inches today, and says he makes nothing of it and that a figure a man in a boat can go and look at is the only kind there is.
6. **306 — nine figures on a slate, and a tenth that is the price of paper. PAID.** Thursday the twentieth, **the cistern charged and walked on none, being the forty-eighth.** A woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall keeps nine February figures on the back of a slate and has had no bill for any of them since the ninth of April, and writes *no quotation* against all nine, and says the whole of the volume's method out loud in about forty people's hearing: **none of those figures is set in this market, every one comes off a manifest out of a merchant's agent at Ternwatch, and the agent's price is set in a city four hundred miles off by people who have never come to this quay and are never going to.** And then the tenth figure, which has not moved in nine years: **a sheet of paper is a penny and forty sheets are a shilling**, and she asks one person in that market to look at it. And in the shed that night a question is put to this yard about the woman of about fifty-eight with the paper in a drawer under her bed, **and it is refused, on the ground that this yard has one address in this country and is not going to make a second, and the reason for the refusal is given as WORSE than it was in April and not better, and both times it cost somebody else and not this yard.**
7. **307 — eleven boats lying off, and a man with three things who will not finish them. PAID, AND THE VOLUME'S SENTENCE IS DELIBERATELY NOT PAID.** Friday the twenty-first. **Eleven boats of the herring third lay are lying off that mole with about fourteen men in them, and not one of them has passed the line, and every one of them is inside the harbor doing nothing wrong.** A candle is fourpence and a candle burned on a boat lying off is not earned. A chandler says the thing nobody else has said: **I have not lost a customer, they are out there.** A man of about sixty of the first lay, forty-one years on that water, asked a question in this harbor twice and was answered neither time, says in about nine people's hearing in a chandler's that he has had three things since Tuesday; **names three honest targets for a coming anger, being a man with a book, a chandler, and the harbor authority of this harbor, and says all three are wrong; AND THEN STOPS ON PURPOSE AND SAYS WHY OUT LOUD, being that a sentence said in a chandler's on a Friday morning is in eleven markets by Sunday and comes back with a man's name on it that the man did not put there, and that he has watched that happen twice on this coast and once it was fair and once it was murder and he could not tell afterwards which was which.** He is asked for a name and has not got one and is not going to go and look for one, and says he has asked this harbor two questions already and the correct number of times to ask a question is three and not four. **He takes two candles at fourpence and goes down to the water and says he will come back into that shop on Monday the twenty-fifth. A boy of seventeen carries nine words up that hill from the *Anna Ray* and is taken up the front street instead.** **THE VOLUME'S CENTRAL SENTENCE AND THE CAPTAIN ARE ON NO PAGE OF THIS BATCH AND ARE MOVEMENT 2'S TO PAY, ONCE. They were in the first draft of this chapter and have been withdrawn, and the new-volume question is therefore NOT YET ASKED and is owed by Batch 0002.**
8. **308 — two hundred and eleven, and a woman who is not going to stop. PAID.** Saturday the twenty-second, **the far bench occupied from ten until four and not approached.** The ship's hand has the notice of the seventeenth copied for a penny out of her own hand and not out of the yard's book, in a room off the fish market, and a copyist of about fifty-nine who has been in that room for twenty-two years and has never once asked anybody what she is copying tells her three things without being asked any of them: **she has made two hundred and eleven copies of ONE NINE-LINE SHEET ABOUT A CHAMBER OF A DROWNED CITY since the twenty-seventh of April, which is a different sheet from the notice of the seventeenth, of which not one word is in it, the two sharing nothing but a counter and a penny, and the naval notice itself has been copied four times since and this was the fourth; and she is not going to stop, and the reason is that a copyist who stops copying is a copyist who has admitted she copied something, and a trade can be put in a schedule and a confession cannot.** **And she names the four buyers she knows, and the first of them is this yard, on the twenty-seventh of April at about half past two, a man of about thirty-two with split hands who did not sit down and paid for one and did not ask for a second, and the third of them is a woman who bought nine at a penny each on the ninth of May and carried them out in a cloth against her chest with both arms, and about whom the copyist has thought for a fortnight and does not know what a person does with nine.** THIS YARD ASKED HER NO QUESTION ABOUT THE WOMAN AND WROTE NOTHING AGAINST HER AND WILL NOT FOLLOW HER, and the reason is on the page.
9. **309 — a can that is not on a chart, and a stove on an afterdeck. PAID.** Sunday the twenty-third. A man of about thirty-one of the third lay, of a coaster out of Ashtide, with a Crown chart of about nine years standing in a bag, says three things in a market in about nine people's hearing: **the can upon a stake at the outer marks is not on the chart, not on the outer marks, not on the mole-head approach, and not in the approaches table at the back; it was there in the last week of March; and he is not going to say where he got the chart and nobody in that market is going to ask him.** The chart is not opened and not shown. **The holder of that writ stood in that market for about four minutes and asked him no question, and said out loud that he had used the four minutes on the not-asking, and that he is going to write the price of it down afterwards instead of before, and that this is the second time in one month and both of them were the same mistake.** Elias Voke, fifty-one, nineteen winters disputed and unpaid, comes ashore and says he is not going to ask this yard for a stove and that the harbor authority's clerk took his letter and said he had no season, and **that has been the best answer he has ever been given and the worst one he has ever been given.** And the sentence that goes in the second column: **this is the second time in five volumes this yard has been able to do exactly nothing about a man who is cold, and the first was a man of twenty-eight in a bed at Ashtide, and both are the same sentence and this yard did not write either half of it, and there is no figure yet that tells unable and decided-not-to apart.**
10. **310 — the close. PAID, IN FULL.** Monday the twenty-fourth, **the wall came down bare for the fifty-fifth time and the cistern was charged and walked on none, being the forty-ninth, and the far bench occupied from ten until about four and not approached.** **The read-back: forty-two entries in the first column at the hour of it and forty-three at the close, one for every day from the fifteenth to the twenty-third and not one day in two of them; one hundred and thirty-nine lines in the second at the hour of it and one hundred and forty-three at the close, being one hundred and fifteen, twenty-four and four; none in the third, with the boy's hand at the head of it and the name beside it that was said out loud once on the thirteenth of May and is not said again; thirty-four in the fourth at the hour of it and thirty-five at the close, and the thirty-fifth is the last thing in that book.** **THE THREE TRUE THINGS, about three different objects, and none improved on: the notice, which has two true sentences four lines apart and a man of thirty-four read both aloud in about thirty seconds and this yard is not going to say either that anybody wrote them that way on purpose or that nobody did; the copies, which cannot be made a conspiracy because the best that can be done with two hundred and eleven is a counter off a fish market and a woman of fifty-nine, and the third part of which is the holder of that writ saying out loud that he wanted to put the woman with a cloth in front of a person with a pen and is not going to, and that the only reason he could do it is that he is good at finding things out, and he is not going to be the other thing as well; and the wall, said from the top of the steps by a man of about sixty of the first lay who was not asked up there, being that there are about eleven people on this coast who cannot read the notice and that nobody in this town has said one word about that in seven days.** Then the last thing done that day: **a man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet out of Bramble Strait comes ashore at about five, does not go up the hill, stands on the stone at the top of the mole steps, and reads out loud in about nine people's hearing the line off a sheet folded in four, being *a page in a shed on the mole at Morrow Quay, in a drawer, fourth of five*,** and says he has been four days on the water to read it off a wall in a town four days up this coast, that he is not going to say who he works for, and that he does not work for anybody, and that the market there would not take the sheet down. **AND HE SAYS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THIS YARD IS, WITHOUT BEING ASKED, IN ONE BREATH: that line is on a wall and it is in a drawer in a shed and it is on about sixty boats, and it is on those boats because a yard printed it, in its first year, with a place for every copy of itself on the face of it, and he has not got anything against that, and he came four days to say it out loud on a step, and he is going back on the tide at about seven, and he is not going to write.** And this yard writes nobody, sends nobody, asks him nothing, and thanks nobody.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 310

- **Calder and Mara.** **She carried a crate up a hundred and forty feet of stone on her own back at about a quarter to seven on Monday the seventeenth, gave her reason once on the steps, was not thanked and thanked nobody, and he did not go down to the slip and she did not look up the hill.** It was not a goodbye and neither of them called it anything. **Her forty marks stand first after food, are not reduced, are not paid, and were not reduced by a crate.** She is four days up that coast in a house with the round of glass in a drawer and is not back before the twenty-eighth. **The concealment is spent and is not told again, and no chapter of this batch names the call or describes it or puts a sound in his mouth that a brother made.**
- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair this batch changed most and neither of them says so, and the change is that she now keeps a book of her own and writes the small figures into it before anyone asks her to.** She had the notice copied for a penny out of her own hand and told the copyist so when she was asked which pocket it came out of. She wrote the two hundred and eleven down as a figure said out loud by a person and not as a page. She told the boat's man not to take a message to that shed. She said out loud that in nine months this harbor will have a record of a Tuesday on which nothing happened and that nobody can check it. **She is twenty-seven, four stitches in a right hand since the twentieth of February, writing in her own left hand, and nothing in these ten days is romantic and everything in it is expensive.**
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on three of the ten days, being the nineteenth, the twenty-second and the twenty-fourth, and not at any hour on the other seven; not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story; **the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** Nothing was put on that bench and read as a gift.
- **Calder and Bevin.** Unchanged and not in a room. Off the stone since the fifteenth of May 2026, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, his hand at the head of it with a name beside it that is neither his nor the holder's. **That name was said out loud once in a boat on the thirteenth of May and has not been said since and is not going to be said in this volume. He was not on the stone on any of the ten days and no name of his is in any column of that book and none has ever been.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** Unchanged and not sent for. Hurt in a right hand in Volume 06, in eleven pieces on the crown of that mole, not thanked and not going to be, **not in the boat of the nineteenth, not asked anything, and not made a teacher and not made a door.** His absence until the second of June is carried and nothing in these ten days made him one thing or the other.
- **Calder and Elias Voke.** **On the page on the twenty-third and not treated as a symbol.** Fifty-one, nineteen winters disputed and unpaid, a hard at Ashtide applied for on the ninth of November and not answered, a season of nine marks that is not going to be paid. He came ashore, said he was not going to ask this yard for a stove, said the harbor authority's clerk took his letter and said he had no season, and said that has been the best answer he has ever been given and the worst one he has ever been given. **This yard asked him nothing, sent nobody, and did not go down to the water.**
- **Calder and the copyist of about fifty-nine, the woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall, the boat's man of about forty, the boat's owner of about fifty-five, the plasterer of about thirty-eight, the doctor of about fifty-five, the man of about sixty of the first lay, the man of about thirty-one of the third lay, and the man of about thirty-four of a screw-steam packet.** **Nine ordinary people, none of them a keeper and all of them, and not one of them asked anything of this yard and not one of them owed anything to it.** **And the standing cost of the batch is theirs, not this yard's: a chandler who answered nine words and can no longer be sure which of nine boats was out; a copyist with two hundred and eleven copies in a town and a reason for not stopping that this yard has no argument against; a glazier with no work in two months paying a boy of nineteen every Friday; a plasterer with two marks and one shilling and eight marks the other way; a doctor putting nine days on a chest; a man of sixty who has asked a question twice and has one left; and a man of thirty-four who came four days up a coast to say one line out loud on a step.**

**Line Diver. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN THIS BATCH AND NONE IN VOLUME 07 BEFORE MOVEMENT 5. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, NOT IMPROVED AND NOT RENAMED. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED. A seam identifies difference and not truth. **AND THE ONE THING THIS BATCH DID TO THE HOLDER'S STANDING IS NOT A STAGE AND IS NOT A POWER: on the nineteenth he spent the last hireable money in that yard on three soundings, because a figure a man in a boat can go and look at is the only kind there is, and on the seventeenth he did not go down to a slip and look at a boat, and on the twenty-second he did not ask a woman one question, and on the twenty-fourth a stranger read his own yard's sheet out loud on his own mole steps and he did not write to him.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** Nothing in these ten days is charged against it and no day of the ten was lost to it, and that is stated rather than left open: **the batch ran ten days on a body that was not asked anything and the body was not charged once, and a later volume may not go back and enter a day of this batch after the fact.**
- **The bag is ninety-two pence, being seven shillings and eightpence**, and it was two hundred and sixty-one pence, being one mark, eight shillings and fivepence, on the fourteenth of May. **The whole of what came into that yard in the ten days ended on the twenty-fourth is nothing, and the whole of what went out is one hundred and sixty-nine pence, being one mark, eightpence and a penny of line on the nineteenth, and the one hundred and sixty-eight is a boat with a man in her for a day and the penny is line.** The figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks is **five hundred and forty-eight pence, being three marks, five shillings and eightpence**, and it is not going to be paid and nobody is to write one word under it saying that anybody is going to.
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, twenty envelopes on a bench, and THIRTY WEEKS HAVE FALLEN DUE WITH NO ENVELOPE.** There was one wage Tuesday in these ten days, being the eighteenth, and the column did not move on it. The next falls due on Tuesday the twenty-fifth for the thirty-first week and will not move on it either.
- **The slate wall came down bare twice, the fifty-fourth on Monday the seventeenth and the fifty-fifth on Monday the twenty-fourth, the counter not restarting, the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting held in that room on any day of this yard's life.** **The cistern was charged on three rota days and walked on none of them, the forty-seventh, the forty-eighth and the forty-ninth.** No figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the nineteenth, the twenty-second and the twenty-fourth, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of them.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for the hundred and thirteenth night. The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and forty-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved.** Nine feet of chain on a nail in that shed wall and a bar of square iron in the drawer, neither sold nor given away, and nobody has asked whose either is.
- **A CUPBOARD OF PLACES, AND NOT ONE OF THEM HAS A HANDLE ON THE INSIDE.** A crate on a mole step for four days. A drawer in a shed on a mole. A counter in a room off a fish market. A market wall in a town four days up that coast. A slip at a hard in this harbor. A net loft. A drawer under a bed in a house four streets off. A box in a boat. A room two streets up a coast road in a town four days off, where a woman of thirty will be until the twenty-eighth of May. **NONE OF THESE IS A KEEPER AND ALL NINE ARE, AND THIS YARD HAS SAID THAT OUT LOUD TWICE IN FIVE MONTHS AND BOTH TIMES WAS TOLD IT BY A PERSON WHO WAS NOT OF THIS YARD.**
- **Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved, nobody sent. Seven pence to that yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, the chest not opened, the bellwright not asked in ten days. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed.**
- **AND A HARBOR POORER ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF MAY THAN ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, WITH THREE FIGURES THAT ARE NEW TO IT: eleven boats of the herring third lay lying off with about fourteen men in them, a candle at fourpence, and a mole-head light that will be out in October on the strength of a February figure nobody has been quoted a different one for.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book and paid by this batch, all nine of them, and the list is at `state/chapter-summaries.md` § *Volume 07, Batch 0001*, Chapter 310:** a restriction that is legal, careful, and impossible to comply with, and whose impossibility is a municipal office's season and not anybody's design; a blockade named as a hand on a price rather than as a closure; a price list set four hundred miles off by people who will never come here; a sheet at a penny and forty for a shilling and about two hundred of one nine-line sheet through one counter in twenty-five days; a copyist who is a trade and not a confession and who is not going to stop and whom this yard will not ask; a page a community put on a wall naming a drawer in this shed; a man of about sixty who names three honest targets for a coming anger and says all three are wrong; a figure about eleven people on this coast who cannot read a notice; and a stranger who came four days up a coast to say one line out loud on a step because a quiet search is worse than a public one.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY ANY LATER CHAPTER:** the plate at the fifth seam and its open note, now carried for a fourth volume; the case of five bells and the limit four people of that coast wrote; the delayed note at eleven and two; the lead plug and the chest and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the certificate of method, whose standing in a market was spent on the twenty-second of April and is not restored; **the form on a step two days down that coast, which no later chapter may say was withdrawn or unserved**; **the Quietening, named once, in Chapter 281, and not named again**; **the woman of about fifty-eight with a drawer under her bed, who was considered as a second address on the twentieth of May and refused, and who may not be written to**; **and **the new-volume question, WHICH IS NOT ON ANY PAGE OF THIS BATCH. A man of about sixty of the first lay named three honest targets for a coming anger on the twenty-first of May, in about nine people's hearing in a chandler's, and said all three are wrong, and stopped on purpose before he said the rest of it, and took two candles at fourpence and went down to the water. THE QUESTION IS OWED ONCE BY MOVEMENT 2 AND IS NOT ANSWED, no chapter of this volume may answer it, and no later volume may answer it out of this one's material.****

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A HARBOR WAS CLOSED ON PAPER IN ELEVEN DAYS, THE OFFICE ITS FIRST CLAUSE NAMES HAS NO SEASON AND NO CLERK WITH AUTHORITY AND THE YARD'S OWN MONEY LASTED FOUR DAYS, A CHANDLER GAVE NINE WORDS IN NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, A COPYIST HAS TWO HUNDRED AND ELEVEN COPIES IN A TOWN AND A REASON FOR NOT STOPPING, ELEVEN BOATS ARE LYING OFF INSIDE THEIR OWN HARBOR LINE, A DOCTOR IS PUTTING NINE DAYS ON A CHEST, A MOLE-HEAD LIGHT WILL BE OUT IN OCTOBER, AND A STRANGER READ A LINE OFF THIS YARD'S OWN SHEET OUT LOUD ON THIS YARD'S OWN MOLE STEPS IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING, AND A HARBOR IS POORER.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 300

**VOLUME 06 IS WRITTEN. CHAPTERS 251 TO 300, FIFTY CONSECUTIVE DAYS FROM TUESDAY THE SIXTEENTH OF MARCH TO FRIDAY THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY, THE FIRST TEN OF THEM TWO DAYS TO A CHAPTER AND THE LAST FORTY ONE DAY TO A CHAPTER. NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 06 IS OWED BY THIS PHASE, THERE IS NO VOLUME-CLOSE OR AUDIT PHASE QUEUED AFTER IT, NONE WAS CREATED, AND A QUEUE THAT POINTS AT A VOLUME 07 OUTLINE WHICH DOES NOT EXIST HAS INVENTED A VOLUME THAT NO PLANNING FILE CONTAINS AND NONE WAS INVENTED HERE.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **291 — the decision, and a machine named. PAID.** Wednesday the fifth. **Six hundred and forty-nine pence in and nothing out, the first money into that yard since the eleventh of April, on a private person's account and for a private person's purpose.** A man of about fifty-five hires the party to look under his own boat and says why out loud before he is asked: whether the thing along her starboard side is his or was there before he bought her. **He gets his answer inside his own hire — a cut in the rock about nine feet long and about two inches across, with dressed sides and square at both ends, about four feet under her starboard side, counted twice and not the property of anybody, and the yard cannot tell him whose it is and puts it in the first column because a man can go and look at it with a pan and a line — and he pays the whole of it without arguing with a figure and does not ask what it meant.** A man of sixty-one is asked for his boat and for nothing else and sets one condition, and **NAMES THE CROWN SEAL IN A SHED, in his own mouth, because he has seen one: a round of glass in a collar with a wheel and a screw, in a bed cut in a sill, the mark of its name cut into the round — a machine and a seal at once, and a term and not a lock, and nobody in this country ever looks at one.** The yard does not enter the word in the first column. **The price of a descent is named out loud before anybody agrees to it at fourteen marks, three shillings and fourpence, and the yard cannot pay it, and the day goes off a book at Ternwatch because a man of sixty-one asked for it, and the holder of that writ says out loud that he has a rule about a man this yard has paid and none about a man this yard is being paid by.** And at four o'clock, before anybody has agreed to anything, **the letting is decided and its price is named: this yard will not read the chamber and will not take one piece out of it, and the only proof it will ever have of anything about a drowned city will be in a thing that closed.**
2. **292 — the working day. PAID.** Thursday the sixth, a rota day, **the forty-fourth charge, walked on none.** The book sends Amos Searle and the yard says no out loud, and the second name comes at the same figure. **The pot is down twenty past eight and up half past eleven at about seventy fathoms, and the gauge reads eighty-four pounds and the mark is not moved.** **A cut face of thirty feet with a doorway in it, a sill with a bed and, under the lip, a rebate; a plate of glass in the bed and not in the rebate; the bed empty; two hundred and nine marks in the sill, counted three times, and a day cut beside them, being the eleventh of May.** Nobody goes in. **He loses the afternoon and writes the day's entry himself, slowly.**
3. **293 — the round, and the storm. PAID.** Friday the seventh, **the far bench occupied from ten until four and not approached.** The reason for going again is said out loud at eight in the morning: **the plate goes into the rebate on the eleventh, and a plate the width of a doorway does not come down on a stone floor and stay off it.** **A round of glass comes up out of the bed with a chain of eleven stamped links on it and a date on every link, and a piece of worked glass bedded in it that will not come away.** It goes on the crown under a tarpaulin and **not into the shed, because the second clause of the notice of the thirty-first keeps recovered transparent mineral out of every shed.** Then the weather: **the skylight, the door light, a pane of plate, two boats' running glass, eleven windows and the lens of the mole-head light, and about a hundred people in the rain and nobody hurt, and no cause named for it in any volume.**
4. **294 — the injury, in three parts. PAID.** Saturday the eighth. **A pane of plate goes over on the crown of that mole across the RIGHT hand of a man of sixty-one, edge first, once.** A bonesetter of sixty who **does not say no** sets it, gives the figure and the date, and will not hear a word about who brought him: **a mark and four shillings, two hundred and eight pence.** **He is not on the water until the second of June and the north bar job is not going to happen, and his boat of about nineteen tons, which he built himself fifty years ago or near it, has taken a stove in the weather and is in eleven pieces on that mole.** He is not thanked and is not going to be.
5. **295 — the accounting, and a figure that comes back. PAID.** Sunday the ninth. **Four marks and a shilling to a glazier for two lights and a skylight, which is the whole of the glass this yard owns in that harbor.** **A man of sixty-one brings his own account of the weather up the steps unasked, in his own book, four streets off, on a page that is not on top of this yard's.** And **the figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks, which has had no subject since the seventh of April, comes back at forty-three pence on a bag of five hundred and ninety-seven, and the chapter says it came back and not that anybody is going to pay it.**
6. **296 — the concealment, in a room with two people in it. PAID.** Monday the tenth, **the wall comes down bare for the fifty-third time and the cistern is charged and walked on none, being the forty-fifth.** **The Oren mark is told once and once only, in her room, to her, and told twice because she sets that as the price, and the first time it was told it was nine seconds in a shed in a voice he could not have repeated.** Four things she will not do, and will not forgive him, and cannot do again. **Neither of them calls it a reunion.**
7. **297 — the letting. PAID.** Tuesday the eleventh, **the wage Tuesday: the column does not move and twenty-nine weeks have fallen due; the far bench occupied from ten until four.** **The round is carried down the mole steps in the open air in front of about nine people, stands in two hands on the stone, and is not put back, and the sentence is: the chamber closes whether it is read or not, and we are letting it close.** And: **that is not a surrender and it is not a proof, and nobody in that boat is going to say this yard was right about it, because it does not know.** At a quarter past two **the plate goes down into the rebate and is not coming up and nothing is holding it up**, and nobody in the boat saw the beginning of it and a man in a boat could see the end of it, **and that is what a figure cut in a sill is for.**
8. **298 — a consequence, a lead, a seal and a loss. PAID.** Wednesday the twelfth. **A lead of about fourteen pounds marked at every fathom and a slate with no name on it, and the whole of that sill entered in the first column in about nine minutes by anybody with a lead.** Then alone on the crown, **the eleven stamped links, and a seal line on the last of them read through a flat piece of glass so as not to scratch at it: *Sealed and entered at the Morrow circuit office by order of Magister Ilya Serr, senior Registry examiner* — dated in the chain and older than the collar of the same office, and a difference in two made things says nothing about which is right.** **HE IS IN NO ROOM.** And at half past two **he cannot say one of the nine lines of the order, and she reads them off the sheet in the drawer in ninety seconds and he has them again, and a thing relearned is not a thing remembered, and the record outlives the man.**
9. **299 — the two marks, a name, and three true things. PAID.** Thursday the thirteenth, **the cistern charged and walked on none, being the forty-sixth; the far bench occupied from ten until four.** **The two marks four hundred yards apart: this yard's own, fouled about a foot and a half where it was four inches in March, and one with a shackle of a make nobody in that harbor makes, whose season of nine marks is not paid and is not going to be asked for.** A man of sixty-one looks at it from ten feet off the bottom for four minutes and refuses to say either of the two things he could say. **The name at the head of the third column is said out loud once in that boat and it is Mara Venn, and it is said once and not again.** Then three statements about **the sill, the round and the room**, all three true, all three different, and none of them Chapter 290's words, marks and house.
10. **300 — the close. PAID.** Friday the fourteenth. **The read-back: thirty-two entries in the first column at the hour of it and thirty-three at the close; a hundred and twelve lines in the second at the hour of it and a hundred and fifteen at the close; none in the third, with the boy's hand at the head of it; twenty-four in the fourth at the read-back and twenty-five at the close, the last of them the last thing in that book.** **The thirteen things**, read out in the flat voice she uses for a column and entered without addition, of which **the fourth is the seal line and the fact that no such person is in a room, and the thirteenth is the poverty**: a working harbor poorer on the fourteenth of May than on the twenty-third of February, the four returns four and no fifth, five drawers five drawers, the plate in eleven feet with its note open, the forty marks twice, the wage column standing, and two hundred and sixty-one pence in a drawer on a mole. And then **a round of glass going up that coast in a drawer in a woman's hand on the eighteenth** — the round that came out of the bed beside the plate, and not a piece of the plate, the two having been separate objects from the seventh of May onward — and her forty marks not reduced and not paid.

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 300

- **Calder and Mara Venn.** **She is the one who named the word on the twenty-fifth of April, and the one who said the third of the three true things on the fourth of May, and the one the name in the third column belongs to, and she was not in the room for the reading on the twenty-ninth and was not asked to be. On the tenth of May he told her the Oren mark, once, in a room with nobody else in it, and he said it twice because she made the price of it, and she said four things she would not do and one thing she cannot do again, and neither of them called it a reunion. On the fourteenth the round of glass went into a drawer in her hand and it did not buy a shilling of her forty marks. He does not get to be thanked and she is not going to forgive him and she is not going to be able to do it again.**
- **Calder and Nessa Pike.** **She is the one who made him say the letting out loud so that it would be a record, and who made him say the thirteen, and who read the nine lines back to him off a sheet in ninety seconds and told him what the loss was. She has four stitches in a right hand and writes in her left. She said the first of the three true things in Chapter 299 about the sill, and she has still not said one word about the cost to the yard of anything in these ten days, and the ledger is in her hand and the ledger is what the ten days are.**
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **He was asked for a boat and not for knowledge, he set one condition, he did not want to be thanked, he named the Crown Seal because he has seen one, he was not asked one question about the stair, he paid for the day's plant and air in his own name, he kept his own account of the storm in his own book and brought it up unasked, he is hurt in the right hand and a boat he built himself is in eleven pieces on that mole, and he did useful work afterwards by looking at a shackle from ten feet off the bottom and refusing to say either of the two things he could say about it.**
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on three of the ten days, being the seventh, the eleventh and the thirteenth, and not at any hour on the other seven; not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story; **the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** Nothing was put on that bench and read as a gift.
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, his hand at the head of it with a name set beside it that is not his and not the holder's, **and that name was said out loud once on the thirteenth of May, in a boat, and it is not going to be said again.** He was not put on anything and was not asked one word about the omissions he has entered, and no name of his is in any column of that book.
- **Calder and Elias Voke.** **Untouched and unasked, for the fifth time.** The six fathoms of his gear are still flat on a course of cut stone at forty fathoms under a lead, and the season of his mark is nine marks and is not paid, and he was not in the boat on the sixth and he was not in the boat on the thirteenth.
- **Calder and the four people of that coast.** **Untouched and unasked, for the fifth time, with a fifth reason written out loud: that this yard has now read the sill of a chamber of that kind at seventy fathoms in its own ground is not a reason to ask them. The complaint was not raised. The limit they wrote and signed stands and the holder did not ask to have it lifted once in these ten days.**

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** One afternoon lost to it, being the sixth of May, in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure. **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, still nameless, not struck out, and in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is one mark, eight shillings and fivepence, being two hundred and sixty-one pence**, and it was five marks, one shilling and fourpence, being eight hundred and sixteen pence, on the fourth. The whole of what came in in the ten days is **six hundred and forty-nine pence on the fifth of May only**, and **the whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December past is now two thousand four hundred and nine pence, and the figure of one thousand seven hundred and sixty the four state files carried is withdrawn and named as withdrawn here.** The whole of what went out in the ten days is **one thousand two hundred and four pence, being two hundred and eight to a bonesetter, six hundred and sixty to a glazier, and a mark and eightpence twice for a boat and a man in her**, and **not one penny of the twenty-eight marks, six shillings and eightpence of plant and air on the sixth and the seventh went out of this yard at all.** The whole of what has gone out since the sixth of December past is **thirteen thousand nine hundred and five pence in twenty-seven transactions at ten counters.**
- **The figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks came back on the ninth of May at forty-three pence, being three shillings and sevenpence, with a subject, and the page says it came back and not that it was paid, and it is not paid. It stands at three hundred and seventy-nine pence at the close, being two marks, four shillings and eleven pence.**
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY-NINE weeks have fallen due with no envelope, the last of them being the twenty-ninth, which fell due on Tuesday the eleventh of May; the next is Tuesday the eighteenth for the thirtieth week and the column will not move on it.** There was one wage Tuesday in these ten days and the column did not move on it.
- **The slate wall came down bare once, the fifty-third, on Monday the tenth, the counter not restarting, the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting held in that room on any day of this yard's life.** The cistern was charged on three rota days and walked on none of them, being the forty-fourth, the forty-fifth and the forty-sixth, and no figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the seventh, the eleventh and the thirteenth, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of them.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for the hundred and third night. The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and thirty-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved.**
- **SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE CHARTER'S PLACE IS EMPTY, AND A FORM OF AN OFFICE THAT YARD DOES NOT BELONG TO IS ON A STEP TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, AND A PAPER WITH A SEAL ON IT IS UNDER A BED IN THIS HARBOR, AND A COPY OF A DROWNED CITY IS IN A DRAWER IN THAT SHED, AND A ROUND OF GLASS IS GOING UP THAT COAST IN A DRAWER IN A HAND THAT IS NOT THAT YARD'S. NONE OF THE FOUR IS A KEEPER AND ALL FOUR ARE, AND THERE IS NO HANDLE ON THE INSIDE OF ANY OF THEM.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April past. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved, nobody sent. Seven pence to that yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, he not asked anything, the chest not opened. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced nor paid. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed. **Nine feet of chain on a nail in that shed wall and a bar of square iron in the drawer, neither sold nor given away, and nobody has asked whose either is.**
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND A PRACTICE AND IS NOT A REGISTRY AND IS NOT A COURT AND IS NOT A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH PAST AND IS NOT AGED BY THIS BATCH, AND ITS FOUR LINES ARE ABOUT A RECORD AND NOT ABOUT A HOUSE, AND THIS YARD DID NOT LOOK IN ONE OF THE FOUR DRAWERS IT CANNOT LOOK IN AND WROTE TO NOBODY. THE OLD EVIDENCE CHAIN IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT AND THE TWO ARE NOT FUSED ON ANY PAGE.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book and paid by this batch, all thirteen of them, and the list of thirteen is in `state/chapter-summaries.md` § *Volume 06, Batch 0005*, Chapter 300:** a chamber that closes with a figure and a day a man can look at before it happens; a letting decided in advance with its price named first; a glass storm with no cause named; a working day's plant and air bought off a real book at the same figure and paid for by a man rather than by a yard; an injury in three parts with a real bill, a real absence and a real consequence; a permanent loss out of a man's own recall with no figure for it; the Crown Seal named as a machine and as a term and not a lock; a seal of a Registry examiner on the old evidence chain, dated in the chain and older than the office that made it, on a line, in no room; **the Crown's history exposed as incomplete and not as false**; a proof that is physical and labor-based and about half unreadable; the concealment told once, in a room, at a price, with nobody calling it a reunion; a name said out loud once that is neither the boy's nor the holder's; and a harbor poorer on the last page than on the first.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY ANY LATER CHAPTER:** the plate at the fifth seam and its open note; the case of five bells and the limit four people of that coast wrote; the delayed note at eleven and two; the lead plug and the chest and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the certificate of method, whose standing in a market was spent on the twenty-second of April and is not restored; **the form on a step two days down that coast, which no later chapter may say was withdrawn or unserved**; **the Quietening, named once, in Chapter 281, and not named again in any of the fifty chapters**; **and the new-volume question, asked on the third of May and not answered in eleven days, which no chapter of this volume may answer and which no later volume may answer out of this one's material.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: THE ANSWER ABOUT A DROWNED CITY TURNED OUT TO BE AT SEVENTY FATHOOMS UNDER THIS MOLE, AND IT WAS FOUND BY PEOPLE WHO WERE NOT LOOKING FOR IT, AND IT WAS NOT READ, AND A GLASS STORM WENT THROUGH A HARBOR IN ABOUT SIX HOURS, AND A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE HAS TWO STITCHES IN A RIGHT HAND AND ELEVEN PIECES OF A BOAT ON A MOLE, AND A MAN OF THIRTY-TWO CANNOT SAY NINE LINES HE CARRIED IN HIS OWN HEAD, AND A WARD OF TWO AND A HALF HAS TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE PENCE IN A DRAWER, AND A HARBOR IS POORER.**

## Volume 06, Batch 0005 summary (Chapters 291–300) — the story state at the end of Chapter 300

**MOVEMENT 5 IS WRITTEN AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S CLIMAX, AND IT IS A CHOICE AND NOT A VICTORY.** In ten days a yard that had five marks and one shilling in a drawer earned six hundred and forty-nine pence from a stranger, bought two days of plant and air off a book four hundred miles off on a man's name and not on its own, went down to about seventy fathoms twice off the south end of its own mole, found a doorway in a cut face with a sill carrying a bed, a rebate, two hundred and nine marks and a day, took a round of glass with a chain of eleven stamped links out of the floor of the room behind a plate that had nothing behind it, caused six hours of weather it will never name, cost a man of sixty-one his right hand and his boat, decided in advance and out loud that it would not read the chamber, let the plate go into the rebate on the eleventh, could not say nine lines it had carried in its own head, told a woman of no office the thing it had kept since the middle of November, said a name out loud once, and closed its own book on a leaf with thirty-three entries, a hundred and fifteen lines, an empty column and twenty-five lines, and a bag with two hundred and sixty-one pence in it.

**THE BATCH'S MIDPOINT IS CHAPTER 296 AND ITS CLIMAX IS CHAPTERS 297 AND 298, WHICH ARE ONE EVENT: THE LETTING AND WHAT IT COST.** The chapters before 296 are the decision, the working day, the round, the hand and the accounting. Chapter 296 is the concealment. Chapters 297 and 298 are the letting, the closing, the lead and the slate, the seal on the chain, and the loss. Chapter 299 is the two marks, the name and the three true things. Chapter 300 is the read-back, the thirteen, the whole standing inventory and the final chapter image.

**THE BATCH'S COST, AND IT IS THE HOUSE'S OWN KIND: SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY-NINE PENCE IN AND ONE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED AND FOUR PENCE OUT, so a net loss of five hundred and fifty-five pence; **twenty-eight marks, six shillings and eightpence, being four thousand five hundred and sixty pence, of plant and air that went on somebody else's book;** a wage column that did not move on the one wage Tuesday in the ten days and twenty-nine weeks fallen due; an afternoon lost to the body with no figure; a right hand, a bill of a mark and four shillings, an absence until the second of June and a boat in eleven pieces; a permanent loss of a portion of the holder's own recall with no figure; a glass storm with no cause named in it; a chamber closed and unread; and a round of glass going up a coast in a drawer in a hand that is not that yard's.**

**CONFLICTS FOUND AND HOW THEY WERE RESOLVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN DEFENDED:**

1. **THE HAND-OFF THAT DISPATCHED THIS BATCH COUNTED ALL THREE OF THE STANDING FIGURES WRONG AND SAID SO ON ITS OWN FACE, AND THE CHAPTERS FOLLOWED THE ANCHOR.** It counted three Mondays in a span that has one, four rota days in a span that has three, and two wage Tuesdays in a span that has one. **THERE IS ONE WALL WIPE, BEING THE FIFTY-THIRD ON MONDAY THE TENTH; THREE CISTERN CHARGES WALKED ON NONE, BEING THE FORTY-FOURTH, FORTY-FIFTH AND FORTY-SIXTH; AND ONE WAGE TUESDAY, BEING THE ELEVENTH, ON WHICH THE COLUMN DID NOT MOVE, SO THE FIGURE THAT GOES FORWARD IS TWENTY-NINE WEEKS FALLEN DUE.** This is the second batch in a row whose hand-off mis-counted and it is recorded at `state/continuity.md` § *Batch 0005 as written*, item 1.3.
2. **THE WORD *QUIETENING* IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THESE TEN CHAPTERS AND THE WORDS *CROWN SEAL* ARE NAMED FIRST IN CHAPTER 291.** A scan of the ten chapters returns nothing for *quieten*, *orison*, *returning memory* and *panel*.
3. **THE MONEY RECONCILES IN ONE LINE: 816 + 649 − 1,204 = 261.** In: six hundred and forty-nine pence on the fifth of May, being three marks for a day's work at the standing rate, a mark and eightpence for a boat and a man in her, and a penny of line, on a private person's account and for a private person's purpose. Out: two hundred and eight to a bonesetter, six hundred and sixty to a glazier, and a mark and eightpence twice for a boat. **The whole of what has come into that yard since the sixth of December past is two thousand four hundred and nine pence and not the one thousand seven hundred and sixty the four state files carried, and the withdrawn figure is named as withdrawn in all four.**
4. **THE DESCENT IS BOUGHT AND IT IS NOT PAID FOR BY THIS YARD, AND THAT IS THE BATCH'S OWN ARGUMENT APPLIED TO ITSELF.** The day is fourteen marks, three shillings and fourpence, the identical figure of the eighth, ninth, tenth and twenty-eighth of April, component for component, and the figure *dearer* remains withdrawn. **It went off a book at a pressure house at Ternwatch because a man of sixty-one asked for it, and the holder of that writ said out loud, before agreeing to it, that a man this yard has paid is a man this yard can be asked about and that he does not know what a man this yard is being paid by is.**
5. **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS CAME BACK WITH A SUBJECT ON THE NINTH OF MAY, AT FORTY-THREE PENCE, AND THE PAGE SAYS IT CAME BACK AND NOT THAT IT WAS PAID.** It is not paid and it stands at three hundred and seventy-nine pence at the close.
6. **THE GLASS STORM IS ON THE PAGE AND NO CAUSE IS NAMED FOR IT IN ANY VOLUME, AND IT IS IN TWO HANDS ON TWO PAGES THAT ARE NOT ON TOP OF EACHING.** No character's action in this batch is caused by it.
7. **THE LETTING IS A DECISION TAKEN IN ADVANCE WITH ITS PRICE NAMED IN THE SAME BREATH, AND IT IS CARRIED OUT ON THE ELEVENTH WITH NOBODY ASKED IN BETWEEN, AND THE SECOND HALF OF IT IS SAID OUT LOUD: it is not a surrender and it is not a proof, and nobody in that boat said this yard was right about it because it does not know.**
8. **THE CONCEALMENT IS TOLD ONCE, IN A ROOM, AT A PRICE SHE NAMED, AND NEITHER OF THEM CALLS IT A REUNION, AND HER FORTY MARKS ARE NOT REDUCED AND HER CERTIFICATE'S STANDING IN A MARKET IS NOT RESTORED AND HE IS NOT FORGIVEN AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO BE ABLE TO DO IT AGAIN.**
9. **NO OFFICE ANSWERS IN A ROOM, NO SENIOR EXAMINER IS A FACE, HALVEN ROOK IS NOWHERE, AND MAGISTER ILYA SERR IS A SEAL LINE ON TWO PAGES AND IN NO ROOM, ON NO MOLE, IN NO MARKET AND NOT IN THIS HARBOR.**
10. **NO ONE OF THE FOUR PEOPLE OF THAT COAST WAS ASKED FOR ANYTHING, THE COMPLAINT WAS NOT RAISED, AND THE FACT THAT THIS YARD HAS NOW READ THE SILL OF A CHAMBER OF THAT KIND AT SEVENTY FATHOOMS IN ITS OWN GROUND IS NOT A REASON TO ASK THEM AND WAS NOT USED AS ONE.**
