## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 280

**MOVEMENT 3 OF VOLUME 06 IS COMPLETE AND ITS TURN IS PAID. A FORM WITH A NAME AND AN ADDRESS ON IT HAS BEEN PUT IN THE ORDINARY POST AND SERVED BY BEING LEFT, AND THE PRICE OF THAT IS A MAN'S AFTERNOON AND A MAN'S DAY AND A SEASON'S PEACE, AND NONE OF THAT PRICE BELONGS TO THIS YARD. AND A WOMAN OF NO OFFICE SAID A THING OUT LOUD IN A FISH MARKET IN ABOUT FORTY PEOPLE'S HEARING AND IT COST HER THE STANDING OF A CERTIFICATE OF METHOD IN A MARKET, AND THE CERTIFICATE CANNOT BE WITHDRAWN, BECAUSE THERE IS NO OFFICE TO TAKE IT FROM. AND THE PRICE OF THE VOLUME'S OWN SOLUTION IS NOW SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROBLEM, AND THE SOMEBODY IS AT THE END OF A STALL IN THIS HARBOR, AND IS NOT FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST UNDER SEVENTY FATHOMS.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **271 — the undertaking broken, and four lines. PAID.** Thursday the fifteenth of April. The thirty-eighth charge, walked on none. **Calder Marr breaks the three things he said on Wednesday the fourteenth out loud in that shed before nine and gives one reason, which is that a form exists and that a yard which does not answer a letter is an address that answers nothing, and an address is an address.** Four unsigned lines go into the post at a penny, and **the fourth line is five words: *I am asking you. Not the yard***, and she reads that line eleven times and the three above it not once.
2. **272 — the person of no office, and the line of the fourth of April. PAID.** Friday the sixteenth. **MARA VENN IS A PERSON OF NO OFFICE, THIRTY, OF THIS HARBOR, AND HAS BEEN SINCE THE FOURTH OF JANUARY PAST, AND THE GEOGRAPHY CONFLICT IS SETTLED ON THE PAGE AND NOT BY INVENTION: the second column's line of the fourth of April which said her letter came four days up that coast IS WRONG, IS NOT STRUCK OUT, and has the correction written against it, and the reason she gives is that a yard which strikes out its own line because it was wrong is a yard which has decided that a wrong line is not a record.** She puts **a form** on the bench — particulars of material held as unsettled, five ruled lines, one filled in with a name and a house in a town two days down that coast, a foot that says served and has nothing after it, and **a seal line with Halven Rook's name on it, entered in the first column because a name on a piece of paper is a thing a man can go and look at.** She **refuses to name the young man who filled in the first line**, and it is entered as refused and not as not-asked. **She has had the sheet eleven weeks, since the fourth of January, and cannot put it in a drawer, cannot burn it, cannot post it and cannot hand it to a yard, and those are four things and she has tried three.**
3. **273 — the four lines, and the mark. PAID.** Saturday the seventeenth. The mark, thirty-six days on it, a foot and three-quarters and two inches, the shackle found with a thumb. Four hundred and eighty pence out. **THE DISCOVERY: the four lines made on the sixth of March past are about a RECORD and not about a HOUSE. There is not one address in them and the word house is not in them at all. A record may be asked who has read it, which is why the second line is written the way it is — a no can be asked about, so a no is not written. A house may be asked nothing. A form cannot be served on a record because a record has no address, and a record is given one by writing down where the drawer is.** And Calder Marr says the turn out loud, once: **this yard did it on the third of April in a good cause, and a page in a drawer in a house is custody an office can reach, and the only reason a form has not been at somebody's door in eleven days is that nobody here has held one, and that is not a protection, it is a fortnight of luck.** **Nessa Pike refuses to copy the four lines into the fourth column**, and a yard does not add a sixth page to anything.
4. **274 — five doors, and a penny. PAID.** Sunday the eighteenth. **Four doors shut on the sheet inside two hours, in this order: not the drawer, not the tin because a tin shuts, not a wall because a sheet on a wall in that harbor goes out of that harbor, and not a fire — and the woman of no office says the last of those out loud for the two of them, that a person who burns a paper with unsettled material on it has handled it, and a person who has kept it is the thing the paper is about, so the burning is the keeping and it is the same door.** Three addresses are ruled out — this shed, the boy, and the man of about thirty who cannot read, which is the only one in that book which is not that yard's. **The reason is not that he is a keeper; a form cannot tell the difference and neither can the holder of that writ. The form goes in the post at half past four at a penny, and the undertaking of the fourteenth is entered in the first column as broken and not as kept.**
5. **275 — the fiftieth wipe, and the outer marks. PAID.** Monday the nineteenth. The fiftieth wipe, the thirty-ninth charge walked on none. **They wait, and there is no figure for waiting. The shipwright says out loud that this yard has now put three things into the world it cannot go and look at, and that the third of them is going to arrive on a step and not in a drawer.** They stand on the crown for twenty minutes, **see the outer marks for the first time from that ground and take no figure and enter nothing**, because the bar has not been narrowed and this party is not going to ask to have it narrowed, in advance or in a boat. And **a boat of this yard may not go to the outer marks either.** And it is decided that **no letter is to be written to the man of about thirty**, because a form on a step and a letter behind it in one week is two things from this yard at one door.
6. **276 — the twenty-sixth week, a lost morning, and three doors. PAID.** Tuesday the twentieth. The wage Tuesday; the column does not move; twenty-six weeks. **He loses the morning to the body and says the only sentence anybody in that harbor has used for it.** In the afternoon the chain and the bar go down the front street and are refused at three doors: a chandler who would not take it at nothing or at four shillings; a boat's owner of about fifty-five who asks whose it is and then says out loud on his own step that the next man who comes down that street with a thing off a wreck will be able to say that this yard asks; and a man of about sixty-one behind a counter who **offers a shilling for the chain and is refused, and asks for the reason and is told that a nail is a thing that cannot be a sale.** What the afternoon cost is not a money figure: about nine people now know.
7. **277 — the outer marks, and a bar that is only a change in the water. PAID.** Wednesday the twenty-first. **The price is named on the Tuesday evening. The bar is read out loud at the boat. Nobody is in the water.** The outer marks are two baulks of green timber with a ring of stone and a can on a stake, and three bearings agree with a chart of about thirty years standing to within a cable's length. **And then the man of the second lay stands up and shows them the bar: it is not a fence and there is no post in it, it is a line of about a mile and a half on which the water darkens and stands up in a low sea, and any man in a boat can see it and any man on a mole cannot.** **The three hundred and fifty-two pence bought the fact that nothing on that ground has changed, and that is a fact and it is in the first column.**
8. **278 — the fortieth charge, and a fish market. PAID.** Thursday the twenty-second. The fortieth charge, walked on none. **No person of that yard is in that market and nobody is sent.** A woman of about fifty-eight with the end stall asks one question in about forty people's hearing — **is a person allowed to burn a thing like that** — and is answered in the words of a method, about a thing that is not glass, in a place with no glass and no bench and no oath in it. **What it cost is a certificate of method and the standing of a certificate in a market: a method's words said in a market are a story told by a woman who used to be certified, and the certificate is not withdrawn and cannot be, because she is of no office and the office that keeps the copy is a building with a door on it and no person behind the counter, and the copy is in a drawer in a town four days up this coast. And what she said was true, and nobody in that market was able to tell whether it was true or not, and that is the whole of the price.**
9. **279 — three dates, and three marks. PAID.** Friday the twenty-third. A letter of one page, in a young hand, signed **Wend Brace, thirty, and Ilse Brace, nineteen**, at the address of the third of April. It asks for nothing and **its three dates are kept apart**: the twentieth, the twenty-first, the twenty-second. **A hand hired by the day at three marks was out of a day's work on the Wednesday because he stood in his own doorway for about ten minutes and did not pick up a sheet off his step; the daughter read it out to him on the Thursday and he had it read twice and he cannot read and the letter says so in those words. The three marks is the boat's man's figure and not this yard's and the boat's man is not named, and it is in the second column because the day after that somebody is going to say to an office that this yard has taken a man's wage off him.** And the refusal: **nobody sent, no money sent, and the three marks are not going to be, and the reason is not that the yard has not got them — the day this yard pays that man three marks he is a man this yard has paid, and this yard put a page in his daughter's mouth in the autumn without asking him and has an arrangement with nothing.**
10. **280 — the close. PAID.** Saturday the twenty-fourth. The far bench is occupied from ten until about four and is not approached. **The leaf is read back in full: twelve entries in the first column at the read-back, being three on the fourteenth of April past and nine since, one for every day from the fifteenth to the twenty-third and no day in two of them, and thirteen at the close with that day's own entry in it; forty-eight lines in the second being seven plus thirty-two plus nine, none in the third, and eleven in the fourth.** **The shipwright says that five of the forty-eight are refusals and that in about four years a man in a city will read that book and say that this yard never did anything, and that it will be the wrong shape of right, and that there is no column in that book for the saying of it.** And then the turn, once: **a house is not a place a thing is safe in; it is a place a person cannot refuse anybody anything about; a drawer is a house, a yard is a house, this shed is a house; and the price of that is a man of thirty who cannot read, a woman of about fifty-eight with a drawer under her bed, and a girl of nineteen — and both of those are ours, and neither of them is money, and we are not going to see either of them again unless we write, and we are not going to write.** And then, for Monday: **a woman in this harbor has told forty people in a market that a keeper is a function, and about sixty boats on this coast have a sheet in them that says where every other copy is, and in about two months those two things are going to meet in a place where neither of them is us.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 280

- **Calder and Nessa.** **They lost two arguments in three days and won one.** She read the form's head and said that the word in it is *house* and the word in the four lines is *record*, and he read the four lines and said the yard did it itself on the third of April. She refused to copy four other people's lines into the yard's own book and gave a reason that stopped him. She refused to put a figure for the boat's man's day in the first column and gave a reason that stopped him. **And in the end she said out loud that five of the forty-eight lines in the second column are refusals and that a man in four years will say that this yard never did anything, and that it will be the wrong shape of right, and that there is no column in that book for the saying of it, and he said that is what we have got.** Nothing in this batch is romantic and everything in it is expensive.
- **Calder and Mara Venn.** **She was asked by a person and not by a yard, on the fourteenth of April he swore he would not, and he asked her on the fifteenth and broke his own undertaking out loud to do it. He did not thank her. He did not ask her for anything else. She stood in that shed on six of the ten days and was asked for nothing.** The concealment was not told and is not due; her forty marks stand first after food and were not mentioned once in the ten days. **And the geography is settled: she is of this harbor, thirty, a person of no office since the fourth of January past, and the wrong second-column line of the fourth of April stands on the page with the correction against it.**
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** Occupied on three of the ten days, being the sixteenth, the twentieth and the twenty-fourth, and not occupied at any hour on the other seven; **not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story**; **the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten days and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** **Nothing was put on that bench and read as a gift. Tobias Wren is not on a page in this batch and was not sent for, and nothing in these ten days made him a teacher and nothing made him a door.**
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, his hand at the head of it. **He was not on the stone on any of the ten days and came down on none of them, was put on nothing, and was not asked one word about the omissions he has entered, and no name of his is in any column of that book and none has ever been.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty who cannot read.** **The batch's verdict, on the page.** This yard wrote to him on the third of April and got no answer, and posted a form at his address on the eighteenth, and the cost of that is an afternoon on the twentieth, a day of three marks on the twenty-first, and a season's peace, and the yard sent nobody and paid nothing and is not going to, and **the reason is that a man this yard has paid is a man this yard can be asked about.** He is a man of this yard in about forty people's hearing and is not one, and he is now the price of the volume's own solution, and this yard does not see him again.
- **Calder and the woman of fifty-eight.** **A stranger and not a page of anything, and she is the batch's last image.** She has a will and a marriage lines and a sealed paper in a drawer under her bed and she is afraid, and nobody has said one word to her, and this yard is not going to write to her.
- **Calder and Elias Voke, Garrow Fisk, Ors Kest, Amos Searle, the man of about thirty-one of the third lay, and the bellwright.** **Unmoved. Not asked anything, asked nothing, and not sent for.** The man of about thirty-one is on the page twice and on both occasions only to say that he is not going to be found, and the second column says why.

### The power state

**LINE DIVER. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN VOLUME 06 AND NONE IN THIS BATCH. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, NOT IMPROVED AND NOT RENAMED. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED, AND ITS SEASON OF NINE MARKS IS NOT PAID.** What this batch paid is the cost of the perception in ordinary work, and it paid it once and named it: **he lost the morning of Tuesday the twentieth and stood at the bench outside that shed until about one with a cup of water and no more, and said the only sentence anybody in that harbor has ever used for it, and nobody asked him a second.** **The standing fact is unchanged: a join identifies difference and not truth, and nothing in these ten chapters settled an argument, proved a motive or told anybody what happened. A mark, a line of white water, a chain, a bar of iron and a form with a name on it are all things a man can go and look at, and not one of them is a join, and not one of them said anything.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** One morning of the twentieth is lost to it, entered in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure, because there is no figure for a day. **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, still nameless, not struck out, and in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is nineteen marks, four shillings and ninepence, being three thousand and ninety-seven pence, and it was twenty-four marks, seven shillings and sevenpence, being three thousand nine hundred and thirty-one pence, on the morning of the fifteenth.** The whole of what came into that yard in the ten days is **nothing**, and that is also the whole of what has come into it since the sixth of December past, being the eleven marks of the sixth of April last, **and nothing has come into that yard on any of the ten days and nothing is going to.** The whole of what went out in the ten days is **eight hundred and thirty-four pence, being five marks, two shillings and tenpence**, being a penny, a day at the face of the second seam at four hundred and eighty pence, a penny, and three hundred and fifty-two pence for a boat and a man. The whole of what has gone out since the sixth of December past is **sixty-five marks, one shilling and eightpence in twenty-one transactions at seven counters**. **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS DOES NOT EXIST AND DID NOT EXIST ON ANY OF THESE TEN DAYS, and will not come back while that bag is above six hundred and forty pence, and nobody in that shed said one word about it at any hour of any of them.**
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY-SIX weeks have now fallen due with no envelope standing against them, the last of them being the twenty-sixth, which fell due on the twentieth, and the next is the twenty-seventh of April, which will be the twenty-seventh week, and the column will not move on that either.**
- **The slate wall came down bare once in the ten days, being the fiftieth Monday since the first of May, on the nineteenth of April, the counter not restarting and the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting was held in that room on any day of this book.**
- **The cistern was charged at no figure on three rota days, being the fifteenth, the nineteenth and the twenty-second of April, and this party walked none of them, being the thirty-eighth, thirty-ninth and fortieth of the charges walked on none since the third of August past. The walk is nil and it stays nil, and no figure was entered against a day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.**
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the sixteenth, the twentieth and the twenty-fourth of April, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for the eighty-fourth night.** The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and seventeen days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the ten days.
- **SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE CHARTER'S PLACE IS EMPTY, AND A FORM OF AN OFFICE THAT YARD DOES NOT BELONG TO IS IN THE ORDINARY POST AND IS ON A STEP TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, AND IT IS NOT IN THE DRAWER AND WAS NOT IN IT FOR AN HOUR, BECAUSE A DRAWER IS A HOUSE.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved, nobody sent. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, and he was not asked anything in these ten days and the chest was not opened. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure, in no sentence with the bed at Ashtide and in no sentence with a certificate. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, neither reduced and neither paid, and not mentioned once. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed with the boy's hand at the head of it. **NINE FEET OF CHAIN ON A NAIL IN THAT SHED WALL AND A BAR OF SQUARE IRON TWO FEET LONG IN THE DRAWER, neither measured nor cleaned since the ninth of April, and NEITHER SOLD AND NEITHER GIVEN AWAY — A SHILLING WAS OFFERED FOR THE CHAIN ON THE TWENTIETH AND WAS REFUSED — AND NOBODY HAS ASKED WHOSE EITHER IS.**
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND A PRACTICE AND IS NOT A REGISTRY AND IS NOT A COURT AND IS NOT A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH PAST AND IS NOT AGED BY THIS BATCH, AND ITS FOUR LINES ARE ABOUT A RECORD AND NOT ABOUT A HOUSE, AND THIS YARD LEANED ON THEM AS IF THEY WERE ABOUT A HOUSE FOR FORTY-TWO DAYS.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the movement's own ten of them:** a form with a name and an address on it, read on a bench and squared with both hands; **a keeper in a town two days down that coast, who is not an officer and did not attend a service because there was no service to attend;** the serving of it by being left; a person of no office asked by a person and not by a yard; a market scene in about forty people's hearing; four refusals, each with a reason against the line; **and the turn, which is that a page in a drawer in a house is custody an office can reach, and that the four lines four people wrote in March are about a record and are not about a house, and that the price of the volume's own solution is now somebody else's problem.**

**Still owed and carried into Chapter 281:** the volume's question, four hundred miles west under seventy fathoms, and the method for reading it, which this yard has and cannot use; **THE WORD *QUIETENING*, WHICH IS NAMED IN CHAPTER 281 AND NOWHERE EARLIER IN THIS VOLUME, IN A CHARACTER'S MOUTH, AND THE WORD *CROWN SEAL*, WHICH IS NOT NAMED IN MOVEMENT 4 AT ALL AND MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291;** the man of about thirty-one of the third lay and his Crown chart; the four pages in four drawers this yard cannot look in; the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, **THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN, FOR A THIRD VOLUME**; the case of five bells, on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of that coast wrote and signed; the delayed note at eleven and two and a hand's width of a second; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road and the two figures and the Kettle; **THE CONCEALMENT, WHICH WAS TOLD ONCE IN CHAPTER 38 OF VOLUME 01 AND IS OWED TO THIS VOLUME AND WAS NOT TOLD IN ANY OF THESE THIRTY CHAPTERS;** the certificate of method whose standing was spent on the twenty-second of April past and which no later chapter may say was restored; **THE FORM ON A STEP IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, WHICH NO LATER CHAPTER MAY SAY WAS WITHDRAWN OR UNSERVED;** and the new-volume question, which is who first used a seal to turn emergency custody into permanent ownership, and is not asked yet.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the complaint against the four people of that coast, which was refused on the eleventh of March and refused again on the twenty-seventh and is not to be raised in this volume, **and the fact that this batch found a made floor four hundred miles from where they keep their page was not used as a reason to ask them**; the going out of the second of May, which is spent; the plate note, which is not paid by a better letter; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the compact's name; the certificate, which cannot be restored and is not going to be asked about; **THE QUIETENING, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 281, AND THE CROWN SEAL, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291, AND NEITHER OF WHICH IS NAMED IN ANY OF THESE THIRTY CHAPTERS.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A WORKING HARBOR OF THAT COAST IS POORER ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH DAY OF APRIL THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, A HARBOR AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED WITH NOTHING ISSUED, A TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT, A MAN OF TWENTY-EIGHT IS IN A BED AT ASHTIDE FOR FIVE WEEKS, A MAN OF FIFTY-ONE HAS LOST ABOUT A HALF OF A SEASON'S GEAR AND HIS GROUND IS STILL SHUT, A YARD HAS SPENT FIVE MARKS, TWO SHILLINGS AND TENPENCE IN TEN DAYS AND EARNED NOTHING, AND IS CARRYING A CHAIN ON A NAIL IT CANNOT SELL AND A BAR IN A DRAWER IT CANNOT GIVE AWAY AND A FORM IN A POST BAG IT CANNOT GET BACK, AND HAS AN ADDRESS IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST IT DID NOT WANT, AND A DRAWER UNDER A BED IN THIS HARBOR IT CANNOT HELP, AND THE ANSWER IS FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST, AND IN ABOUT TWO MONTHS A WORD SAID IN A FISH MARKET AND A SHEET IN ABOUT SIXTY BOATS ARE GOING TO MEET IN A PLACE WHERE NEITHER OF THEM IS THAT YARD.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 270

**MOVEMENT 2 OF VOLUME 06 IS COMPLETE AND ITS TURN IS PAID. THE VOLUME'S QUESTION HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE ANSWERABLE AND THIS PARTY HAS BEEN FOUND TO BE THE WRONG PARTY FOR IT. A DESCENT WAS BOUGHT AND NOT FOUND, IT WENT TO FORTY FATHOOMS IN A TRENCH OFF THE SOUTH END, IT COST A POT, THREE DAYS OF A CROWN HOUSE'S AIR AND A MAN'S SEASON, AND IT BROUGHT UP A THING THAT IS NOT A RECORD AND A PERSON WHO IS NOT A WITNESS. THREE DAYS ON WHICH A PERSON OF THAT YARD WENT INTO THE WATER WERE ENTERED IN THAT YARD'S OWN FIRST COLUMN WITH THE REASON AGAINST THE LINE AND THE PRICE NAMED BEFOREHAND, BECAUSE THERE IS NO OTHER BOOK TO ENTER THEM IN, AND THAT IS THE VOLUME'S PROBLEM AND IT WAS PAID AND NOT RENAMED.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **261 — the rate, and the cut. PAID.** Monday the fifth of April. The forty-eighth wipe, the thirty-fifth charge walked on none, and nothing in or out. **GARROW FISK NAMES THE CROWN HOUSE RATE OUT LOUD ON THE MOLE STEPS IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE'S HEARING: nine marks a day for the compressor, the housing, the pipe, the gauges and one man off a Crown house book; two marks and eightpence a day for his own time; a mark and two shillings a day for a hand on the hose, the rate the 28 September 2026 review corrected on the page and which this file had not taken up; thirty-six marks and eight shillings for three days. NOBODY IN THAT HEARING SAID IT WAS SMALL.** His condition is not caution and it is not about what is under a diver's feet; it is about a line, and the cut is therefore a cut in a line made above the water — a bight rove through a shackle, the two ends on the crown, the bight cut on the surface. **NESSA PIKE MAKES THE THREE TURNS ON THE WATER SIDE, AGAINST THAT YARD'S OWN PRACTICE, BECAUSE A SHACKLE ON THE FACE OF THE SECOND SEAM HAS THREE TURNS ON THE WATER SIDE, AND THE FOURTH COLUMN GETS ITS SECOND LINE.** And **ELIAS VOKE, FIFTY-ONE, OF THE *ANNA RAY* OF THE SECOND LAY, COMES UP WITH HIS NET HUNG AT FORTY FATHOOMS AND A MILE AND A HALF OF GROUND SHUT AGAINST SIX BOATS, AND OFFERS ELEVEN MARKS BEFORE ANY PRICE HAS BEEN SPOKEN OF.**
2. **262 — the first money in twenty-three days. PAID.** Tuesday the sixth of April. The twenty-fourth week falls due and the column does not move, and the holder of that writ **corrects his own sentence of the thirtieth of March in the open and asks that the old one not be struck out.** Voke pays eleven marks, counted twice and read back and counted back. The set is engaged for the eighth, ninth and tenth, **Fisk says out loud that he wrote the yard's name on a sheet and not in the Crown house book, and that a Crown house book has a column for a depth and no column for a year, a name or a reason, and enters that himself, unsigned.** And the form for unsettled material enters as legal pressure: **this yard became an address on the third of April, and an address is a thing that can be given to a man who is going somewhere.**
3. **263 — the cut, and the book that is not there. PAID.** Wednesday the seventh of April. A shackle of that yard's own iron, three turns on the water side, **a serving half a turn out of true, entered in the fourth column and not the first because a thing which is not is not a thing a man did.** A man of twenty-six hired at a mark and two shillings a day. **THE SIX CONDITIONS READ ALOUD AT THE BOAT, NO FIRST ENTRY AND NOTHING TO ENTER, AND THEN THE SENTENCE THAT LANDS L22: THERE IS NO HARBOR AUTHORITY'S BOOK TO GO IN, AND THAT YARD'S OWN BOOK IS NOT THAT BOOK AND IS NOT THE SAME THING.** **AND THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY ASKS HOW FAR OFF THE GROUND IS AND FISK ANSWERS IT BEFORE HE HAS FINISHED ASKING: THE OUTER MARKS ARE A MILE AND A QUARTER OFF THE HEAD OF THAT MOLE, THE BAR IS FOUR HUNDRED YARDS OFF THE OUTER MARKS, THE BAR BEGINS ABOUT A MILE AND A HALF OUT ON THAT LINE, AND THE CUT IS OFF THE SOUTH END AND ROUND THE CORNER FROM ALL OF IT, AND NOBODY HAS NARROWED THAT BAR AND THIS PARTY IS NOT GOING TO ASK, AND HE ASKS FOR IT TO BE SAID AGAIN IN THE BOAT AND BEFORE THE TWO MEN GO DOWN.** The pot is charged to **eighty-four pounds on a face of a hundred and fifty**, and a pencil mark is left on the face where the needle stood, and eighty-four is not near the end of it. **AND THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS CEASES TO EXIST, AND NOBODY SAID A WORD ABOUT IT.**
4. **264 — the forty fathoms. PAID.** Thursday the eighth of April. The thirty-sixth charge walked on none. A day of work done and not booked, because there is no paper to book it against. **The two ends of the bight are cut on the surface at about eleven with a man at forty fathoms and nothing on the surface of the earth holding anything.** And the bottom is not a quarry: **it is a laid floor in courses with a figure cut at the near end of every course, running from one to forty-one without a break, and a socket in the top course with a bar of iron in it and a chain made to the bar, and a net hung across thirty feet of it.** He comes up with a figure he cannot get out of his hand, and nobody asks him what he means.
5. **265 — the net. PAID.** Friday the ninth of April. The warp comes off the bar, the bar comes out of the socket, **and the net comes up, slow and wide and all at once, and takes Amos Searle up about eleven feet into the edge of a course of squared stone.** He says one thing and asks for it in his own words: a net that has been hung eleven days comes up slow, and if he had known it he would have gone under it and not beside it. **Fisk says on the crown of the mole in about a hundred people's hearing that the shoulder is not out and is gone, and that the book carries the man as unfit for five weeks and then as fit for light work, and that the word light is his house's word and he has never been able to make a man light.** The day is a waste and everybody says so.
6. **266 — the third day, and the bill. PAID.** Saturday the tenth of April. **A Crown house sent a man, Hesk Ottrim, thirty-one, up on the Friday night in a coach that took fourteen hours, at the book's own figure, and he says out loud that he asked for the job.** Two hundred and eight fathoms of net come up out of four hundred and eleven, with eleven of eleven floats and the head rope entire, **and the belly is still down and the middle was the money.** **The Crown house book came up the road on the Friday night in the same coach that brought the second man, and at about seven on the Saturday morning, with the door open and about four people in the street and the market not up, FISK READS THE ENTRY OUT, and the word light is his house's word and there is no light work in a holder's trade, and the ship's hand enters the four lines in the second column in his words and the figure in no column.** Fisk names his travel at one mark and fourpence a day for six days and counts it out on the front step in front of about eleven people, and says the fortnight before was his own and is not going on that book, **and then goes in that boat to Ashtide and is away from the eleventh to the fifteenth, as he said out loud on the step.** **The bill goes out as three separate figures — a boat to a hospital at Ashtide, a man's fee, a week's keep of a bed — and Fisk goes in that boat on his own account and says so, and there is no figure for it and there is not going to be one.** Nine feet of chain and a two-foot bar are in that shed.
7. **267 — the chain, the boy, and the lost day. PAID.** Sunday the eleventh of April. **The chain is hung on a nail and lies on the floor, and a man of the second lay says it is not chain that came off a boat and that he would not take it if he could.** The boy comes down on his own account, is put on nothing, and says one thing: **the second column is getting full, and it was not getting full in the spring.** **The man of the second lay asks the ship's hand for the figure in the bag, is given it out loud, is told that it is not a third of what the job cost, asks for it to be written on the front of the shed, is refused and is given the reason against the refusal, and says that is fair, and does not ask again.** **The holder of that writ loses the day to the body** and says the only sentence anybody in that harbor has ever used for it, **and the fourth line of the fourth column is dictated at the bench and written by the ship's hand in her own left hand.**
8. **268 — the bearing, and the mole's foot. PAID.** Monday the twelfth of April. The forty-ninth wipe, the thirty-seventh charge walked on none. **He cannot hold a slate and can hold a compass, and a bearing of north-west by west, about two hundred and seventy, taken four times off the crown of the mole and once in a boat along the courses on the floor, IS THE SAME LINE AS THE BEARING OF THE CROWN OF THAT MOLE ON A SHEET ROLLED BEHIND THE TIDE TABLE IN THAT SHED. THE MOLE HAS A FOOT AT FORTY FATHOOMS AND THE FOOT IS NOT RUBBLE ON A SLOPE.** And then nothing is done about it: nobody is sent for, nothing is written, nothing goes on a wall, and the reason is that a refusal is better than a sheet. Fisk does the arithmetic of seventy fathoms and says the third part of it is not a number and is who owns a machine.
9. **269 — the turn, argued twice and badly. PAID.** Tuesday the thirteenth of April. The twenty-fifth week falls due and the column does not move. **Voke says out loud that he will not pay the difference and why.** And the four sentences: **the floor is not about the fleet, the floor is not the answer, the floor is the method, and this party is the wrong party for it** — said twice, both attempts left standing in the first column. The two depths and the one bearing go in the first column, where a man can check them, and the rest goes in the second.
10. **270 — the close. PAID.** Wednesday the fourteenth of April. The leaf read back in full: **three entries in the first column, seven lines in the second, none in the third, and six in the fourth, being the lines of the fourteenth of May and of the fifth, the seventh, the eleventh, the thirteenth and the fourteenth of April.** The third column is empty, nobody is appointed to it, the boy's hand is at the head of it. The turn in four sentences and no more, and the form for unsettled material at the end of it: **a form is served by being left at an address, the price of that is a person's afternoon and their fear, and this yard is not going to be the reason.** The whole standing inventory, once.

She made the cut wrong on purpose and defended it in front of a man of a pressure house. Nothing in this batch is romantic and everything in it is expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** A man of sixty-one at a far bench, **occupied on three of the ten days, being the tenth, the twelfth and the fourteenth of April, and not occupied at any hour on the other seven**; not asked for anything on any of them, asking nothing on any of them, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and **Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the ten days and was in that harbor on all ten and up no coast road on any of them.** **NOBODY NAMED HIM AS THE ANSWER TO ANYTHING IN THIS BATCH, AND THE NOT-NAMING CARRIES THE REASON OF THE SECOND OF APRIL FORWARD UNCHANGED AND UNIMPROVED: A MAN ASKED ON A MOLE WHETHER HE CUTS ANSWERS IT WITH A PRICE, AND A PRICE ANSWERED TO A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF A PRESSURE HOUSE IS A THING THIS YARD WOULD THEN HAVE TO PAY, AND IT HAS NOT GOT, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO ASK A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE WHAT HE WILL TAKE. - **Calder and Amos Searle.** **Three days, one of them in the water, and then a net.** He asked for the gas to be called twice and it was. - **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, the boy's hand at the head of it. **He came down once on the eleventh on his own account, was put on nothing, was not asked one word about the omissions he has entered, and said that the second column is getting full.**

He was not asked anything and asked nothing, and the batch's nearest temptation — using a bearing or a floor as a reason to go and find the man with the Crown chart — was refused on the page on the twelfth.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH.** The body is charged: **one day lost on the eleventh of April, entered in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure, because there is no figure for a day, and the reason is the reason that has been against that line on every lost day since the sixth of October past.** **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, still nameless, not struck out, and in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is twenty-four marks, seven shillings and sevenpence, being three thousand nine hundred and thirty-one pence, and it was sixty-five marks and threepence, being ten thousand four hundred and three pence, on the morning of the fifth of April.** The whole of what came into that yard in the ten days is **eleven marks**, and that is also the whole of what has come into it since the sixth of December, because nothing came in at all after the fourteenth of March. The whole of what went out in the ten days is **fifty-one marks and six shillings**, being 8,232 pence, and the whole of what has gone out since the sixth of December is **fifty-nine marks, twelve shillings and twopence in seventeen transactions at six counters**, which is the figure every chapter from the tenth to the fourteenth now carries, **and eleven marks is one thousand seven hundred and sixty pence and has been printed as one thousand seven hundred and seventy-six in four chapters and is now right in all of them.** **THE FIGURE THE BAG IS SHORT OF THE WAGE OF FOUR MARKS DOES NOT EXIST AND HAS NOT SINCE THE SEVENTH OF APRIL, and nobody in that shed said one word about it at the time.**
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY-FIVE weeks have now fallen due with no envelope standing against them.** Two wages of four marks were not paid in these ten days, on the sixth and the thirteenth of April, and the column did not move on either and the envelopes did not move.
- **The slate wall came down bare twice, being the forty-eighth and the forty-ninth Mondays since the first of May, on the fifth and the twelfth of April, the counter not restarting and the clerk keeping his own page, and no sitting was held in that room on any day of this book.**
- **The cistern was charged at no figure on three rota days and this party walked none of them, being the thirty-fifth, thirty-sixth and thirty-seventh of the charges walked on none since the third of August past. The walk is nil and it stays nil. No figure was entered against any day that is not a Monday or a Thursday.**
- **The far bench is occupied on three of the ten days, being the tenth, the twelfth and the fourteenth of April, and was not occupied at any hour on the other seven, and the holder of that writ did not go over to him on any of the ten.**
- **The bench under that pump is bare for a seventy-fourth night, counting from the Sunday of the thirty-first of January, and it is the only bare thing in that shed.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about three hundred and seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the ten days.**
- **SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE CHARTER'S PLACE IS EMPTY. NOTHING IN A TIN SINCE THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF APRIL. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to that harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, and he was not asked anything in these ten days and the chest was not opened. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of that harbor with her name on the figure, and that is in no sentence with the bed at Ashtide. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, and nothing was asked of her and nothing was written back. Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed with the boy's hand at the head of it, and he was not on the stone on any of the ten days. NINE FEET OF CHAIN ON A NAIL IN THAT SHED AND A BAR OF SQUARE IRON TWO FEET LONG IN THE DRAWER, AND NOBODY CAN USE THE CHAIN AND NOBODY WOULD TAKE IT, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED WHOSE EITHER IS.**
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND A PRACTICE AND IS NOT A REGISTRY, A COURT OR A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH AND IS NOT AGED BY THIS BATCH.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the movement's own ten of them:** the air, and its Crown house rate, said out loud; a cut made above the water on a bench; a descent to forty fathoms bought and not found; a pot, three days and a body; a mole with a foot at the bottom of it; a chain that is not a record; a man in a bed at Ashtide; **and the turn, which is that the volume's question is answerable and this party is the wrong party for it.**

**Still owed and carried into Chapter 271:** the volume's question, which is now known to be answerable and is four hundred miles west under seventy fathoms; **the form for unsettled material, which is a form and not a favour, has never been served on anybody, and is now attached to an address, because this yard wrote a letter to a man who cannot read and became an address on the third of April;** the man of about thirty-one of the third lay and his Crown chart; the four pages in four drawers this yard cannot look in; the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN, for a third volume; the case of five bells, on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of that coast wrote and signed; the delayed note at eleven and two and a hand's width of a second; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road and the two figures and the Kettle; **THE CONCEALMENT, WHICH WAS TOLD ONCE IN CHAPTER 38 OF VOLUME 01 AND IS OWED TO THIS VOLUME AND WAS NOT TOLD IN ANY OF THESE TWENTY CHAPTERS;** and the new-volume question, which is who first used a seal to turn emergency custody into permanent ownership, and is not asked yet.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the complaint against the four people of that coast, which was refused on the eleventh of March and refused again on the twenty-seventh and is not to be raised in this volume, and the batch found the method of laying stone four hundred miles from where those four people are and used it as no reason to ask them; the going out of the second of May, which is spent; the plate note, which is not paid by a better letter; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the compact's name; **THE QUIETENING, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 281, AND THE CROWN SEAL, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291, AND NEITHER OF WHICH IS NAMED IN ANY OF THESE TWENTY CHAPTERS.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A WORKING HARBOR OF THAT COAST IS POORER ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY OF APRIL THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, A HARBOR AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED WITH NOTHING ISSUED, A TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT, A MAN OF TWENTY-EIGHT IS IN A BED AT ASHTIDE FOR FIVE WEEKS BECAUSE A NET CAME UP ON HIM, A MAN OF FIFTY-ONE HAS LOST ABOUT A HALF OF A SEASON'S GEAR AND HIS GROUND IS STILL SHUT, AND A YARD HAS BOUGHT THREE DAYS OF A CROWN HOUSE'S AIR AND LOST FORTY MARKS AND SIX SHILLINGS DOING IT, AND IS CARRYING A CHAIN ON A NAIL THAT IT CANNOT SELL AND CANNOT GIVE AWAY, AND THE ANSWER IS FOUR HUNDRED MILES WEST.**

## Volume 06, Batch 0002 summary (Chapters 261–270) — the story state at the end of Chapter 270

**Movement 2 is written. The air has a price, the cut is made on a bench above the water, the descent went to forty fathoms and cost a pot, three days and a body, and the batch's turn is the volume's turn: the question is answerable and this party is the wrong party for it.** In ten days a fireman of a pressure house named a Crown house rate out loud in front of nine people and would not pretend it was small; a shipwright made a shackle wrong on purpose and wrote down why; a skipper of fifty-one lost the middle of his net, offered eleven marks before anybody had mentioned a price, refused to be argued up, and said out loud that he would not pay the difference; a descent went to forty fathoms in a trench off the south end on a line that was cut on the surface with a man at the bottom; a net came up on a man of twenty-eight and put him into a stone course and into a bed at Ashtide for five weeks; a bearing of north-west by west about two hundred and seventy was taken off a crown of a mole and found to be the same line as the bearing of the crown of that mole, which means the mole has a laid and numbered foot at forty fathoms a mile and a half out; and a boy of twenty-two stood in a shed door and said that the second column is getting full.

**THE BATCH'S MIDPOINT IS CHAPTER 265 AND ITS CLIMAX IS CHAPTER 270.** The chapters before 265 are a price agreed and a cut made and a book that is not there. Chapter 265 is where the work costs a body. Chapter 270 is where the turn is paid, in four sentences, and the whole standing inventory is carried once.

**THE BATCH'S COST, AND IT IS THE HOUSE'S OWN KIND: ELEVEN MARKS IN AND FIFTY-ONE MARKS AND SIX SHILLINGS OUT, so a net loss of forty marks and six shillings; a wage column that did not move on two Tuesdays; twenty-five weeks fallen due; a day lost to the body on the eleventh; a man of twenty-eight unfit for five weeks from the ninth of April; a bed at Ashtide paid a week and not a second; and a man of fifty-one who will not be hired again this season and will not be thanked.**

## Where the story is at the end of Chapter 260

**MOVEMENT 1 OF VOLUME 06 IS COMPLETE AND ITS TURN IS PAID. THE VOLUME'S CENTRAL PRESSURE IS A PARTY WITH NO INSTRUMENT OF ANY KIND. THE VOLUME'S QUESTION HAS BEEN ASKED ONCE, AT A MOLE HEAD, IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, AND HAS NOT BEEN ANSWERED. NOTHING WAS FOUND, NOTHING WAS RAISED, NOBODY WENT IN THE WATER, AND FOURTEEN DAYS OF THE TWENTY WERE SPENT FINDING OUT THAT A THING ON THE BOTTOM HAD BEEN HANDLED BY SOMEBODY WHO IS NOT THE YARD.**

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **251 — the instrument is gone. PAID.** Tuesday the sixteenth, Wednesday the seventeenth of March. **The ship's hand counts the drawer twice and comes out with six pieces of paper and finds that the charter's place is empty and clean and the wood is a slightly different colour where a thing had been lying on it for four months.** She reads the form of the fourth of March from the top to the bottom and finds that the whole of it asks this yard for nothing, and then does the arithmetic: a hirer at the second seam pays for a piece of paper and the paper is not here, so there is no day to sell. **FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE SIXTH OF OCTOBER A WORKING DAY CANNOT BE BOOKED AT ALL, and the twenty-first week falls due on a Tuesday on which no envelope is made.** The boat of about forty tons is hired at a mark and eightpence because the man of the second lay will not go out past a fouled mark with a hand short, and at the mark there are two bright places on the shackle the size of a thumbnail.
2. **252 — the boat that is not the yard's. PAID.** Thursday the eighteenth, Friday the nineteenth. The cistern is charged on the Thursday and walked on none, being the thirtieth. **TOBIAS WREN, SIXTY-ONE, HALF DEAF, WHO HAS NOT BEEN ON A PAGE SINCE VOLUME 02, COMES UP THE MOLE BECAUSE HE HEARD ON SATURDAY AT A FISH MARKET THAT A MARK WAS FOULED AND SAYS HE DID NOT COME UP TO BE ASKED.** He asks one question and it is who is paying, and he names his terms before any of them is asked for: six marks a day for the boat whatever the month, a hand of about forty called Ruad paid separate by the day, and fuel at what fuel costs. **He says he will not be a teacher, and that in thirty-one years by another man's account nobody ever asked him what was in a thing he went into and he has never said, and that the last time he took a wreck apart there was nothing in the frame he could carry and a thing on the bottom that would have fitted in his coat, and he went home.** No boat of his was hired and no six marks was paid.
3. **253 — nineteen days. PAID.** Saturday the twentieth, Sunday the twenty-first. **THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT COMES UP THE COAST ROAD IN ANOTHER MAN'S CART, NINETEEN DAYS AFTER HE WENT UP IT, THINNER, WITH A FOREARM THAT HAS A SHAPE TO IT, AND READS THE FORM OF THE FOURTH OF MARCH IN FOUR MINUTES STANDING AND SAYS THERE IS NOTHING IN IT HE COULD NOT HAVE SAID OUT LOUD ON A MOLE.** He brings back four lines in a hand that is not his own and not hers — two of a place, one of a month nobody here uses, and one sentence — **and the sentence is that four people will not send a man to a coast where the man who writes things down is the one everybody remembers, and he had asked them once for a witness alive who had been on that water and was refused three times before the sentence was read to him.** The far bench is occupied on the Sunday from ten until four and **he did not go over to him at any hour of the day, and said the reason out loud to a doorframe, and asked that the words go in the book and not the reason.** Four days lost to the body on the road, in the second column, with no figure.
4. **254 — the forty-sixth wipe, and the shackle. PAID.** Monday the twenty-second, Tuesday the twenty-third. **THE WALL BEHIND THE REEVE'S BENCH CAME DOWN BARE FOR THE FORTY-SIXTH TIME SINCE THE FIRST OF MAY, THE COUNTER DID NOT RESTART, THE CLERK KEPT HIS OWN PAGE, AND A CLERK OF THAT HARBOR AUTHORITY SAID OUT LOUD THAT THE STANDING INSTRUCTION IS A WIPE EVERY MONDAY AT EIGHT WHETHER THERE IS A SITTING OR NOT, AND THAT HE HAS A PAGE OF DATES AND WOULD NOT GIVE IT TO ANYBODY WHO HAD NOT ASKED.** The cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-first. **The holder offers to take the slate and is refused by the ship's hand on the ground that a private hire of a boat is not a place to put a man in the water, and he says so first and asks for it entered.** At the mark: three bright places and not two, the Wednesday's two not struck out, a shackle that has been off the frame and back on the wrong way up, and a wire cut and mended with three turns on the water side of a frame where this yard turns on the landward side. The twenty-second week falls due and the column does not move.
5. **255 — what fouling says. PAID.** Wednesday the twenty-fourth, Thursday the twenty-fifth, and the cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-second. **A MAN OF THE SECOND LAY WITH NINETEEN YEARS IN THE WATER READS THE SLATE AND GIVES FOUR THINGS IN ORDER: A SEASON FOR GROWTH, BEING NINE WEEKS IN A HARD YEAR AND ELEVEN IN A SOFT ONE; BRIGHT IRON FOR A HAND INSIDE A FORTNIGHT; A SPANNER AND A MORNING FOR A MENDED CUT; AND THAT NONE OF THOSE THREE KNOWS A NAME AND ANYBODY WHO SAYS WHICH OF FOUR PEOPLE DID IT IS SELLING.** He says all four of them out loud at the head of that dock in eleven people's hearing and asks that it be entered that he said no word about the four people four days down that coast and is not going to. **He also says that a mark with two parties in it gets a wire through in the dark by a man with no lights, and that he has seen two of them off the Sill in his first year and does not know the names of either and is not going to be asked.** The limit four people of that coast wrote and signed is quoted in the first column and stands.
6. **256 — a line, a flat, and four columns. PAID.** Friday the twenty-sixth, Saturday the twenty-seventh. **THE FOULING IS A FOOT INSTEAD OF FOUR INCHES; THERE IS A FOUR-STRAND UNTARRED LINE TIED WITH A SHEET BEND; AND THE SHACKLE HAS A QUARTER-INCH FLAT ON THE CROWN OF THE BOW THAT THE SEA DOES NOT MAKE, AND THE SHIP'S HAND NAMES THE MAKE BECAUSE SHE HAS MADE THE OTHER ONE, AND THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY SAYS THERE IS ONE SMITH ON THIS COAST WHO FINISHES THEM THAT WAY AND THAT HE IS SIXTY-EIGHT AND HAS A SHOP OFF THE YARD AT TERNWATCH.** Three things are said out loud with their prices before any of them is agreed: a cut, which wants a boat and a man and an instrument this yard has none of; a bigger mark, at four marks of iron, which is the only one it could pay for and the one it does not want; and a complaint, which is a name in a book in a town four days down that coast. **The holder wants the complaint, is refused, loses the argument to his own sentence of the eleventh of March, and asks that it be entered that he lost it to his own sentence and not to a better one.** **Saturday: a fourth leaf is ruled on the back of a sheet of chandler's paper with four columns — what was there, who saw it, what was done, and what it is not — the fourth head written with a blunt nib, and it does not go on any wall in that harbor and never will.**
7. **257 — the question, and not an answer. PAID.** Sunday the twenty-eighth, Monday the twenty-ninth, and the wall comes down bare for the forty-seventh time and the cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-third. **A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF THE THIRD LAY WITH A COASTER OUT OF ASHTIDE PUTS A CROWN CHART ON THE FISH QUAY WHERE ANYBODY CAN GET AT IT AND ASKS, IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE'S HEARING, WHETHER THE FLEET WAS SCUTTLED OR WHETHER IT WENT DOWN, AND GIVES HIS OWN SMALL REASON FOR WANTING TO KNOW.** The holder of that writ answers, badly, and knows it: three things, and a statement made before them that none of them is an answer — nobody in that harbor is old enough; the only thing that could answer it is at seventy fathoms about four hundred miles west-southwest of that mole and its name is not going to be said in a market; and this party holds no instrument of any kind. **The man calls it three numbers and a refusal and is told yes. He then asks one question, being whether the thirty-eighth line will be there in four years, and is told the honest thing, and calls that the answer.** Nothing of it was written down, and the reason is in the second column.
8. **258 — a season that ends with nothing issued. PAID.** Tuesday the thirtieth, Wednesday the thirty-first. The twenty-third week falls due and the column does not move, and it is the whole of that year's list. **THE REEVE GIVES THREE THINGS AND SAYS BEFORE GIVING THEM THAT A MAN WHO IS GIVEN THREE THINGS HAS NOT BEEN REFUSED THREE THINGS: NO INSTRUMENT AFTER THAT DAY, THE LEDGER BEING SPENT; THAT HIS OFFICE IS NOT THE OFFICE THAT CAN GIVE THE CHARTER BACK AND NEVER WAS, SAID A THIRD TIME BECAUSE A TRUE SENTENCE DOES NOT WEAR OUT; AND THE ONE THING IT CAN DO, WHICH IS TO SEAT TWO PEOPLE AND TAKE A FINDING AS IT IS GIVEN, AT A COST OF TWO CLERKS AND HIMSELF, ONE AFTERNOON A WEEK, IN A ROOM HE HAS TO BE WARM FOR.** The yard asks who the other side is and is told that the other side is a man of fifty of the second lay and a smith in Ternwatch who has never heard of the yard, and that seating either as a party would be inventing a proceeding to get at a name. **HE SAYS OUT LOUD THAT HE IS NOT A FRIEND OF THAT PARTY AND THAT THIS IS NOT A RESCUE, AND THE REASON HE SAYS IT IS SO THAT THE STORY WILL BE HARDER TO TELL IN A MONTH.** Nothing was written to the tide gang and nothing to the man of the second lay.
9. **259 — the air, and the condition. PAID.** Thursday the first, Friday the second of April. The cistern is charged and walked on none, being the thirty-fourth and last of this batch, and the third lay fills at seven in the morning with one berth short of two. **GARROW FISK, THIRTY-FOUR, OF A PRESSURE HOUSE AT TERNWATCH, COMES UP THE HILL WITH THAT YARD'S PRINTED SHEET FOLDED AT THE THIRTY-EIGHTH LINE AND SAYS HE IS NOT HERE ABOUT A JOB AND WANTS TO KNOW WHETHER THAT LINE IS TRUE, AND IS TOLD THAT IT IS.** He offers a compressor and a housing and a man off a Crown house book at a Crown house rate, will not pretend the figure is small and will not pretend that this party is a Crown hull, and sets one condition: **he will not go under anything that has not been cut, and that is not a rule in a book but what happened to a man he worked beside for nine years who is alive and does not go down at all now.** Two marks and eightpence a day, named before he was asked, and it was paid. Asked who cuts, the yard says it has not got a cutter, and the man sits on the top step for an hour and a half and is brought out a cup of water and no more. **NOBODY IN THAT SHED NAMED THE ONLY MAN IN THAT HARBOR WHO COULD, AND THE NOT-NAMING IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON.**
10. **260 — the batch's turn, and the close. PAID.** Saturday the third, Sunday the fourth. **A LETTER OF ONE PAGE ASKING NOTHING GOES INTO THE ORDINARY POST AT A PENNY FOR A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY WHO CANNOT READ IN A TOWN TWO DAYS DOWN THAT COAST, AND THE HOLDER OF THAT WRIT DOES NOT SIGN IT, GIVING AS THE SECOND OF HIS TWO REASONS THAT A NAME ON A PIECE OF PAPER ABOUT A MARK THAT TWO PARTIES HAVE A CLAIM TO, GOING TO A TOWN WHERE FOUR PEOPLE KEEP A PAGE IN A DRAWER, IS THIS YARD'S NAME IN AN OFFICE'S FILE IN ABOUT TWO YEARS; AND THE LETTER IS SIGNED AT THE FOOT IN THE HAND OF THE MAN OF THE SECOND LAY.** **A LETTER FROM A PERSON OF NO OFFICE CAME UP THE HILL ON THE FRIDAY AND SAYS ONE FACT AND ASKS FOR NOTHING: AN OFFICE SHE WORKED IN FOR NINE YEARS HAS A FORM FOR MATERIAL THAT OFFICE CALLS UNSETTLED, AND A PERSON WHO KEEPS UNSETTLED MATERIAL IN A HOUSE IS A KEEPER OF IT UNDER THAT FORM, AND WHETHER THAT MEANS A HOUSE OR A DRAWER OR A CUPBOARD THE FORM DOES NOT SAY, AND SHE HAS NOT SEEN IT SERVED ON ANYBODY AND CANNOT SAY WHAT IT DOES, AND SHE WILL COME IF A PERSON ASKS HER AND WILL NOT COME IF A YARD ASKS HER. NOTHING WAS ASKED OF HER AND NOTHING WAS WRITTEN BACK, AND NOT WRITING BACK IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST.** Sunday: the far bench is occupied from ten until four and is not approached. **THE FOURTH LEAF HAS ONE ENTRY IN ITS FIRST COLUMN AND ONE LINE IN ITS FOURTH: THE FOURTEENTH OF MAY, WHICH IS NINE WEEKS FROM THE DAY THE MARK WAS SET, AND IS NOT A DATE ON WHICH THE FOULING WILL BE A SEASON'S BUT A DATE ON WHICH ANYBODY WHO GOES AND LOOKS CAN SEE THAT IT IS NOT.**

### The relationship pressure at the end of Chapter 260

- **Calder and Nessa.** **The pair this batch changes most, and the change is that he has lost three arguments in ten days and two of them to her, and he asked for both to be entered.** He wanted the complaint and was refused by his own sentence of the eleventh of March. He offered to take the slate and was refused on the ground that a private hire is not a place to put a man in the water. **He lost the complaint to her reading of his own words and asked that it be recorded that he lost it to his own sentence and not to a better one, and she has entered that and has not improved on it. He is the man who reads the form in four minutes and says there is nothing in it he could not have said out loud on a mole, and she is the woman who counts the drawer twice and does the arithmetic nobody wanted to do.** Nothing in this batch is romantic and everything in it is expensive.
- **Calder and Alden.** **DO NOT MOVE.** A man of sixty-one at a far bench, **occupied on three of the twenty days, being the nineteenth, the twenty-first and the twenty-sixth of March, and not occupied at any hour on the other seventeen**, not asked for anything on any day, asking nothing on any day, no fragment, no report talk, no second story, and **Calder Marr did not go over to him on any of the twenty days, and he was in that harbor on fifteen of them and up that coast road on five, and neither of those is entered and neither is a reason.** **NOBODY NAMED HIM AS THE ANSWER TO WHO CUTS, AND THE NOT-NAMING IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN, AND THE REASON GIVEN IS ABOUT THE TRADE AND NOT ABOUT A FAMILY: A MAN ASKED ON A MOLE WHETHER HE CUTS ANSWERS IT WITH A PRICE, AND A PRICE ANSWERED TO A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR OF A PRESSURE HOUSE IS A THING THIS YARD WOULD THEN HAVE TO PAY, AND IT HAS NOT GOT, AND IT IS NOT GOING TO ASK A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE WHAT HE WILL TAKE. NOTHING WAS PUT ON THAT BENCH AND READ AS A GIFT.**
- **Calder and Mara.** **A LETTER, ONCE, IN THE ORDINARY POST, ON THE SECOND OF APRIL, AND NOBODY HAS ASKED HER FOR ANYTHING.** She is a person of no office and has been since the fourth of January. **What she sent is a form and not a favour: an office's form for unsettled material, a house as a place a keeper keeps it in, and the fact that she has never seen it served and cannot say what it does. And a condition, which is that she will come if a person asks her and will not come if a yard asks her, and that she has thought for three days about the difference between those two things and has not got round to it.** **NOTHING WAS ASKED OF HER, NOTHING WAS WRITTEN BACK, AND THE REASON IS IN THE SECOND COLUMN AND NOT THE FIRST, because the first column is a record of what a man did and not of what a man did not do.** Her forty marks stand first after food and were not paid and were not reduced and were not mentioned in her letter.
- **Calder and Tobias Wren.** **One scene, twenty minutes, on the mole's steps, and neither man is grateful and neither man wants to be.** He came because he heard a mark was fouled and not because he was asked, and he asked one question and it was who is paying, and he named his price before he would agree to anything, and he said he would not be a teacher before anybody asked him to be. **No boat of his was hired and no six marks was paid and the conversation cost him a morning of walking up a hill and nothing else, and the yard did not thank him and he is not owed thanks.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty-four of the second lay.** **The chapter reads the slate and gives the four things, and says them in a street because the ship's hand asked him to say them where nine people could hear, and he says them, and he asks that it be entered that he said no word about the four people of that coast.** He begins a sentence at the water side of a frame and does not finish it, and the rest of it is about the four, and nobody finishes it for him.
- **Calder and Ors Kest.** **One scene, in the reeve's office, and he is still not a friend of this party and said so in his own office before anything else happened.** He gave three things, said a true sentence a third time, priced the one thing he has left out of himself, told the yard that its mark has no second party it could seat, and said that he does not invent proceedings. **THE SEASON OF THAT OFFICE ENDED ON THE THIRTY-FIRST OF MARCH AND NO INSTRUMENT HAS BEEN ISSUED OUT OF IT SINCE, AND THE NEXT INSTRUMENT ANY OFFICE IN THAT HARBOR ISSUES, IF ONE EVER DOES, IS NOT GOING TO BE A THING THAT COULD BE USED TO GO AND LOOK AT ANYTHING.**
- **Calder and Bevin.** **Unchanged and not in a room.** Off the stone since the fifteenth of May, forty marks standing whole, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed, the boy's hand at the head of it. **THE BOY CAME DOWN TO THE MOLE ON THE SUNDAY FOURTH OF APRIL AT ABOUT ELEVEN ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT BECAUSE THERE WAS NOTHING ON THE STONE TO BE ON, AND HE WAS NOT PUT ON IT.**
- **Calder and the man of about thirty-one of the third lay.** One scene, at the head of that dock, and he asked the volume's question and was refused and asked nothing and was not asked anything, and **he sails on the chart, and the berth he did not get in the third lay on the Sunday went to a boat out of the north basin, and that is the batch's whole cost to a third party and it is entered.**

### The power state

**LINE DIVER. NO STAGE IS TAKEN IN VOLUME 06. THE FAULTREADER STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 03, WAS SPENT, AND WAS NOT RE-TAKEN, IMPROVED OR RENAMED ON ANY PAGE. THE BELLWRIGHT STAGE WAS TAKEN IN VOLUME 05 AND IS NOT IMPROVED, AND ITS SEASON OF NINE MARKS IS NOT PAID AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE ASKED FOR IT.** What changed in this batch is method and it is in other people: a price named before a yes, a condition that stands without its reason, a refusal made twice in the same words, a slate read back three times by three people, a leaf with a column for what a thing is not, and a cup of water and no more. **THE BELL IS A MARK, A FRAME, A LINE AND A SHACKLE AND IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, and no buoy, no bell and no mark went into the water on a day this yard did not pay for and nobody was in the water at any time on any of the twenty days. No finding of worked glass was made, nothing was raised, and no return of any kind was made out of any of the twenty.** The standing fact is unchanged: **a seam identifies difference and not truth, and nothing in these ten chapters settled an argument, proved a motive or told anybody what happened.** **AND THE ONE THING THIS BATCH DID TO THE HOLDER'S STANDING IS NOT A STAGE AND IS NOT A POWER: on the twenty-seventh of March he wanted to go up a coast and knock on a door, and did not, and asked for it to be written down that he did not.**

### The bodies and the dated positions

- **THE CONDITION IS NAMED NOWHERE IN THIS BATCH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE TO BE NAMED.** The body is charged: **four days lost on the coast road in Chapter 253 and one day lost on the first of April in Chapter 259, both entered in the second column with a reason against the line and no name in it and no figure, because there is no figure for a day. His forearm was bad again after nineteen days in a cart and is entered and not named.** **The four lines above the named line of the twentieth of July are still four, are still nameless, are not struck out, and are in about sixty boats on that coast.**
- **The bag is sixty-five marks and threepence, being ten thousand four hundred and three pence, and the figure the bag is short of the wage of four marks is nine thousand seven hundred and sixty-three pence. THE WHOLE OF WHAT CAME INTO THAT YARD IN THE TWENTY DAYS IS NOTHING, and that is the first twenty-day run in five volumes in which nothing came in at all, and the reason is the form of the fourth of March and not a mood.** The whole of what went out in the twenty days is five marks, two shillings and ten pence, being eight hundred and thirty-four pence, and the whole of what has gone out of that yard since the sixth of December past is eight marks, six shillings and two pence in eleven transactions at five counters.
- **The wage column stands at twenty-six lines and one hundred and four marks, the fifth of March the oldest, and there are twenty envelopes on a bench, and TWENTY-THREE weeks have now fallen due with no envelope standing against them, being the whole of that year's list.** Three wages of four marks were not paid in these twenty days, on the sixteenth, the twenty-third and the thirtieth of March. The walk is nil and it stays nil.**

- **The bench under that pump is bare for a sixty-fourth night, counting from the Sunday of the thirty-first of January, and it is the only bare thing in that shed.**
- **The two objects of nobody's are about two hundred and ninety-seven days up the crown of that mole, about nine feet apart, under two tarpaulins, one with a corner off it since the seventeenth of June and not lashed back, and neither has moved, and that party did not go near them on any of the twenty days. The man of sixty-one who owns a boat looked at them for a moment on the nineteenth of March and went up the steps.**
- **SIX PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN THAT DRAWER AND THE CHARTER'S PLACE IS EMPTY AND CLEAN AND THE WOOD IS A SLIGHTLY DIFFERENT COLOUR WHERE A THING HAD BEEN LYING ON IT FOR FOUR MONTHS. THE FOURTH LEAF IS NOT IN THAT DRAWER AND IS ON A LEAF RULED ON THE BACK OF A SHEET OF CHANDLER'S PAPER ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF MARCH, AND THERE IS NO SECOND COPY OF IT.** Nothing in a tin since the twenty-eighth of April. Three marks to a man of Ashtide, unmoved and unasked about. Seven pence to this yard's own shipwright, unpaid. Eight marks and a day of a boat to this harbor's own bellwright since the twenty-third of May, unargued, and he was not asked anything and the chest was not opened. Eight shillings and tenpence to a woman of this harbor with her name on the figure. **Two marks and eightpence paid to a man of about thirty-four of a pressure house at Ternwatch on the second of April, and his travel is not given and is not yet owed and is not to be treated as a debt until he names it.** Forty marks standing whole to a boy of twenty-two, the three nots standing, the third column unfilled and unappointed with a name beside the boy's hand at the head of it, and the boy not on the stone. Forty marks first after food to a person of no office, untouched, unoffered, and a letter from her in the ordinary post on the second of April and nothing asked of her and nothing written back.
- **A CHAIN OF CUSTODY IS A JURISDICTION AND A PRACTICE AND IT IS NOT A REGISTRY, A COURT OR A HARBOR AUTHORITY, AND IT WAS MADE ON THE SIXTH OF MARCH AND IS NOT AGED BY THIS VOLUME'S OUTLINE OR BY ANY CHAPTER OF ITS FIRST MOVEMENT. Five pages in five drawers in five towns in five hands, one page to a drawer, no two of them the same page, and this yard did not look in any of the four it cannot look in and did not write to the town that put a page on a wall. The agreement about who may read a page has no name and the reason is a counter in a room off a fish market.**

### What is owed and what is not

**Owed to the book, and this batch paid the movement's own ten of them:** the instrument that is not there; a party that cannot be hired; a boat that is not the yard's and the price of it; nineteen days up a coast road and four lines in a hand that is not his own; a question asked at a mole head and three facts that are not an answer; a season that ended with nothing issued and a reeve who said out loud that he is not a friend; a fireman of a pressure house and one condition; a fourth column; and a letter to a man who cannot read and a letter from a woman of no office, and neither answered.

**Still owed and carried into Chapter 261:** the volume's question, which is whether the fleet was scuttled or whether it went down, and the answer is under seventy fathoms of water and this party cannot get there; **a cutter, which nobody in that harbor can supply and the one man who could was not named;** the air, and the Crown house rate for it; the mark, and the fourteenth of May; the fouling, and the two thousand pounds of a foot and a half of somebody else's green; **the form for unsettled material, which is in a letter and not in any office's hand, and the question of whether a house is a drawer;** a man of thirty-four of a second lay who sails on a chart in Veyr; **the four pages in four drawers this yard cannot look in;** the plate at the fifth seam, in eleven feet, seen and not measured and not touched, THE NOTE AGAINST IT OPEN, for a third volume; the case of five bells, on nobody's schedule, with the limit four people of that coast wrote and signed; the delayed note at eleven and two and a hand's width of a second; the lead plug and the undertaking of the second of July; the three custody items and the live question no paper answers; the run under this town; the compartment, which is spent; the first echo's witness; Neave Tarrant, nine winters, not found, one line; the two objects of nobody's; the answer inside the delayed note, reserved to the Volume 15 midpoint; the coast road and the two figures and the Kettle; **THE CONCEALMENT, WHICH WAS TOLD ONCE IN CHAPTER 38 OF VOLUME 01 AND IS OWED TO THIS VOLUME AND IS NOT TOLD IN ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS;** and the new-volume question, which is who first used a seal to turn emergency custody into permanent ownership, and is not asked yet.

**NOT OWED AND NOT TO BE RESTARTED BY A LATER CHAPTER:** the complaint against the four people of that coast, which was refused on the eleventh of March and refused again on the twenty-seventh and is not to be raised in this volume; the going out of the second of May, which is spent; the plate note, which is not paid by a better letter; the third column, the boy's hand, and the name beside it; the forty marks twice; the three figures that must not be swapped; the compact's name, which is on one page of Volume 05 and is not to be said again; **THE QUIETENING, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 281, AND THE CROWN SEAL, WHICH MAY NOT BE NAMED BEFORE CHAPTER 291, AND NEITHER OF WHICH IS NAMED IN ANY OF THESE TEN CHAPTERS.**

**AND THE THING THAT IS NOT OWED AND IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH'S LAST POSITION: A WORKING HARBOR OF THAT COAST IS POORER ON THE FOURTH DAY OF APRIL THAN IT WAS ON THE TWENTY-THIRD OF FEBRUARY, A HARBOR AUTHORITY'S SEASON ENDED WITH NOTHING ISSUED, A TIDE GANG IS FOUR MEN SHORT AND THE THIRD LAY IS A BERTH SHORT, AND A YARD THAT HAS BEEN TWENTY DAYS WITHOUT A PAPER OF ANY KIND HAS SENT ONE LETTER AND RECEIVED ONE, AND NEITHER HAS BEEN ANSWERED, AND NOBODY NAMED THE ONLY MAN WHO COULD HAVE ANSWERED THE OTHER HALF OF IT.**

## Volume 06, Batch 0001 summary (Chapters 251–260) — the story state at the end of Chapter 260

**Movement 1 is written. The leash is gone and the yard cannot be hired, and the question is under seventy fathoms of water, and this batch found out that the only people on this coast who could answer it are four people this yard is not going to ask.** In twenty days a shipwright found out that a party with no paper has nothing to sell; a retired salvage foreman named the price of a boat and said he would not be a teacher; a man came home from a coast road with four lines in somebody else's hand and a sentence that is a refusal; a mark was looked at three times and was found to have been handled, lifted, mended, fouled faster than the water can do it, and tied with a knot this yard does not use; a man with nineteen years in the water said out loud in a street that fouling does not know a name; the holder wanted to knock on a door and did not, and lost the argument to his own sentence; a leaf with four columns was ruled and the fourth of them says what a thing is not; the volume's question was asked at a mole head and answered with three facts that are not an answer; a harbor authority's season ended with nothing issued and a reeve said out loud that he is not a friend; a fireman of a pressure house came up a hill with a folded sheet of thirty-eight lines and offered air and set one condition; and a letter went to the ordinary post for a man who cannot read, and a letter came up the hill from a person of no office, and neither was answered.

**THE BATCH'S MIDPOINT TURN IS CHAPTER 256 AND ITS TURN IS PAID IN THE PAGE: a fourth column, headed *what it is not*, in a book in one town, that nobody can check.** The chapters before it are a party learning what it has lost and a mark learning who else has been on it. Chapter 256 is where the volume's method arrives, and everything after it is that method being paid for. **The batch's climax is Chapter 260**, where a yard which spent five volumes refusing to be an address becomes one address more, for a man who cannot read, at a penny, unsigned.

**THE BATCH'S COST, AND IT IS THE HOUSE'S OWN KIND: NOTHING CAME IN.** Twenty days, no income, eight hundred and thirty-four pence out, a wage column that did not move on three Tuesdays, twenty-three weeks fallen due, a day lost to the body on the first of April, four days lost to the body on a coast road, and **a Sunday berth in the third lay that went to a boat out of the north basin because a man was at the head of that dock being answered by this yard.**

**CONFLICTS FOUND AND HOW THEY WERE RESOLVED, RECORDED RATHER THAN DEFENDED:**

## Required updates after each batch

A writer phase that completes a batch updates these same files and does not set phase status:

- `state/chapter-summaries.md`: one entry per chapter, two to five sentences each, plus the compact volume index.
- `state/continuity.md`: new canon facts, changed relationships, power costs and gains, discovered world rules, and any proposed canon change.
- `state/open-threads.md`: promises opened, promises closed, and threads carried forward.
- `state/current.md`: the story state at the end of the batch, so the next batch starts from the right place, plus the batch summary.

### The movement's beats, in order, as they stand on the page

1. **241 — what the holder of the writ is on the first of March.
